jobs.description:
Posting Details

I. DEPARTMENT INFORMATION

Job Description Summary:

The Antibiotic Resistance Action Center ( ARAC ) at the George Washington University Milken Institute School of Public Health is seeking a collaborative, highly motivated, and scientifically rigorous Research Associate to join the Molecular Epidemiology and Microbiome research group. Led by Drs. Cindy Liu and Lance Price, our group investigates the impact of environmental and occupational exposures on human health within a dedicated One Health framework. Our research program is specifically focused on characterizing nasal, urogenital, and gut microbiome commensals, with the goal of leveraging commensal microbial communities to develop evidence-based strategies that prevent and treat diverse infectious and inflammatory conditions.

To achieve this, our group operates through a robust process by integrating hypothesis generation from observational, cohort-based studies with downstream mechanistic studies in advanced in vitro models, and further translating those findings into public health applications, including live biotherapeutic and point-of-care diagnostic development.

To support this dynamic process, we are seeking a Research Associate to conduct cutting-edge research who can thrive within a fast-paced, advanced multidisciplinary setting. This position offers a unique opportunity to own a diverse and exciting portfolio of research projects within a highly collaborative team, while actively engaging with, mentoring, and guiding passionate undergraduate and graduate students.

Additional Responsibilities Include: Research, Data Management, and Analysis

Methodology Development, Optimization, & Validation: Lead the development, optimization, and validation of research protocols for assigned research projects, including targeted literature searches, performing rigorous troubleshooting of failing assays, and contributing directly to follow-up experimental design.
R&D Translation to Scale-Up Implementation: Manage the lifecycle of assigned research projects, successfully progressing workflows from the initial method development and benchtop R&D stages through to large-scale, high-throughput validation and implementation studies.
Data Analysis: Independently process, analyze, and interpret experimental datasets, including the use of appropriate analytic (statistical/epidemiological) methods required to evaluate experimental outcomes, determine statistical significance, and prepare publication-quality tables and figures.
Sample, Data, and Workflow Management: Oversee sample tracking, processing workflows, and comprehensive lab and data analysis management for large-scale studies containing clinical and environmental sample and metadata collections designed for multi-omic, culture-based, and in vitro studies.

Manuscript & Grant Preparation

Contribute directly to writing, critically reviewing, and formatting drafts for manuscripts and grant applications, in collaboration with the PIs and other research team members. Present findings professionally at academic or scientific conferences

Laboratory Operations:

Day-to-Day Laboratory Functions: Assist with day-to-day laboratory functions, including inventory control, bio- and chemical safety compliance, and equipment maintenance, and provide technical mentorship to undergraduate and graduate ( MPH ) research trainees in collaboration with the PIs and other research team members.
Regulatory Coordination: Coordinate laboratory compliance functions, including biosafety protocols, CDC permit applications, sample transfer documentation, and sample shipping in collaboration with the PIs and other research team members.

The omission of specific duties does not preclude the supervisor from assigning duties that are logically related to the position.

Minimum Qualifications:

Qualified candidates will hold a master’s degree and 1 year of experience in a related discipline. Degree must be conferred by the start date of the position.

Additional Required Licenses/Certifications/Posting Specific Minimum Qualifications:

Preferred Qualifications:

Core Competency & Adaptability: A proven track record as an independent contributor in at least two of the Core Methodology Areas listed below is preferred, paired with the necessary background knowledge, drive, and technical agility to expand into the remaining fields, is desired.
Molecular, Multi-Omics, & High-Throughput Workflows: Direct experience in the development, independent optimization, and validation of custom molecular assays (such as PCR /qPCR), sample preparation for multi-omics (metagenomics/transcriptomics, bulk or single-cell), and high-throughput workflows utilizing liquid-handling robotics is a plus. This area forms the descriptive foundation of our cohort and intervention studies.
Commensal Bacteriology & Live Biotherapeutic Formulation: Mastery of developing, optimizing, and validating bacterial culturing protocols for both aerobic and anaerobic organisms, including the isolation, selection, and physiological phenotyping of diverse commensal species using clinical specimens, is preferred. Direct experience working with lyoprotectant optimization and formulation testing for live biotherapeutics is a plus and considered a significant asset to support both observational and translational research studies.
Primary Epithelial Cell Culture & Host-Microbe/Microbe-Microbe Interactions: Hands-on expertise in using primary epithelial cell models to study host-microbe and microbe-microbe interactions, including downstream phenotypic and physiological characterization, including immunohistochemistry ( IHC ), confocal and fluorescence microscopy, and barrier function assays to assess commensal function is desired.
Immunoassays & Point-of-Care Testing ( POCT ): Direct experience in the configuration, development, optimization, and validation of immunoassays (such as ELISA ) and the evaluation or implementation of point-of-care diagnostic testing modalities to translate laboratory discoveries into scalable, translational public health solutions is preferred.
Peer-Reviewed Publication Record: A documented history of scientific contribution, evidenced by a record of peer-reviewed publications (as a first author or co-author), is a plus.
Conference Presentations: Experience preparing and delivering presentations at professional academic or scientific conferences is preferred.
Education & Experience: A master’s degree in Biology, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Microbiology, or a related scientific field, with dedicated research experience, is desired.
Advanced Epidemiological & Statistical Analysis: Proficiency or advanced training in applying complex epidemiological methods, linear/non-linear modeling, or multivariate survival analyses to complex patient cohorts and experimental data is a plus.
Bioinformatics Skills: Direct experience performing computational data analysis using custom bioinformatics pipelines for microbiome sequencing, genomic characterization, or multi-omic datasets using statistical software (e.g., R, Python) is preferred.
Translational & Regulatory Knowledge: Experience or a structural understanding of translational pipelines, including CMC compliance, Investigational New Drug ( IND ) related documentation, or participation in supporting clinical trial studies is desired.
Project Portfolio Management: Demonstrated capability to operate effectively as an individual contributor who can multitask, manage time efficiently across distinct studies, and make technical decisions under limited supervision is a plus.

As a Data Science Leader, B2B Marketing & Demand Generation, you will partner with our B2B Marketing organization and help accelerate how businesses discover, adopt, and grow with AI.

We believe electricity powers modern life. As part of our Power sector, you’ll help shape how electricity is generated, transmitted and delivered as global energy demands grow. From massive data centers to modernizing transmission systems, our industry-recognized engineers and scientists have been at the forefront of grid transformation for more than a century. You’ll work side-by-side with these experts and contribute to reliable, resilient and sustainable power systems, helping communities thrive and industries expand. This isn’t just a job, it’s a chance to drive infrastructure forward, power innovation and leave your mark on our energy future.

jobs.description:
- Contract - San Diego, CA

Drive cutting‑edge multi‑omics discovery by leading high‑complexity genomic workflows from tissue to data.

Proclinical is seeking a Genomics Research Associate for a contract role in San Diego, CA.

Primary Responsibilities

The Research Associate will support the general genomics workflows, integration of novel genomics pipelines into larger operational networks and working groups, and standardization of genomics pipelines to drive efficiency and impact of R&D efforts. The ideal candidate will have a strong track record of supporting centralized genomics services.

Skills & Requirements

Bachelor's or master's degree in molecular biology, Biochemistry, Genetics, Biotechnology, or a related field with 3-5 years of professional laboratory experience
Strong hands-on experience with Molecular Biology (i.e. Nucleic acid extraction and QC, RT-PCR, and Cloning)
Strong hands-on experience in NGS library preparation and QC.
Experience with reagent validation, protocol optimization, and troubleshooting
Knowledge and hands-on experience with operating sequencing platforms including MiSeq, NextSeq, and Nanopore Sequencing.
Hands-on experience with single-cell genomics assays.
Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and record-keeping, particularly in electronic lab notebooks (ELNs).
Experience and/or familiarity with the application of spatial genomics technologies, histology workflows, and/or automation platforms is a plus
Experience working with human or animal tissue samples is a plus.

The Genomics Research Associate's Responsibilities Will Be

Provide daily operational support for genomics instrumentation and service pipelines.
Process incoming Genomics Requests from sample receipt through QC, library preparation, sequencing and data handoff, following established Hub protocols.
Perform nucleic acid extraction and QC, RT-PCR, and NGS library preparation and QC.
Operate sequencing platforms (NextSeq, Nanopore) and run single-cell genomics assays.
Support reagent validation, protocol optimization and troubleshooting to keep workflows efficient and reproducible.
Keep accurate, detailed records, including electronic lab notebook (ELN) entries, and track request status.
Communicate workflow status clearly to genomics team members, SDI researchers and Scientific Operations to meet project milestones.
Assist with documenting and standardizing workflows

jobs.title: Bioinformatics Programmer
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Bioinformatics Programmer will develop, validate, and maintain predictive machine learning workflows for cancer research. The successful candidate will architect advanced, high-throughput computational frameworks focusing on structural informatics, foundational deep learning architectures, advanced latent variable extraction, and integrative analyses across highly complex multi-omic, molecular, and clinical datasets, with emphasis on reproducible research, translational impact, and high-quality software development. This role is intended for an experienced technical specialist who can contribute at a senior level through demonstrated productivity, independent execution, and strong analytical judgment.

Apply By Date
: 11/29/2026 by 11:59pm

Minimum Qualifications - For full consideration, applicants are encouraged to upload license and/or certification if required of the position

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computational biology, bioinformatics, biology, engineering, statistics, mathematics, biology, or a related field.
At least 5 years of directly relevant experience in cancer research, including software engineering, scientific computing, bioinformatics, or computational modeling.
Thorough knowledge of bioinformatics methods, applications programming, web development and data structures.
Thorough knowledge of bioinformatics programming design, modification and implementation.
Understanding of relational databases, web interfaces, and operating systems.
Strong project management skills.
Thorough knowledge of modern biology and applicable field of research.
Communication skills to work with both technical and non-technical personnel in multiple fields of expertise and at various levels in the organization.
Ability to communicate technical information in a clear and concise manner.
Ability to interface with management on a regular basis.
Self motivated, work independently or as part of a team, able to learn quickly, meet deadlines and demonstrate problem solving skills.
Thorough knowledge of web, application and data security concepts and methods.
Demonstrated productivity through peer-reviewed publications, preprints, open-source software, internal tools, technical reports, or comparable documented work.
Strong proficiency in Python and/or R.
Demonstrated, long-term functional expertise in predictive modeling, advanced statistical modeling, the extraction of complex latent biological features, and high-dimensional data analysis.
Proven capacity to engineer distributed computational pipelines and deploy highly optimized multi-omic algorithms for large-scale data ingestion and analysis.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver reliable results.

Preferred Qualifications

Deep functional experience leveraging advanced artificial intelligence modalities, expansive language architectures, and advanced latent-variable extraction techniques to cancer or biomedical data.
Demonstrated capability in computational structural biology, specifically encompassing the advanced simulation of macromolecular interactions, dynamic conformational analysis, and complex drug-target elucidations
Familiarity with survival analysis, classification, clustering, and model interpretation
Experience with multi-omic datasets and cutting-edge translational research workflows, including the computational analysis of complex disease models and deeply stratified patient cohorts.
Familiarity with workflow managers, containerization, and high-performance computing.
Evidence of technical leadership or mentorship in collaborative research settings.

Key Responsibilities

40% - AI, Machine Learning & Computational Modeling
40% - Multi-Omics Analytics, Data Engineering & Reproducible Workflows
15% - Translational Research & Scientific Collaboration
5% - Technical Leadership, Mentorship & Methodological Innovation

Department Overview

The Department of Urologic Surgery is a multidisciplinary clinical and research department dedicated to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disorders of the urinary tract and male reproductive system. The department integrates patient care, surgical innovation, research, and education, serving as a regional and national leader in the management of both common and complex urologic conditions. As part of an academic health system, the department plays a central role in training the next generation of urologists and maintains active involvement in medical student education. The department is also deeply committed to basic, translational, and clinical research, with investigators leading studies on cancer biology, novel therapeutics, surgical outcomes, health disparities, and quality improvement. Through its combined missions of patient care, education, and research, the Department of Urologic Surgery strives to advance the field, improve patient quality of life, and train future leaders in urologic health.

jobs.title: RESEARCH ASSISTANT III- Zwick Lab
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:
Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We celebrated our 100-year legacy in 2024. This significant milestone marks a century of seminal discoveries in immunology, infectious diseases (such as COVID-19, flu, HIV), neuroscience, heart disease, cancer, and more. Located in La Jolla, California, the institute houses six research departments, multiple Nobel laureates, a top-ranked graduate school and a leading postdoctoral training program. Scripps Research encompasses two elite and highly innovative institutes, the Calibr-Skaggs Institute for Innovative Medicines and Scripps Research Translational Institute, which merge foundational studies in biology, chemistry and computer science with translational science to produce pioneering drugs and advances in digital and precision medicine. Together, we cultivate new scientific leaders and expand the frontiers of knowledge to deliver medical breakthroughs impacting human health around the globe. If you have a passion for making a difference, this could be your opportunity to join our transformative team.

POSITION TITLE:
Research Assistant III

Position Summary

The Zwick Laboratory in the Department of Immunology & Microbiology at Scripps Research is seeking a motivated and highly organized Research Assistant (RA II or RA III, depending on experience)
to join our team studying antibody responses and developing next-generation vaccines and biologic therapies.

Our research focuses on HIV vaccine design, broadly neutralizing antibodies, HIV envelope (Env), and germline-targeting immunogens
, with opportunities to extend these approaches to other viral pathogens and antibody-based therapies. Current studies combine molecular and cellular immunology, virology, antibody biology, flow cytometry, next-generation sequencing, and structure-guided vaccine design, including vaccine studies in mouse and nonhuman-primate models.

We are especially interested in someone who enjoys hands-on experimental work, wants to understand the scientific questions behind the experiments, and can grow into increasing responsibility within the laboratory.

In this position you will plan and conduct complex or novel research projects that involve the performance of non-routine procedures, development of new or improved techniques and evaluation criteria, thorough data analysis and complex interpretations of results; assist in designing experiments; operate sophisticated scientific lab equipment; may plan and conduct a small or average size project or a large portion of a more diverse project; may supervise or provide work direction and training to a small staff of professional-level employees; perform other related duties, tasks and responsibilities as required or assigned.

Responsibilities And Duties

The successful candidate will contribute directly to ongoing research and, depending on experience, may:

Maintain, transfect, and characterize mammalian cell lines, including stable cell lines
Perform flow cytometry and fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), including data analysis and standardized presentation of results
Carry out PCR and prepare samples for next-generation sequencing
Perform ELISA and other antibody-binding and functional assays
Support HIV virology and antibody neutralization studies
Organize, analyze, interpret, and clearly present experimental data
Coordinate experiments with laboratory personnel, Scripps core facilities, collaborators, and external service providers
Maintain accurate experimental records, sample inventories, and laboratory workflows
Troubleshoot experiments and communicate progress, problems, and next steps promptly
As experience grows, assist with training junior personnel and day-to-day laboratory organization

Prior experience in either immunology/cell biology or molecular biology/virology
would be valuable. Candidates do not need experience in every technique; we are looking for someone who is technically capable, eager to learn, and interested in developing breadth across these areas.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree or higher in biology, immunology, microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry, biotechnology, or a related field.
Requires a minimum of 5 years’ experience.
Candidates possessing a master’s degree, 3+ years’ experience required.
Strong experimental organization and attention to detail
Reliability, productivity, follow-through, and effective communication
Ability to troubleshoot and manage several ongoing experimental priorities
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with others
Interest in increasingly interpreting data and understanding how individual experiments contribute to the larger scientific question

We are especially interested in candidates looking for a stable position with opportunities to grow in responsibility over time
. For the right person, the position offers the opportunity to take on increasing responsibility for experimental coordination, laboratory organization, mentoring, and day-to-day research operations.

Physical Requirements

This position works in a laboratory or vivarium environment. Further details of the physical requirements of established essential functions for this position will be addressed/discussed during the interview process.

COMPENSATION:
The expected hiring range for this position is $72,384 - $84,375 per year, commensurate with experience. Consideration will be given to experience that exceeds the listed requirements.

Comprehensive Benefits Include

Employer Contributed Retirement Plan – Depending on eligibility, employees receive an employer contributed retirement plan (no employee contribution required) and the option to contribute to a 403(b) (which is similar to a 401(k) using your own pre or post-tax dollars)
Full Suite of Health and Welfare plans including three medical plan options (including an HSA available option), dental, vision, life insurance, disability, EAP and more Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (Medical/Dependent Care)
Competitive vacation and sick leave policies
Free, on-site parking

jobs.description:
Job Description

Bioinformatics, Field Applications Scientist

Clinical Genomics & Human Genetics | Central/Mountain/Pacific Time Zones

About Us

Oxford Nanopore Technologies is transforming how scientists analyze DNA and RNA through real-time, scalable sequencing technology. Our platforms enable researchers to analyze native DNA and RNA, from short to ultra-long fragments, supporting advances in human genetics, clinical research, biopharma, and beyond. Our goal is to enable the analysis of anything, by anyone, anywhere.

About The Role

We are seeking a Bioinformatics, Field Applications Scientist with a strong background in human genomics, clinical bioinformatics, or biopharma applications, combined with experience in long-read sequencing technologies.

In this role, you will partner with our Sales team and customers to provide scientific and technical expertise across Oxford Nanopore sequencing platforms and bioinformatics software. You will help researchers design experiments, troubleshoot sequencing and analysis workflows, interpret complex genomic data, and successfully adopt our technology.

We are particularly interested in scientists with hands-on experience analyzing human genetic or clinical sequencing data, including applications in oncology, rare diseases, inherited disorders, precision medicine, or therapeutic development.

This opportunity is well suited to a technically strong bioinformatics scientist who enjoys solving problems, collaborating with researchers, and translating complex scientific concepts into practical solutions. Prior commercial experience is valued, but we also welcome candidates from clinical laboratories, biotechnology, pharmaceutical research, and translational research environments who demonstrate strong communication skills and an interest in customer-facing scientific work.

Location:
Field-based, United States. Candidates should reside in the Central, Mountain, or Pacific time zones, particularly Colorado, Texas, and the western U.S.

Travel:
Approximately 30–40%, including customer visits and occasional overnight travel.

What You'll Do

Provide bioinformatics expertise and technical support to customers working in human genetics, clinical genomics, oncology, and biopharma research.
Support the design, implementation, troubleshooting, and optimization of next-generation and long-read sequencing analysis workflows.
Guide customers through genomic data analysis, including variant calling, structural variant detection, genome assembly, transcriptomics, and other relevant applications.
Collaborate with Sales to deliver technical consultations, product demonstrations, scientific presentations, and customer training.
Help customers transition from short-read sequencing technologies to long-read sequencing applications, where appropriate.
Troubleshoot bioinformatics pipelines, sequencing data quality, computational environments, and software-related challenges.
Translate complex scientific and computational concepts into clear, actionable recommendations for researchers and laboratory teams.
Build and maintain strong technical relationships with customers to support successful adoption of Oxford Nanopore technologies.
Partner with internal commercial, technical support, and product development teams to address customer needs and share market insights.
Document customer interactions and technical activities in the CRM.

What You'll Bring

Education: Advanced degree in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genetics, Genomics, Molecular Biology, or a related life sciences discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
Human Genomics Experience: Demonstrated hands-on experience analyzing human genomic or transcriptomic datasets, including applications in human genetics, molecular diagnostics, oncology, inherited disease, or related human biological research.
Clinical or Biopharma Bioinformatics: Practical bioinformatics experience supporting at least one of the following:
Clinical genomics, molecular pathology, or genomic diagnostic workflows.
Pharmaceutical or biotechnology research, including drug discovery, biomarker identification, or therapeutic development.
Translational research involving human disease, patient-derived samples, or clinically relevant genomic datasets.

Long-Read Sequencing: Hands-on experience with long-read sequencing technologies and associated bioinformatics analysis workflows.
NGS Data Analysis: Experience developing, implementing, or troubleshooting sequencing analysis pipelines involving one or more of the following: genomic variant calling, structural variant analysis, genome assembly, transcriptomics, or genomic annotation.
Programming and Computing: Proficiency in Python or R, experience working in UNIX/Linux environments, and familiarity with high-performance computing or cloud-based analysis environments.
Scientific Communication: Ability to explain complex bioinformatics concepts clearly to scientists and stakeholders with varying levels of computational expertise.
Problem Solving: Demonstrated ability to independently investigate technical challenges, interpret data, and collaborate with scientific teams to identify solutions.
Travel: Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30–40% to support customer engagements, training, and scientific events.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience in a Field Applications Scientist, Bioinformatics Support Scientist, Technical Applications Scientist, or other customer-facing scientific role.
Direct experience with Oxford Nanopore platforms, software, and analysis tools such as MinKNOW, Dorado, or EPI2ME.
Experience supporting clinical sequencing technologies, bioinformatics software, or genomic analysis platforms.
Familiarity with human structural variants, somatic and germline variant analysis, cancer genomics, or rare disease applications.
Experience with workflow management and reproducible analysis tools such as Nextflow, Snakemake, Docker, or similar platforms.
Experience delivering scientific presentations, technical workshops, or training to external users.
Familiarity with AWS or other cloud computing environments.

Travel & Work Style

This is a field-based position requiring regular customer engagement and travel, generally 30–40%, including occasional overnight trips. Candidates should be comfortable working independently, collaborating across teams, and supporting customers with varying scientific and computational needs.

Compensation & Benefits

The salary range for this position is $97,479 to $121,849, depending on skills and experience. Certain roles within Oxford Nanopore Technologies are eligible for annual bonuses and stock awards based on individual performance. U.S. employees have access to healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan with company match, short- and long-term disability coverage, basic life insurance, commuter benefits, and other offerings.

Oxford Nanopore Technologies is committed to equal employment opportunity. Please note that no terminology in this advert is intended to discriminate on the grounds of a person's gender, marital status, race, religion, colour, age, disability or sexual orientation. Every candidate will be assessed only in accordance with their merits, qualifications and abilities to perform the duties of the job.

About Us

Oxford Nanopore Technologies: Our goal is to bring the widest benefits to society through enabling the analysis of anything, by anyone, anywhere. The company has developed a new generation of nanopore-based sensing technology for faster, information rich, accessible and affordable molecular analysis. The first application is DNA/RNA sequencing, and the technology is in development for the analysis of other types of molecules including proteins. The technology is used to understand and characterise the biology of humans and diseases such as cancer, plants, animals, bacteria, viruses, and whole environments. With a thriving culture of ambition and strong innovation goals, Oxford Nanopore is a UK headquartered company with global operations and customers in more than 125 countries.

jobs.description:
Job Description

This position is represented by SEIU Local 2007 and the collective bargaining agreement between the university and SEIU Local 2007 governs the terms and conditions of employment.

This position has been deemed critical by the School of Humanities and Sciences Dean’s Office and is exempt from the hiring freeze.

Work Arrangement:
This is an on-site only position based on the Stanford campus

Budgeted Salary:
The budgeted base salary for this position is $34.58 per hour.

The School of Humanities and Sciences (H&S)
is the foundation of a liberal arts education at Stanford. The school encompasses 24 departments and 25 interdisciplinary programs. H&S is home to fundamental and applied research, where free, open, and critical inquiry is pursued across disciplines. As the university’s largest school, H&S serves as the foundation of a Stanford undergraduate education no matter which discipline students pursue as a major. Graduate students work alongside world-renowned faculty to pursue and shape foundational research that leads to breakthroughs and discoveries that shed new light on the past, influence the present, and shape the future. Together, faculty and students in H&S engage in inspirational teaching, learning, and research every day.

Department/Program Description

The Department of Biology at Stanford University is devoted to discovering fundamental knowledge of the living world: from the behavior of single molecules to dynamics of cells, organisms, populations, and interactions of biological systems with our planet. We are dedicated to developing innovative training experiences for the next generation of biologists and to building an inclusive learning environment that unites members from diverse disciplines and life experiences. The Department is the largest in the School of Humanities and Sciences with over 100 active and emeritus faculty, lecturers and research staff, over 240 PhD and postdoc trainees and over 60 non-academic staff who advance the department’s research and teaching missions. The department serves over 220 undergraduate students who major in Biology and more than 3,600 enrollees in our courses each year. Learn more about the department at biology.stanford.edu.

Position Summary

We are seeking a Life Science Technician I (LST I) to join the Lowe Lab and help launch a new transgenic echinoderm facility. Based at Hopkins Marine Station, this LST I will rear transgenic sea urchins and sea stars from larvae through metamorphosis and maintain juveniles and adults in Tecniplast aquatic housing racks. Day-to-day work is primarily animal husbandry: rearing and feeding larvae, maintaining the phytoplankton cultures used as larval food, caring for adult sea urchin and sea star broodstock, and keeping the rack systems clean and running. Because the rearing and housing methods were developed by

collaborating labs and are new to Hopkins, the technician will play a key role in adapting and troubleshooting them. The role also includes microinjecting eggs with transgenic constructs, keeping meticulous records of animals, cultures, and transgenic lines, and providing occasional administrative support to the lab. The technician will work under the direction of the PI and senior lab members. This is a 100% FTE, bargaining unit, onsite, one-year fixed-term position with possibility of renewal.

Preferred Requirements

Additional highly preferred qualifications for this position include:

Bachelor’s degree in biology, marine biology, or a related field.
Experience with aquatic animal husbandry, such as rearing marine invertebrate larvae or maintaining seawater or recirculating aquarium systems.
Experience culturing microalgae or other live feeds.
Experience with microinjection or other fine manipulation under a microscope.
Exceptional organization and record-keeping, with close attention to detail.
Strong problem-solving skills and comfort adapting and troubleshooting new protocols.
Willingness to work a flexible schedule, including occasional weekend and holiday animal care.

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Very simple animal dissection such as removing a readily accessible organ, preparation before and assistance during surgery, administration of medication and post-surgery care.
Histological procedures involving fixation of tissue and staining specimens with stains that do not require microscopic control in proceeding from step to step.
Maintenance and transfer of established cell lines where the culture conditions are well defined.
Biochemical assays (often colorimetric or spectrophotometric) of compounds or enzymatic activity using well-established procedures where the determination of any settings or adjustments is provided to the technician.
Molecular biology assays (polymerase chain reaction, sequencing reactions) where the protocol is well established.
Operation of instruments (e.g., spectrophotometer, fraction collector, scintillation counter, PCR machines, light microscope, cell counter) where the settings are simple or prescribed; techniques such as centrifugation (not involving density gradients) or limited black and white photography.
Isolation, purification and maintenance of bacteria and basic manipulation of bacterial plasmids using well-established protocols; determination of the concentration of cells.
Complete and accurate documentation of the work performed.

Minimum Education And Experience

One year’s employment experience in laboratory work or a combination of equivalent education and relevant work experience/training (e.g., one year of college science).

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Work requires the ability to follow detailed instructions and keep accurate records.

jobs.title: Research Associate
jobs.description:
Department Overview

The OHSU Dermatology Research Division merges basic, clinical and translational research in epithelial cell cancers and dermatologic diseases. Our basic and clinician-scientists are committed to innovative research on cancer and inflammation of skin with an impact on understanding causes and improving future treatment of muco-cutaneous diseases and providing more effective patient care.

The person who fills this position will report to Noah Hornick, MD, PhD, Assistant Professor, in investigating methods for surveillance of melanoma recurrence / metastasis, as well as mechanisms of inflammation in the skin during adverse reactions to cancer immunotherapy. Responsibilities will include conducting experimentation that leverages techniques including the processing of human tissue samples (skin, tumor, and blood) in order to extract single cells, nuclei, DNA, RNA, and protein; histologic work including the chromogenic and fluorescent labeling and imaging of slides, preparation of spatial, single-cell, and bulk RNA libraries for sequencing, cell culture, and flow cytometry. The Research Associate will also be responsible for contributing to documentation and data analysis related to this experimentation, as well as to the preparation of figures for publication.

Function/Duties of Position

Supports basic day-to-day functions of the lab, including assisting with ordering supplies. Oversees and assists with training of new or temporary students and other personnel. Attends all laboratory research and division/department meetings.
Independently sets up and carries out cell culture experiments with cell lines and primary human skin cells. Analyzes results using techniques listed in position summary. Independently prepares, labels, and images slides using stains, immunolabeling, and in situ hybridization with both chromogens and fluorophores. Processes human blood and tissue to produce single-cell suspensions, single-nucleus suspensions, peripheral blood mononuclear cells, serum, and plasma. Prepares cDNA libraries for sequencing from fixed and frozen tissue through 10X Genomics protocols: Visium, Chromium, Chromium Flex, and Epi Multiome. Prepares and labels single-cell suspensions from patient samples and cultured cells, performs flow cytometry analysis.

Required Qualifications

Master’s Degree in relevant field AND 3 years of relevant experience OR
Bachelor’s Degree in relevant field AND 5 years of relevant experience.
At least 1 year of required experience in biomedical research lab
Fluency with relevant mathematics / basic statistics, experience with MS Excel
Ability to perform the job duties with or without accommodation.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in relevant field and 5 years of relevant experience.
Prior imaging or histology experience, single-cell transcriptome analysis experience, R programming, and python programming experience are helpful
Knowledge of immunology, dermatology, or sex hormone biology

Additional Details

The schedule will be full-time (40 hours per week), though the hours can be flexible on mutual agreement and may include evening and weekend work as needed depending on experimental timing demands. The location will be primarily in the dermatology laboratory and associated equipment rooms in CHH1. Specialized experiments will be conducted in core facilities. Exposure as part of this position may include human tissues and fluids.

Why apply to OHSU?

We are Oregon's only public academic health center.

In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington.

All are welcome.

OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply.

To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu

Farallon Institute Seeks an Experienced Research Assistant in Marine Science

The successful candidate will assist with a variety of projects within Farallon Institute in coordination with a team of interdisciplinary marine scientists working on projects in biological oceanography (zooplankton patchiness and top predator biodiversity), ecosystem and environmental fisheries management, and global seabird ecology. Industrial automation and networking

Bachelor’s degree
Bilingual in Spanish
Experience with:

Linux operating systems

Ability to work independently in field environments

jobs.title: Data Analyst
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Since opening our first self-storage facility in 1972, Public Storage has grown to become the world’s largest owner and operator of self-storage facilities. With thousands of locations across the United States and Europe and more than 170 million net rentable square feet, we are also among the largest landlords globally.

Recognized as a Great Place to Work by the Great Place to Work Institute, Public Storage is a member of the S&P 500 and FT Global 500. Our common and preferred stock is traded on the New York Stock Exchange.

As the nation’s leading self-storage provider, we are known for our iconic orange doors and our commitment to delivering simple, reliable storage solutions to millions of customers.

 **Job Description**

Public Storage runs at a scale that makes the work interesting. More than 4,500 locations and growing, a national customer base, prices that move every day, and a footprint expanding across the U.S. and into Canada. Our Data and Analytics team sits with the business partners who own those decisions and works with them on the critical problems: pricing, promotions, marketing, operations, real estate acquisitions, and forecasting supply and demand.

Our platform runs on Google Cloud, including BigQuery, Vertex AI, Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Cloud Run, GKE, and Terraform, along with dbt Cloud, Airflow/Cloud Composer, Looker, and modern CI/CD. We're a small, senior team that operates like a startup inside an S&P 500 company. Short paths from idea to production, real ownership, and work that shows up in the business instead of in a slide deck.

Analysts here aren't a report factory. In this role you'll support our customer teams, working with customer data to answer the questions that change what we do the following week. You'll write real SQL against a modern warehouse, build dashboards people actually use, and learn the difference between a number that's interesting and a number that's decision-grade. You'll work closely with a senior data scientist who reviews your work and helps you grow, and you'll learn to work alongside AI analysis tools, which means your value is in framing the question and validating the answer.  
  
What You'll Do

**Analysis**

* Write clean, efficient SQL against BigQuery to answer business questions from our customer teams and other business partners
* Build and maintain dashboards and self-serve reporting in Looker, and support customer team partners in using them
* Investigate anomalies and trends in customer and business data: find the driver, not just the delta
* Support experiment readouts and performance measurement for customer initiatives, such as campaigns and promotions, with correct methodology

**Data Craft**

* Contribute dbt models and tests for the metrics you own, with documentation others can read
* Validate data before you publish it, with reconciliation, sanity checks, and known caveats stated up front
* Handle customer data responsibly, following our privacy and access standards
* Use AI assistants to accelerate query drafting and exploration, and critically review everything they produce

**Communication**

* Turn analysis into a short, clear recommendation with the assumptions visible
* Present to business partners in their language, not in yours
* Document metric definitions so the same question gets the same answer next quarter

  
**Qualifications**  

* Bachelor's degree in a quantitative or business field, such as statistics, economics, finance, business analytics, mathematics, engineering or computer science, with a minimum of 3 years of analytics, reporting or business intelligence experience; or Master's degree in one of these fields with 1 year of analytics, reporting or business intelligence experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential functions of the job
* Solid SQL skills, including joins, window functions, and aggregation logic
* Experience building dashboards in Looker, Tableau, Power BI, or similar
* Strong Excel or Google Sheets modeling skills
* Clear written and verbal communication; comfort presenting to business stakeholders

Preferred

* 3+ years of analytics experience, including customer, marketing, digital, retail, or consumer analytics
* Experience with a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, or Databricks
* Exposure to dbt, Git, or version-controlled analytics workflows
* Working knowledge of Python or R for analysis
* Exposure to A/B testing, statistical significance, and experiment interpretation
* Experience with web and digital analytics such as Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics, or clickstream data
* Interest in using LLMs and AI tools to accelerate analytical work

Skills & Technologies

* Core: SQL, Looker, Excel/Sheets, data storytelling
* Cloud & data: BigQuery, Google Cloud Platform, dbt (exposure)
* Analytics: cohort and funnel analysis, segmentation, trend and variance analysis, KPI design
* AI: prompt engineering, AI-assisted analysis with human validation

  
**Additional Information**

**Workplace Environment:**

One of our core values is working as OneTeam. We believe in the value of in-person collaboration while recognizing the importance of flexibility. Public Storage teammates are expected to work in the office five days per week, with the option to use up to three flexible remote-work days each month.

\*\*Sponsorship for Work Authorization is not available for this posting. Candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S. without restrictions or requiring sponsorship now or in the future. We do not provide training plans or support for F-1 OPT, STEM OPT extensions, or future visa sponsorship.\*\*

We’re a startup building a new lab, so you’ll help set it up and your input will shape how it runs.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Own safe work practices in the lab, including PPE, acid handling and housekeeping, and speak up when something isn’t right.
* Handle and prepare ore samples: crushing, screening by particle size, and splitting representative samples.
* Prepare samples for analysis using digestion, dilution and filtration.
* Run elemental and compositional analysis of solid and liquid samples using ICP, AA, XRF and titration, including calibrations and QC checks.
* Build, operate and maintain ore leaching columns alongside R&D and engineering.
* Record results in the lab information system (LIMS) and keep clear, accurate records.
* Perform basic troubleshooting and preventive maintenance on lab and prep equipment.
* Communicate results and issues clearly to the team and at shift handover.
* Help write and improve SOPs as the lab grows.

**Qualifications & Experience**
-------------------------------

* 1+ years of hands-on experience in an analytical, assay, metallurgical or environmental lab. Mining or assay lab experience is a strong plus.
* Hands-on experience with at least one of ICP, AA, XRF or titration.
* Experience with sample prep, including digestion, dilution and filtration.
* Strong safety mindset and experience handling acids and chemicals.
* You follow step-by-step procedures carefully and keep accurate records.
* Comfortable with physical, hands-on work in a lab environment.
* Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in chemistry, geology, metallurgy or a related field preferred.
* Experience with leach or column testing, or with a LIMS, is a plus.

**Schedule**
------------

* Shifts: 8am–5pm and 11am–8pm, with some flexibility when column tests or project deadlines need it.

**Working Environment & Physical Requirements**
-----------------------------------------------

* Hands-on, onsite lab role in the San Francisco Bay Area. You’ll work alongside R&D, process engineering and software teams.
* Lab work involves acids, chemical reagents, and dust and noise from crushing and sample prep equipment. Full PPE is provided and required.
* Physical work: standing for long periods, lifting up to 50 lbs (ore samples, buckets, column materials), and repetitive prep tasks.

**Our culture is built on four principles:**
--------------------------------------------

**Everyone Gets Home Safe.** We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

**Extreme Ownership.** We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

**Engineer Out Requirements, then Automate.** We simplify, optimize, and then automate for scale.

**Share Your Legos.** We collaborate openly, share knowledge, and empower each other to build bigger, better solutions.

**Join us as we build the future of responsible mineral sourcing and supply!**

* **Certified Laboratories** – Provides comprehensive analytical and microbiological testing, primarily supporting food, beverage, cosmetics, OTC, and dietary supplement industries.

Join an award-winning team of dedicated professionals committed to our core values of quality, compassion and community! Chino Valley Medical Center, a member of Prime Healthcare, offers incredible opportunities to expand your horizons and be part of a community dedicated to making a difference.

Chino Valley Medical Center is a 112-bed community hospital established in 1972 and centrally located in Southern California’s Chino Valley. A nine-time recipient of the Healthgrades Patient Safety Excellence Award (2014-2022), Chino Valley Medical Center has been recognized nationally for its quality, including as among the 100 Great Community Hospitals by Becker’s Hospital Review in 2018 and as among the 100 Top Hospitals by IBM Watson Health. Chino Valley Medical Center is committed to serving the community’s health care needs with top-rated emergency care as well as senior services, orthopedics, surgical services and more. Learn more at www.cvmc.com.

  
Responsibilities:

The Certified Phlebotomy Technician I, under California Business and Professions Code section 1246, primarily perform skin puncture or venipuncture on patients of all ages for the purpose of obtaining a blood specimen for analysis in the clinical laboratory and is under the supervision of Laboratory Director / Manager / Supervisor.

This individual: 1) performs computer data entry, filing, telephone communication and other clerical duties, 2) possesses adequate knowledge of the terminology of tests ordered in the laboratory, 3) demonstrates good communication skills and telephone etiquette in greeting patients and other visitors in a polite and friendly manner, 4) demonstrates proper phlebotomy technique and the use of equipment in collecting specimens from newborns to geriatric patients, 5) processes microbiology, immunology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, chemistry and blood bank specimens, 6) processes specimens for referral to reference laboratories, 7) stocks routine supplies, 8) maintains the cleanliness of storage areas, trays, centrifuges, refrigerators, freezers and work areas, 9) processes or load specimens on automated laboratory instrumentation in accordance with established policy and procedures, 10) may be assist to Pick up samples at hospital/ OR, assist lab specialty in sorting out samples for analysis and put away samples, assist pathology, inventory, replenish supplies, order supplies, mail pick up/ delivery, faxing, answering phone, product deliveries, etc.. 11) other tasks or responsibilities may be assigned by the department manager/director.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, TRAINING**

  

* High School Diploma, or equivalent, required.

* Active California Certified Phlebotomy Technician I license required.
* BLS certification within forty-five days of hire and maintained current, according to hospital requirement.
* Minimum of one year of clinical laboratory experience, preferred.

Under the immediate direction of the Laboratory Phlebotomy/Processing Supervisor and the Laboratory Assistant Director, the Certified Phlebotomist II performs various duties associated with specimen collection and processing for laboratory testing. jobs.description:
Description:

Title: QC Technician

Pay Rate: $21.00, DOE

Shift: Graveyard, 9pm-5:30am

Quality Control Technician will be responsible for overseeing the quality of the product being packed on all lines of production during their shift. It is the duty of QC personnel to inform Production Shift Supervisors and/or Manager of any discrepancy during packing to improve or correct the quality of the product. Responsible for sorting and inspecting walnuts during the production process at GDN, and GDN In Shell.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

* HACCP – a daily inspection will be made to ensure that production personnel are correctly performing tasks related to HACCP.
* Pre-operational inspections of the processing equipment.
* ATP Swab at beginning of shift and on allergen change overs.
* Perform oxygen level test when required by work instructions.
* Weight checks of product and controlled weights.
* Employee/staff GMP inspections at the beginning of the shift.
* Production packing lines – check-packing lines at the beginning of the shifts as well as any time product is changed to ensure quality of product is appropriate. Check for any excessive defect found in lines and inform production personnel immediately of any discrepancy.
* Packing labels – check production labels to ensure dates, product and customer information is correct and up to date. Double check customers’ specifications for label at the beginning each order.
* Cracker tests – sample the product being shelled at the cracker and determine the percentage of halves being produced. Determine if percentage is normal and notify supervisor if there are any concerns or discrepancies. Repeat this 3-4 times per shift when cracker is running normally.
* Quality tests – hand sort samples at determined frequency. Collect all defect found from hand inspections and weight to determine percentage that is currently found in product. Make annotations electronically and in QC log for quality records. Let production and WC personnel know of any significant finding immediately.
* DFA paperwork – verify all DFA paperwork at the end of each shift to ensure no mistakes are made by inspectors and notify supervisor if any discrepancies are found.
* Defect from lines – collect all defect found in the reject buckets from the lines at the end of each order completion. Weigh and record the defect and any comments in QC log. Do this for every order being packed during shift.
* Color percentages – sample product from packing lines to obtain a color percentage and make sure it is within the customer’s specifications when
* available. If no specifications are available for color use GDN standards specifications and make sure it is within passing range of DFA inspection. Notify supervisor of any off-color during packing to ensure a prompt correction.
* Overall production quality – evaluate overall packing quality during production, this could include but is not limited to boxes, liner, tape, BHT, weight, labels, sanitation, etc.
* Assist in clean up as needed.
* Follows and ensures adherence to established Grower Direct Nut Co., local, state, and federal regulations and requirements as well as food safety, sanitation, food production and nutritional guidelines.
* Established and ensures adherence to procedures and standards, which are in agreement with these regulations, requirements and guidelines. OTHER RESPONSIBILITIES
* Responsibilities are not limited to the above mentioned and may include assisting other departments within reasonable and related tasks.

Requirements:

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

* Will frequently stand, walk, use hands to finger, handle and feel, reach with hands and arms, talk and hear, taste and smell.
* Will occasionally sit and occasionally climb or balance and stoop, kneel crouch or crawl.
* Must use both hands for rapid mental muscular coordination, simultaneously.
* Must be able to reach high and low levels, frequently.
* Must be able to push/pull/lift with arms below waist/at shoulder/above shoulder level up to 30 pounds frequently.
* Must lift with arms up to floor to waist, waist to shoulder 30 pounds.
* Must be able to constantly stand/stoop/walk/bend, up to 12 hrs.
* Ability to strenuous flex/grip with wrist/hands frequently (15 flexion/minute).
* Work environment
* May work near moving mechanical parts.
* May work around wet or humid conditions, in high, precarious places, fumes or airborne particles, outdoor weather conditions, extreme cold (non-weather), extreme heat (non-weather), risk of electrical shock, and/or risk of vibration

QUALIFICATIONS/SKILLS

* Minimum of High School Diploma or GED equivalent required.
* Ability to multi-task, prioritize jobs.
* Previous Quality Control experience, preferred.
* Must be able to work on many different projects at one time.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills required.
* Must be dependable, reliable, and able to work independently.
* Must be able to work overtime and/or weekends as needed.
* Accurately complete documents and paperwork that is related to the job.
* Must be computer literate.
* Punctual and good attendance is necessary.

jobs.title: Research Associate, Upstream Development
jobs.description:
Description:

**SUMMARY:**

Zylidac Bio LLC is seeking a Research Associate with hands-on cell culture and bench-scale bioreactor experience. The position will support the execution of upstream process development activities within our biologics CDMO operations, working independently on routine assignments and with guidance on more complex studies. The position reports directly to the Sr. Director, Upstream Development. This exciting opportunity offers candidates the chance to be part of a professional, customer-focused pharmaceutical company with a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.

Zylidac Bio LLC is a leading Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization specializing in the development and manufacturing of biologics, particularly antibodies. We are committed to delivering high-quality products and services that meet the evolving needs of our clients in the biopharmaceutical industry.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Upstream Process Development Support

* Execute mammalian cell culture experiments in shake flasks and bench-scale bioreactors (e.g., 3–50 L) following defined protocols.
* Prepare media, feeds, buffers, and cell culture reagents.
* Perform routine bioreactor operations including inoculation, feeding, sampling, and harvest.
* Monitor critical process parameters, including pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), agitation, temperature, and gas flow; perform predefined adjustments according to approved protocols and promptly escalate unexpected trends or deviations.

Data Generation & Documentation

* Collect, perform routine analysis of, and summarize process data, including cell growth, viability, metabolites, and product titer; communicate findings to supervising scientists for interpretation and next-step recommendations.
* Maintain accurate and compliant laboratory documentation in electronic lab notebooks (ELN) or paper records.
* Draft experimental summaries and contribute to technical reports and protocol revisions with guidance.

Analytical & Laboratory Support

* Perform routine upstream analytics (e.g., cell counts, viability, osmolality, glucose/lactate, metabolite analysis).
* Assist scientists with troubleshooting and root cause investigations by documenting observations, compiling data, and executing assigned follow-up experiments under guidance.
* Assist with routine equipment maintenance, calibration checks, and laboratory upkeep under established procedures; escalate equipment issues to the appropriate personnel.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

* Work closely with Process Scientists, Downstream Development, Analytical Development, and Manufacturing teams.
* Support technology transfer readiness by executing assigned studies and generating reproducible upstream data under the guidance of Process Scientists.
* Maintain accurate, complete, and traceable laboratory records in accordance with applicable procedures and data integrity requirements; follow GMP requirements where applicable to assigned activities.

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS – SKILLS & REQUIREMENTS:**

* Experience with common upstream analytical tools for cell counts, viability, osmolality, and glucose/lactate or other metabolite analysis.
* Flexibility to support off-shift or weekend work to meet cell culture study schedules and time-sensitive experimental needs, including manufacturing or troubleshooting support as assigned.
* Ability to independently execute routine assignments, seek guidance when appropriate, and collaborate effectively within a team.
* Demonstrated aseptic mammalian cell culture proficiency.
* Strong experimental execution and organizational skills.
* Clear written and verbal communication, documentation, and problem-solving skills.

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Biochemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
* An associate degree with additional relevant experience may also be considered.
* Typically 0-3 years of hands-on experience in mammalian cell culture or upstream process development with a bachelor’s degree, or 4+ years with an associate degree; relevant industry or academic laboratory experience may be considered.
* Practical experience with shake flasks and bench-scale bioreactors.
* Familiarity with CHO or similar production cell lines.

Extractions

jobs.title: Entry Civil Engineer
jobs.description:
The intent of this job posting is to fill one (1) regular, full-time position and establish an eligibility list which may be used to fill current and future, permanent and limited-term, vacancies for up to two (2) years.

We are posting this opportunity for an Entry Civil Engineer along with a Journey Civil Engineer position. The department will be filling only one position at either level. If you are interested in also being considered for a Journey Civil Engineer, you will need to apply to that requisition separately.

Application Preparation: As part of the application process, candidates will be required to answer four (4) supplemental questions when submitting their application. Please be advised, "Refer to resume" responses will not be accepted.

Purpose

Under general supervision, assists in performing minor to moderately complex civil/structural engineering core responsibilities, including problem resolution/project assignments, in the most efficient, safe and cost-effective manner, and that comply with regulatory requirements and restrictions.

Nature and Scope

There are four (4) levels in this job classification series that have similar job content but with progressively more challenging degrees and levels of skill, responsibility, knowledge, experience and qualification requirements:

Flex Classifications (that permit progression from lower-level classes to higher level classes without examination based upon assessment of an individual's experience and performance) within the series:

Entry:
Incumbent acquires knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the tasks associated within the series but are not yet demonstrating these at the Journey level.
Journey:
Incumbent is demonstrating the required skills and knowledge to independently perform the full scope of the job.

Non-Flex Classifications (that promote from lower-level classes to higher level classes and require an examination, such as an interview, based upon individual experience and performance) within the series:

Senior:
Advanced journey level resource who is responsible for advanced assignments, as dictated by the work needing to be performed; may serve in a lead capacity.
Principal:
Subject matter expert/lead level and is responsible for leading the most advanced work, as dictated by the work needing to be performed.

Entry to Journey: Incumbents at the entry level are required to successfully “progress” to the journey level within 60 months of appointment to remain within the job series.
Seniors and Principals must be hired through a promotional process and do not automatically progress from lower levels in the series.

Duties and Responsibilities

Assists and learns, under the guidance of senior staff, to develop civil construction drawings and mapping related to high voltage electrical transmission and distribution systems for both underground and overhead systems.
Assists in the Civil design work for various SMUD assets, which may include completing studies and calculations of minor projects varying from drainage to structural design; applies national, state, and local agency standards and guidelines while completing engineering work.
Assists in contract and project development under the supervision of other engineering staff.
Supports field crews and contractors to ensure construction is in accordance with SMUD requirements and plans.
Assists and learns to complete project tasks according to industry standards and with industry specific tools including PLS CADD.
Assists and learns to complete design tasks that meet ASCE, ACI, NESC, CPUC General Orders, and company standards.
Assists in the review of developments and encroachments within the Transmission Line rights-of-way.
Learns how to use the full suite of Microsoft products and other applications such as Bluebeam or Adobe to edit PDFs.
Assists with basic design assignments, draft plans, revise drawings, and update maps using AutoCAD and Civil 3D.
Performs other related duties as needed to include working outside of typical business hours when necessary.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in civil engineering from an accredited college or university.

Required Experience Qualifications

At least one (1+) year of progressively responsible relevant work experience in the design, construction, or maintenance of civil or structural assets.

Knowledge Of

Basic theories, principles and practices of civil/structural engineering design; basic theories, principles and regulations governing safety and construction of civil/structural systems and facilities; basic fundamentals, procedures and practices related to construction/fabrication/installation methods, equipment and materials; basic computer aided drafting and design software (such as AutoCAD); basic fundamentals, procedures and practices related to engineering mathematics and statistical analysis techniques; safety policies, practices and procedures; pertinent federal, state, and local codes, laws, and regulations; office procedures, methods, and equipment including computers and applicable software applications such as word processing, spreadsheets, and databases; English grammar, punctuation and vocabulary standards.

Skills To

Nature and Scope

There are four (4) levels in this job classification series that have similar job content but with progressively more challenging degrees and levels of skill, responsibility, knowledge, experience and qualification requirements:

Flex Classifications (that permit progression from lower-level classes to higher level classes without examination based upon assessment of an individual's experience and performance) within the series:

Entry
: Incumbent acquires knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the tasks associated within the series but are not yet demonstrating these at the Journey level.
Journey
: Incumbent is demonstrating the required skills and knowledge to independently perform the full scope of the job.

Non-Flex Classifications (that promote from lower-level classes to higher level classes and require an examination, such as an interview, based upon individual experience and performance) within the series:

Senior
: Advanced journey level resource who is responsible for advanced assignments, as dictated by the work needing to be performed; may serve in a lead capacity.
Principal
: Subject matter expert/lead level and is responsible for leading the most advanced work, as dictated by the work needing to be performed.

Entry to Journey: Incumbents at the entry level are required to successfully “progress” to the journey level within 60 months of appointment to remain within the job series.

jobs.description:
Description

SCHEDULE

Night Shift

4x10 Schedule

LOCATION

There will be a 4 week onsite training in Rancho Bernardo, CA and then the job will be hybrid.

Why Millennium Health?

Millennium Health LLC is an accredited specialty laboratory with more than a decade of experience in medication monitoring and drug testing services, helping clinicians monitor the use and misuse of prescription medications and illicit drugs. The testing is used by healthcare professionals to obtain objective information about patients’ recent use of prescription medications and/or illicit drugs and helps monitor the effectiveness of treatment plans. Everyone that joins our team is key to our ability to support the clinicians and patients.

General Summary

The Clinical Laboratory Scientist, Data Review will review chromatographic data and calculated results obtained from a variety of standardized urinalysis tests in a toxicology laboratory for the detection of prescription and illicit drugs using advanced LC-MS-MS technology and EIA; applies toxicological and chromatographic rule sets to determine acceptability of results; requests additional testing as necessary; approves reports and patient results to ordering physicians.

Essential Functions

The following are intended to be examples of the accountabilities for which the person in this position is responsible. This is not intended to be complete or all-inclusive and does not preclude management from assigning related functions for which the individual has demonstrated competency through performance.

Responsible for testing to troubleshoot result issues.
Reports laboratory test results for all test methods approved by CAP, NY and CLIA.
Ensures accuracy and quality of test results meeting required turnaround times.
Enters testing data and reviews chromatography and calculated results from a variety of standardized tests on urine samples using advanced LC-MS-MS technology and EIA for the detection of prescription and illicit drugs.
Evaluates the validity of results obtained, maintains proper records of results and creates a report of results.
Maintains quality control and LC-MS-MS chromatographic data prior to release or results to physicians.
Ensures that testing methods follow established quality control procedures.
Identifies, troubleshoots, documents and resolves test result issues.
Documents issues using the Laboratory Occurrence Management (LOM) form.
Acts as a resource to laboratory technicians, laboratory assistants and associate scientists.
Follows safe laboratory practices and participates in operational support activities necessary to maintain and optimize testing capabilities.
May oversee the duties of clinical laboratory technicians, clinical laboratory assistants and associate scientists who prepare specimens or perform other less complex procedures.
Participates in internal laboratory audits.

Secondary Accountabilities

Remains aware of evolving needs and opportunities, showing flexibility in doing whatever is appropriate to support the Company’s success. Pursues educational opportunities to maintain advanced and up-to-date knowledge in the field. Performs all other related duties as required and assigned and understands that the items in this description are not all-inclusive.

Requirements

SKILLS/KNOWLEDGE/ABILITIES

2+ years’ experience in high complexity testing; CLIA/CAP environment
Must maintain continuing education units required by California Department of Health Services
Knowledgeable in laboratory methods and techniques
Knowledgeable of equipment and supplies used in a laboratory
Proficient in MS applications (Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Outlook)
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to communicate with all levels of employees
Effective attention to detail with high degree of accuracy
Bachelor’s degree with current California CLS license
ASCP license highly preferred

jobs.title: Remote Medical AI Trainer
jobs.description:
Overview

We are currently hiring experienced clinicians to evaluate how frontier AI models handle real clinical work: an assessment and plan from a history and exam, a medication reconciliation with interaction checks, a triage decision, a discharge summary, patient education, or a clinical protocol. You bring the judgment you have built co signing a resident's note only after fixing the plan, catching the interaction the order set missed, and knowing when a presentation does not fit the obvious diagnosis. We bring the model output that judgment is needed to grade.

In this role, you will design challenging, realistic tasks drawn from your own practice, such as a SOAP note and plan for a constructed case, a medication reconciliation with interaction review, a triage decision with rationale, a discharge summary, a patient education handout, or a clinical protocol or standing order set, run them through frontier AI agents, and evaluate what comes back against a professional standard.

You will work with realistic professional files, the kind a practitioner in your field actually handles, which you assemble yourself. Some tasks are compact, built around a handful of files; others are larger scenarios that take several days to build. In every case the goal is the same: a task a competent professional in your field would complete correctly and a frontier model currently gets wrong.

This is not a traditional clinical role. You will be helping build better AI by putting your knowledge to work in a structured, flexible, fully remote environment. The work is long form and self directed, and clear written reasoning matters as much as technical depth.

Description

Design challenging, realistic clinical tasks drawn from your own day to day practice: the scenario, a prompt phrased the way you would brief a trusted colleague, and the supporting files a clinician would need (constructed or de identified histories, exam findings, labs, imaging reports, medication lists, prior notes), which you author yourself.
Run those tasks through frontier AI models and evaluate the deliverable they produce (the note, plan, reconciliation, summary or protocol) against the standard you would hold a colleague to.
Compare two model outputs on identical prompts and files, decide which performed better, and document where each fell short.
Write detailed grading rubrics that specify what a correct deliverable must contain, such as the right differential considered, the right red flags addressed, the right medication decisions, the right communication for the recipient, and explain in writing why a response passes or fails each one.
Flag concrete failures with evidence: unsupported assessments, missed contraindications or interactions, anchoring on the obvious diagnosis, fabricated or ignored data, unsafe or inappropriate communication, and off brief interpretation of the ask.
Contribute across your setting and adjacent ones, and review and refine tasks built by other clinicians.

Qualifications

2+ years of current or recent hands on clinical practice preferred. In progress Bachelors degree or higher.
Licensed clinician: RN, NP, PA, MD or DO, PharmD, or an allied health license with independent clinical judgment (for example respiratory therapy, physical therapy, midwifery). Licensed candidates may be asked to verify licensure during the assessment.
Depth in at least one setting or specialty: acute care and med surg, emergency, critical care, primary care and family medicine, pediatrics, obstetrics, behavioral health, geriatrics and long term care, perioperative, oncology, pharmacy.
Working understanding of adjacent settings, enough to know what those workflows involve and how they are run, so you can assess work outside your own unit and point out what was done correctly or incorrectly.
Reads and writes clinical documentation at a practitioner level and grounds decisions in current guidelines and the patient context rather than habit.

Additional Information

100% fully remote.
Can be part time or full time. Minimum requirement is 10 hours per week.

Doctors
