jobs.description:
About Us

Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We are celebrating our 100-year legacy in 2024. This significant milestone marks a century of seminal discoveries in immunology, infectious diseases (such as COVID-19, flu, HIV), neuroscience, heart disease, cancer, and more. Located in La Jolla, California, the institute houses six research departments, multiple Nobel laureates, a top-ranked graduate school and a leading postdoctoral training program. We work hand-in-hand with researchers of the Scripps Research Translational Institute and Calibr to merge foundational studies in biology, chemistry and computer science with translational science to produce pioneering drugs and advances in digital and precision medicine. Together, we cultivate new scientific leaders and expand the frontiers of knowledge to deliver medical breakthroughs impacting human health around the globe. If you have a passion for making a difference, this could be your opportunity to join our transformative team.

POSITION TITLE:
Research Assistant II

Position Summary

Plan and conduct complex research projects centered on 3D organoid culture, primary tissue cell isolation, and assay development in support of translational research programs. Independently perform non-routine procedures, develop new or improved techniques, design experimental approaches, analyze data, and interpret complex results. Operate sophisticated scientific lab equipment; plan and execute discrete projects or significant portions of larger research initiatives; may provide work direction and training to junior staff. Perform other related duties as required. This is an on site position based on our La Jolla, CA campus.

Responsibilities And Duties

Work under minimal supervision and independently execute a broad range of laboratory techniques, exercising judgment to adapt established methods to project-specific requirements. Receive direction on overall objectives, complex experimental features, and potential approaches.
Isolate primary cells from human tissue specimens, including biopsies and surgical resections. Establish, maintain, passage, and characterize 3D organoid cultures derived from primary human tissue, with particular attention to viability, growth kinetics, and phenotypic stability.
Develop, optimize, and validate cell-based assays in 3D organoid and primary cell systems, including readouts for viability, proliferation, differentiation, drug response, and disease-relevant phenotypes.
Maintain iPSC cultures including directed differentiation protocols and downstream characterization.
Process in vivo samples and integrate ex vivo data with in vitro experimental results.
Interpret and analyze experimental data; troubleshoot technical issues and modify procedures to improve robustness, throughput, or biological relevance.
Contribute to experimental design as part of broader research plans. May perform routine equipment maintenance and provide technical guidance and training to other team members.
Perform other related duties, tasks and responsibilities as required or assigned.

Position Requirements

Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific discipline (cell biology, molecular biology, biomedical engineering, or related field), or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
Requires 3-5 years of experience. Candidates possessing a master’s degree, 2+ years of experience required.
Hands-on experience with 3D organoid culture is required, including establishment from primary tissue, long-term maintenance, passaging, and characterization. Familiarity with patient-derived organoid systems strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience isolating primary cells from human tissue (biopsy, surgical resection, or equivalent), including enzymatic/mechanical dissociation, viability assessment, and downstream culture establishment.
Proficiency with standard cell culture techniques.
Experience with imaging, flow cytometry, qPCR, or other relevant characterization methods.
Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and ability to communicate experimental results clearly.

Physical Requirments

This position works in a laboratory or vivarium environment.
Details of established essential functions for this position will be addressed/discussed during the interview process.

Compensation

The expected hiring range for this position is $70,304 to $75,000 per year, commensurate with experience. Consideration will be given to experience that exceeds the listed requirements.

Comprehensive Benefits Include

Employer Contributed Retirement Plan – Depending on eligibility, employees receive an employer contributed retirement plan (no employee contribution required) and the option to contribute to a 403(b) using your own pre or post-tax dollars.
Full Suite of Health and Welfare plans including four medical plan options (including an HSA available option), dental, vision, life insurance, disability, EAP and more
Access to Flexible Spending Accounts (Medical/Dependent Care)
Competitive vacation and sick leave policies
Free, on-site parking

jobs.title: Human Genetics and Genomic Curation Research Assistant (Research Data Assistant)
jobs.description:
MMGE - MOLECULAR GENETICS (IN-MOLG-IUINA)

One of the first human genetics departments in the country, the Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics at Indiana University (IU) School of Medicine has a rich history of training geneticists and genetic counselors and providing genetic consultation and counseling services. Currently ranked fifth in the nation among Genetics Departments for National Institutes of Health (NIH) Funding, received in 2023, the department contributes to the understanding of numerous genetic conditions through the integration of basic research in genetic and genomic mechanisms, translational research in disease models, and clinical trials in rare and common genetic diseases.

This research-focused position in the Azaiez-Booth Laboratory supports investigation of how genes and genetic variants contribute to human disease. The role combines scientific literature evaluation, genomic evidence curation, and research-data analysis across projects in human genetics and genomic medicine. Current activities include work with the ClinGen Hearing Loss Expert Panels, whose gene and variant classifications are publicly released and used by clinical laboratories to interpret genetic test results, as well as related laboratory and collaborative research projects.

Department-Specific Responsibilities

Evaluates and synthesizes scientific evidence, contributing to gene-disease and variant assessments, discusses findings with researchers, clinicians, and expert-panel members, and helps prepare presentations, reports, and manuscripts.
Identifies and critically reviews relevant scientific literature and genomic resources.
Extracts and synthesizes genetic, genomic, and clinical information, including population, segregation, functional, and computational evidence.
Applies established curation frameworks to prepare preliminary gene-disease validity assessments and variant evidence curations, documenting the rationale and questions requiring further scientific review.
Maintains accurate, well-documented research databases and curation records, including supporting references and assessment rationales.
Performs quality and consistency checks, synthesizes findings across curations and research datasets.
Conducts descriptive analyses to support laboratory and collaborative projects.
Prepares evidence summaries, tables, figures, and presentations.
Presents assigned work at laboratory and collaborative meetings, including virtual ClinGen Hearing Loss Expert Panel meetings; explains the evidence and criteria applied; and participates in scientific discussion.
Incorporates feedback and contributes to technical reports, grant progress reports, abstracts, and manuscript components.
Helps develop and improve research resources, templates, and procedural documentation.
Organizes assigned work, maintain clear records of progress and outstanding questions, and communicate with supervisors and collaborators to meet agreed priorities and timelines.

General Responsibilities

Assists with the research and collection of data from internal and/or external sources in support of research project(s).
Conducts descriptive analysis with collected data and assists with evaluative analysis.
Creates, updates, and maintains various databases and charts.
Prepares data analysis and grant reports for funding agencies.
Assists with creating technical reports, journal articles, and public presentations as needed.
May develop, schedule, or coordinate projects in support of research efforts.
May assist project personnel in the development of research projects.

Combinations of related education and experience may be considered. Education beyond the minimum required may be substituted for work experience. Work experience beyond the minimum required may be substituted for education.

EDUCATION

Required

Bachelor's degree (preferably in public policy, public administration, public health, social sciences, or a related field)

Preferred

Bachelor's degree in genetics, genomics, molecular biology, biology, biochemistry, biomedical sciences, neuroscience, bioinformatics, or a closely related scientific or health-related field
Coursework or additional training in human genetics, genomics, molecular genetics, genetic disease, molecular biology, bioinformatics, or a related biomedical discipline

Preferred

WORK EXPERIENCE

Some experience in a related field
Experience in an academic, clinical, laboratory, computational, or biomedical research setting; or work with human genetic, genomic, clinical, biological, or other scientific datasets
Prior gene or variant curation experience

Skills

Required

Proficient written and verbal communication skills
Maintains a high degree of professionalism
Demonstrated time management and priority setting skills
Demonstrates a high commitment to quality
Possesses flexibility to work in a fast paced, dynamic environment
Highly thorough and dependable
Familiarity with and openness to learn qualitative and mixed methods
Familiarity with statistical software preferred.
Must possess strong attention to detail.

This role requires the ability to effectively communicate and to operate a computer and other standard office productivity equipment. jobs.description:
Job Summary
We are seeking a Software Engineer with a strong embedded systems background to design, develop, and execute validation test code for hardware and firmware platforms. In this role, you will analyze hardware schematics, datasheets, and firmware interface documentation to translate complex technical requirements into executable test scripts. Working in a fast-paced lab environment, you will handle on-demand test requests, validate behavior on embedded targets and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) setups, and drive root-cause failure analysis across hardware, firmware, and test-code layers.

Key Responsibilities
Requirement Translation & Test Development:
Read technical documentation—including schematics, datasheets, register maps, and firmware specs—to extract requirements and write original, executable test code in Python and Lua.
Rapid Prototyping & Execution:
Respond quickly to evolving and on-demand test requirements, delivering reliable validation code for embedded targets, bring-up boards, and HIL setups.
Code Quality & Debugging:
Write unit tests and actively debug your own code using debuggers, breakpoints, logging, and embedded debug tools (e.g., JTAG/SWD, serial consoles) rather than relying solely on end-to-end test reruns.
Failure Analysis & Triage:
Perform hands-on fault isolation, issue reproduction, and root-cause analysis by examining boot logs, panic/crash logs, core dumps, and device telemetry to separate hardware, firmware, and software issues.
Lab Validation:
Operate lab instrumentation—including oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, and multimeters—to verify signal integrity, hardware interfaces, and device behavior.
Production & End-to-End Testing:
Execute dry runs, support hardware/firmware test stations, and run diagnostic tooling within production software environments.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Clearly document test findings and proactively communicate design decisions, workflows, and failure root causes to hardware, firmware, and software engineering teams.

Basic Qualifications (Must-Have)
Education:
BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science (with an embedded focus), or equivalent practical experience.
Programming & Scripting:
Strong hands-on proficiency in Python (writing original code from scratch) and the ability to translate requirements into working scripts in real time (Python, Lua, etc.).
Embedded Systems:
Hands-on experience with firmware or embedded software on microcontrollers or SoCs, with a deep understanding of hardware-software interactions.
Hardware Protocols:
Working knowledge of communication interfaces and protocols including UART, SPI, I2C, USB, and CAN.
Hardware Validation & Lab Tools:
Proven experience with board bring-up, HIL testing, test fixtures, and using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, and power supplies.
Diagnostics & Triage:
Demonstrated ability to analyze boot logs, crash dumps, and telemetry to isolate and reproduce faults.
Software Engineering Practices:
Solid experience writing unit tests, using interactive debuggers, and running code across multiple software suites.
Communication & Agility:
Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to explain technical thought processes unprompted, adapt to rapid requirement shifts, and maintain flexible hours when project milestones require it.

Intuit is a global technology platform that helps consumers and small businesses overcome their most important financial challenges. This role leads partnership across analysts, engineers, data scientists, researchers, marketers, communicators, and product managers, mentoring other analysts and setting the standard for how we deliver operational dashboards and analyses that drive business decisions. This person operates with a high degree of autonomy, translates ambiguous business questions into rigorous analytical frameworks, and regularly presents findings and recommendations to senior leadership. Responsibilities

Own and drive the measurement strategy for high-priority initiatives across Intuit platform, establishing comprehensive KPI frameworks, leading indicators, and analytical approaches that connect activities and investments to business outcomes.

Lead high-impact, cross-functional analytical initiatives that span multiple programs, stakeholders, and data domains, navigating ambiguity and aligning teams around shared objectives and measurable outcomes.
Proactively identify emerging trends, performance opportunities, and business risks, moving beyond descriptive reporting to deliver predictive and prescriptive insights that shape future strategies.

Provide technical leadership in the design and application of advanced analytical methodologies, including experimentation, causal inference, incrementality measurement, attribution modeling, forecasting, and statistical modeling.
Establish rigorous analytical frameworks to evaluate the effectiveness of brand, reputation, internal and external communications, and corporate responsibility initiatives.
Lead the development of scalable measurement approaches that enable a holistic understanding of performance across channels, audiences, and initiatives.
Partner with data engineering, data science, and technology teams to influence data architecture, instrumentation, data pipelines, and analytical infrastructure that support reliable, scalable, and efficient decision-making.
Identify and champion opportunities to leverage emerging analytical techniques, automation, and AI-enabled capabilities to improve analytical efficiency, depth, and business impact.
Maintain hands-on technical expertise, independently conducting complex analyses, developing analytical prototypes, and solving challenging data problems when needed.

Qualifications

8+ years of experience working in a data analytics role supporting marketing and web, including leading complex, ambiguous analytical initiatives.

Hands-on expertise with Python and statistical modeling techniques (e.g. regression, classification, time series) to answer a wide range of measurement questions. Familiarity with market mix modeling and multi-touch attribution is a plus.
Hands-on experience with web analytics and clickstream data to support event tracking and instrumentation (e.g., Adobe Analytics, Segment, marketing attribution) preferred.
Meticulous attention to detail, with the ability to consistently produce accurate and error-free work even under tight deadlines.
Ability to tell stories clearly and concisely with data, and how they drive business outcomes.
Demonstrates strong business acumen and curiosity.
Ability to lead through influence across all levels and possess strong written and verbal communication skills. Outstanding communications skills with both technical and non-technical colleagues.
Excellent problem-solving skills and end-to-end quantitative thinking.

The Position

2027 Summer Intern – Translational Safety (Bioinformatics)

Department Summary

We are now accepting applications for the Genentech 2027 Summer Internship Program in Development Sciences (DevSci); this post is for a computational biology role in Translational Safety (TS). Translational Safety is an integral part of DevSci. We contribute to the organization’s success by providing scientific insights and ensuring the safety of molecules that advance through the pipeline to patients. We do this to support the DevSci vision to deliver the right drug in the right dose to the right patient. We are also committed to providing better outcomes for our people, patients, business, and communities by advancing and boldly championing diversity, equity, and inclusion in our work.

The selected candidate will use dose-resolved single-cell RNA-seq data to model how cell populations respond to chemical perturbations. The intern will benchmark foundation models alongside other computational approaches for capturing dose-dependent responses and predicting the effects of previously unseen compounds. The project will also compare in vitro perturbation states with relevant in vivo cellular programs to identify response features that are most informative for human-relevant toxicology.

This internship position is located in South San Francisco, on-site.

The Opportunity

Model perturbation responses: Develop and benchmark computational approaches to capture reproducible, dose-dependent cellular responses.
Test generalization: Evaluate whether learned response patterns can predict the effects of compounds not used during model development.
Interpret mechanisms of toxicity: Integrate transcriptomic responses with biological pathways, chemical properties, and toxicological information to understand cellular stress and injury.
Assess translational relevance: Compare in vitro perturbation signatures with relevant in vivo cellular programs to evaluate their relevance for human safety.

Program Highlights

Intensive 12-weeks, full-time (40 hours per week) paid internship.
Program start dates are in May/June (Summer).
A stipend, based on location, will be provided to help alleviate costs associated with the internship.
Ownership of challenging and impactful business-critical projects.
Work with some of the most talented people in the biotechnology industry.

Required Education

Required Majors:
STEM major (preferably in Toxicology or related) with coursework in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Data Science, Computer Science, Bioengineering or similar.

Required Skills

Experience working in an HPC/cloud environment to manage large biological datasets.
Familiarity with machine learning frameworks or predictive modeling.
Experience analyzing transcriptomic, proteomic, or other high-dimensional biological data.

Knowledge of liver biology and toxicology.

Department Overview

This position provides technical support in the Transfusion Services to complete laboratory testing for OHSU

hospital and clinic patients. The incumbent will be a qualified Medical Laboratory Technician with generalist

processes utilizing both gel and tube. This position will also have some limited testing responsibilities in the

Core Lab. Specimen processing, test performance, and result reporting is performed independently after

appropriate training. Additional review of results is required in the case of unusual/complex results,

procedural problems, or when dictated by policy or procedure. The person filling this position will be of

professional demeanor and perform their duties with an attitude, which will best serve the clients of the

department.

Function/Duties of Position

Medical Laboratory Technician Testing Duties

Perform routine lab testing; accurately record results and interpretations by computer entry and/or legibly in writing.
Use lab instruments to include the Grifols Erytra. Utilize supplies and equipment responsibly and according to lab and manufacturer's guidelines and Transfusion Service procedures.
Perform gel and manual serologic testing to resolve problems encountered in routine testing, accurately record results and interpretations.
Follow established policies and procedures but obtain consult to resolve complex issues; bring to the attention of the Medical Laboratory Scientists, Technical Coordinator, Manager, or Medical Director. Seek guidance from or notify the Technical Coordinator, Manager, Medical Director, or Resident, when appropriate.

Recognize incorrect or unusual blood product orders and take steps to modify the order after consult with patient physician or Transfusion Service medical staff or resident.
Maintain and manage an adequate inventory of perishable blood products and ensure that excessive wastage does not occur.

Sign in blood products received from Red Cross with appropriate documentation. Issue and receive blood products to and from patient care areas.

Perform Quality control, periodic maintenance and Proficiency Testing as assigned.
Perform and document maintenance of analyzers, blood storage and other equipment. Troubleshoot equipment and interact with vendors, as needed.

Document proper temperature of blood products in transit from hospital to hospital, and internally at OHSU.
Inspect blood products for appropriate appearance. Organize, check for accuracy, and report blood product usage statistics as assigned.
Maintain inventory of supplies and ordering; alert Technical Coordinator or Manager when supplies are low in a timely manner.
Accurately bill blood products and testing, and record audit trail of product use in compliance with regulatory and accrediting requirements.

Completion of a 2 year accredited program in Medical Laboratory Technician training plus MLT (ASCP) within 90 days of hire or AMT certification within 90 days of hire. Depending on date of training, different continuing education requirements will apply. OR
Bachelor’s degree in a chemical or biological science and two years of Laboratory Technical Assistant training/experience performing standardized laboratory tests in the specialty area(s) in which high complexity testing will be performed; MLT (ASCP) or AMT certification preferred. Depending on date of training, different continuing education requirements will apply.

General knowledge of laboratory terminology, equipment, materials and techniques, regulations and safety.
Skill in handling of laboratory specimens, record keeping and laboratory equipment.
Skill in identifying cells and cell morphology.
Skill in using several different computer systems, including: word processing, dedicated LIS/HIS, etc.
Ability to follow written and oral instructions accurately, and operate and maintain standard laboratory equipment.
Ability to work independently within established guidelines, to adjust to rapidly changing priorities, and apply problem-solving skills.
Ability to demonstrate performance of job duties to trainees.
Demonstrate personal integrity, efficiency, and ability to adjust to rapidly changing testing priorities.
Ability to work in a multi-tasking environment and display technical skills at many different workstations throughout the laboratory.

Preferred Qualifications

Generalist experience in Transfusion Services within last two years preferred.

and holidays; working at multiple laboratory or hospital sites; traveling between laboratories and sites by

jobs.description:
The group you’ll be a part of

In the Global Products Group, we are dedicated to excellence in the design and engineering of Lam's etch and deposition products. We drive innovation to ensure our cutting-edge solutions are helping to solve the biggest challenges in the semiconductor industry.

The impact you’ll make

Join Lam as a Product Engineer with expertise in Data Science and Advanced Analytics, where you'll combine hands-on semiconductor experimentation with modern analytical methods to solve complex process and hardware challenges.

In this role, you will work directly with process development, technology development, product engineering, and customer escalations. You will design and execute experiments, develop advanced test vehicles, analyze data from multiple sources, and apply statistical and machine learning techniques to identify root causes, optimize processes, and uncover underlying physical mechanisms.

Operating at the intersection of semiconductor engineering, experimental science, and data analytics, you will transform laboratory and field data into actionable insights that improve product performance, accelerate technology development, and support data-driven engineering decisions.

What You’ll Do

This position is for a Product Engineer with Data Science specialization within the Selective Etch Product Group, part of the Global Products Group, based in Fremont, CA.

Process Development & Engineering

Perform process engineering research, development, characterization, and evaluation in support of Lam's semiconductor capital equipment and systems.
Support new technology development, product qualification, and customer deployment activities.
Design, execute, and analyze experiments to investigate process, hardware, and system-level performance.
Develop advanced test vehicles and apply systematic problem-solving methodologies to improve product capability and reliability.
Compile and evaluate experimental data to establish process understanding and engineering recommendations.

Customer Escalations & Root Cause Analysis

Lead technical investigations associated with customer escalations by combining engineering fundamentals, experimental observations, and advanced analytics.
Apply statistical analysis, engineering judgment, and structured root-cause methodologies to identify failure mechanisms and drive corrective actions.
Partner with cross-functional teams to rapidly resolve product and process issues impacting customer performance.

Data Science, AI & Advanced Analytics

Develop predictive models and data-driven methodologies that improve understanding of process behavior and equipment performance.
Apply machine learning, artificial intelligence, statistical modeling, and advanced analytics techniques to laboratory, manufacturing, and field data sets.
Develop analytics tools, automated workflows, and visualization methods that enable engineers to efficiently analyze complex datasets.
Utilize data science methodologies to optimize experiments, improve process windows, accelerate root cause analysis, and support technology development.

Collaboration & Communication

Collaborate closely with process engineers, hardware engineers, systems engineers, field organizations, and customers to solve challenging technical problems.
Communicate technical findings and recommendations clearly to engineering teams, management, and customer stakeholders.
Contribute to building a culture of scientific rigor and data-driven decision making across the organization.

PhD or Master's degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Engineering Physics, or a related engineering or scientific discipline.
Demonstrated expertise in Data Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Statistics, Scientific Computing, or Advanced Analytics.
Strong foundation in engineering fundamentals, experimental methods, and quantitative analysis.
Experience designing, executing, and interpreting laboratory, research, or engineering experiments.
Proven ability to apply statistical methods, machine learning, or AI techniques to scientific or engineering problems.
Programming experience with Python and commonly used scientific computing, machine learning, and data analytics libraries.
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to audiences with varied levels of expertise.
Passion for solving real-world engineering challenges through a combination of experimentation, data analysis, and scientific reasoning.

Candidates with advanced degrees in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or related quantitative disciplines may also be considered if they have demonstrated experience applying data science techniques to experimental, scientific, manufacturing, semiconductor, or engineering problems.

Preferred Qualifications

Semiconductor process, equipment, product engineering, or technology development experience.
Experience with semiconductor plasma, etch, deposition, surface science, or related applications.
Experience applying AI and machine learning techniques to physical systems, manufacturing processes, or scientific data.
Knowledge of Design of Experiments (DOE), Statistical Process Control (SPC), multivariate statistics, regression analysis, and predictive modeling.
Experience developing predictive models, anomaly detection algorithms, or engineering analytics tools.
Laboratory experience involving physics, chemistry, materials characterization, or semiconductor process development.
Experience translating experimental observations into predictive models and actionable engineering recommendations.
Familiarity with root cause analysis methodologies and failure analysis techniques.
Strong organizational skills and demonstrated ability to manage multiple technical projects simultaneously.
Excellent collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively in cross-functional and matrixed environments.

Automation & Tooling: Build robust Python-based frameworks for automated testbench generation, regression management, and intelligent failure triage.
Infrastructure Architecting: Design, develop, and maintain CAD infrastructure for verification. Enable seamless handoffs between IP & SOC verification teams. Use advanced techniques like formal verification paired with AI to shift left verification development.

jobs.title: Electrical Walkdown/Turnover Subject Matter Expert (SME) (Data Center)
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Here at Jacobs, we apply our expertise and knowledge as we look into the future with great optimism and focus. We don’t settle until we give our best and know that we’re making a difference.

We're seeking to hire an Electrical Walkdown/Turnover SME
for an onsite role at our data center project in Saint Francisville, LA
.

As an Electrical Walkdown/Turnover Subject Matter Expert
, you will be responsible for coordinating and facilitating the field verification and documentation of electrical systems and equipment installed by Construction.

This will be achieved through technical leadership of electrical walkdown activities on an active construction site. You will guide construction, electrical subcontractor, field Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client personnel through defined system, subsystem, partial-system, and equipment scopes.

You will actively collaborate with field quality and electrical subcontractors to verify adherence to applicable inspection, testing, and turnover-documentation requirements. This includes confirming that required pre-commissioning activities have been performed and that supporting records are available for insulation-resistance testing, continuity testing, grounding and bonding verification, torque verification, cable testing, phase rotation, and voltage verification.

The role does not independently perform, approve, or certify electrical testing unless specifically authorized and qualified to do so. Its primary responsibility is to verify that the required work and supporting documentation are complete, traceable, and suitable for turnover progression.

You will use CxAlloy for punch-list entry and tracking, readiness reviews, test-record visibility, walkdown documentation, and assembly of electrical construction turnover packages. You may also use Autodesk Construction Cloud to review applicable drawings, submittals, RFIs, field records, and quality documentation.

In coordination with Project Controls, Construction, Quality, Turnover, Startup, and CQV, you will help provide a planned and documented approach for the final turnover of electrical facilities, systems, and equipment in alignment with the P6 schedule and verified field readiness.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and facilitate electrical walkdowns with Construction, subcontractors, Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client representatives.
Serve as the primary electrical technical resource for walkdown preparation, field verification, punch development, and turnover-package review.
Confirm that walkdown scope is clearly defined by system, subsystem, equipment, area, and applicable boundary.
Participate with Construction and CQV in establishing logical electrical system and partial-system boundaries that support timely installation, construction completion, turnover, startup, and commissioning.
Read and interpret single-line diagrams, wiring and connection diagrams, electrical schematics, cable schedules, panel schedules, equipment layouts, grounding drawings, control diagrams, and vendor drawings.
Verify installed electrical work against approved drawings, project specifications, applicable checklists, and defined turnover scope.
Confirm that equipment and asset tags are installed, legible, and aligned with applicable drawings and turnover records.
Review the availability and traceability of megger and insulation-resistance records, continuity and point-to-point records, grounding and bonding records, torque and termination records, cable test records, breaker test records, transformer inspection and test records, phase-rotation records, and voltage-verification records.
Identify incomplete construction, missing documentation, incorrect installation, accessibility concerns, labeling deficiencies, and turnover-boundary discrepancies.
Document field conditions accurately and objectively without assuming responsibility for contractor correction or construction completion.
Enter and track electrical punch-list items in CxAlloy using clear descriptions of the exact location, equipment or system, observed condition, and required correction.
Coordinate with Construction and field Quality regarding issues identified during electrical walkdowns; support assignment of punch ownership and target dates.
Review submitted punch-closure evidence and coordinate reinspection when required while preserving applicable Quality, commissioning, and client acceptance requirements.
Review electrical turnover packages for completeness, organization, traceability, and alignment with the defined scope, including applicable drawings, inspection records, test records, checklists, certificates, punch status, and supporting documentation.
Coordinate electrical readiness forecasts with the P6 schedule and identify milestone dates not supported by verified field or documentation readiness.
Participate in turnover planning, readiness reviews, construction-completion discussions, and construction-to-CQV handoff activities.
Promote a professional, collaborative, and problem-solving culture and support continuous improvement of electrical walkdown checklists and documentation practices.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
At least 5 years of electrical construction, Quality, commissioning, startup, or turnover experience, including at least 2 years focused on electrical systems turnover, walkdowns, or systems completion.
Experience on data center, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial, power, utility, or other major capital projects.
Ability to lead electrical walkdowns with subcontractors, Quality personnel, CQV representatives, and clients.
Ability to read and interpret electrical construction drawings and vendor documentation.
Knowledge of electrical installation, inspection, testing, and turnover-documentation requirements.
Understanding of systems-based scoping, electrical turnover-package assembly, LOTO processes, and electrical safe-work requirements.
Strong organization, issue tracking, communication, and collaboration skills.
Ability to spend continuous hours on an active construction site, including wearing PPE, traversing stairs, walking through construction areas, and participating in standing field meetings.
Ability to remain onsite for the duration of the assignment.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Experience with CxAlloy and Autodesk Construction Cloud.
Familiarity with Good Documentation Practices and P6 turnover milestone planning.
Experience with medium-voltage equipment, transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, busway, grounding systems, or data-center electrical distribution.
OSHA 30
Familiarity with NFPA 70, NFPA 70E, and applicable NETA testing practices.
Experience reviewing electrical turnover packages and punch-list closure evidence.

jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Here at Jacobs, we apply our expertise and knowledge as we look into the future with great optimism and focus. We don’t settle until we give our best and know that we’re making a difference.

We're seeking to hire an Electrical Walkdown/Turnover SME
for an onsite role at our data center project in Saint Francisville, LA
.

As an Electrical Walkdown/Turnover Subject Matter Expert
, you will be responsible for coordinating and facilitating the field verification and documentation of electrical systems and equipment installed by Construction.

This will be achieved through technical leadership of electrical walkdown activities on an active construction site. You will guide construction, electrical subcontractor, field Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client personnel through defined system, subsystem, partial-system, and equipment scopes.

You will actively collaborate with field quality and electrical subcontractors to verify adherence to applicable inspection, testing, and turnover-documentation requirements. This includes confirming that required pre-commissioning activities have been performed and that supporting records are available for insulation-resistance testing, continuity testing, grounding and bonding verification, torque verification, cable testing, phase rotation, and voltage verification.

The role does not independently perform, approve, or certify electrical testing unless specifically authorized and qualified to do so. Its primary responsibility is to verify that the required work and supporting documentation are complete, traceable, and suitable for turnover progression.

You will use CxAlloy for punch-list entry and tracking, readiness reviews, test-record visibility, walkdown documentation, and assembly of electrical construction turnover packages. You may also use Autodesk Construction Cloud to review applicable drawings, submittals, RFIs, field records, and quality documentation.

In coordination with Project Controls, Construction, Quality, Turnover, Startup, and CQV, you will help provide a planned and documented approach for the final turnover of electrical facilities, systems, and equipment in alignment with the P6 schedule and verified field readiness.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and facilitate electrical walkdowns with Construction, subcontractors, Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client representatives.
Serve as the primary electrical technical resource for walkdown preparation, field verification, punch development, and turnover-package review.
Confirm that walkdown scope is clearly defined by system, subsystem, equipment, area, and applicable boundary.
Participate with Construction and CQV in establishing logical electrical system and partial-system boundaries that support timely installation, construction completion, turnover, startup, and commissioning.
Read and interpret single-line diagrams, wiring and connection diagrams, electrical schematics, cable schedules, panel schedules, equipment layouts, grounding drawings, control diagrams, and vendor drawings.
Verify installed electrical work against approved drawings, project specifications, applicable checklists, and defined turnover scope.
Confirm that equipment and asset tags are installed, legible, and aligned with applicable drawings and turnover records.
Review the availability and traceability of megger and insulation-resistance records, continuity and point-to-point records, grounding and bonding records, torque and termination records, cable test records, breaker test records, transformer inspection and test records, phase-rotation records, and voltage-verification records.
Identify incomplete construction, missing documentation, incorrect installation, accessibility concerns, labeling deficiencies, and turnover-boundary discrepancies.
Document field conditions accurately and objectively without assuming responsibility for contractor correction or construction completion.
Enter and track electrical punch-list items in CxAlloy using clear descriptions of the exact location, equipment or system, observed condition, and required correction.
Coordinate with Construction and field Quality regarding issues identified during electrical walkdowns; support assignment of punch ownership and target dates.
Review submitted punch-closure evidence and coordinate reinspection when required while preserving applicable Quality, commissioning, and client acceptance requirements.
Review electrical turnover packages for completeness, organization, traceability, and alignment with the defined scope, including applicable drawings, inspection records, test records, checklists, certificates, punch status, and supporting documentation.
Coordinate electrical readiness forecasts with the P6 schedule and identify milestone dates not supported by verified field or documentation readiness.
Participate in turnover planning, readiness reviews, construction-completion discussions, and construction-to-CQV handoff activities.
Promote a professional, collaborative, and problem-solving culture and support continuous improvement of electrical walkdown checklists and documentation practices.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
At least 5 years of electrical construction, Quality, commissioning, startup, or turnover experience, including at least 2 years focused on electrical systems turnover, walkdowns, or systems completion.
Experience on data center, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial, power, utility, or other major capital projects.
Ability to lead electrical walkdowns with subcontractors, Quality personnel, CQV representatives, and clients.
Ability to read and interpret electrical construction drawings and vendor documentation.
Knowledge of electrical installation, inspection, testing, and turnover-documentation requirements.
Understanding of systems-based scoping, electrical turnover-package assembly, LOTO processes, and electrical safe-work requirements.
Strong organization, issue tracking, communication, and collaboration skills.
Ability to spend continuous hours on an active construction site, including wearing PPE, traversing stairs, walking through construction areas, and participating in standing field meetings.
Ability to remain onsite for the duration of the assignment.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Experience with CxAlloy and Autodesk Construction Cloud.
Familiarity with Good Documentation Practices and P6 turnover milestone planning.
Experience with medium-voltage equipment, transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, busway, grounding systems, or data-center electrical distribution.
OSHA 30
Familiarity with NFPA 70, NFPA 70E, and applicable NETA testing practices.
Experience reviewing electrical turnover packages and punch-list closure evidence.

Nestled between Burbank and Pasadena, Adventist Health Glendale is one of the area's leading healthcare providers. Adventist Health Glendale is proud to be part of the thriving, diverse community since 1905.

Job Summary

Prioritizes and performs a wide variety of clinical laboratory tests on various biological specimens. Reviews, evaluates, documents and reports results. Preserves confidentiality of patients and follows lab safety and maintenance protocols. Serves as technical consultant upon delegation by the medical director and mentor to laboratory personnel and trains and supervises trainees, laboratory assistants and clerks as needed.

Job Requirements

Education and Work Experience:

Bachelor’s Degree in medical technology, clinical laboratory science, biological sciences, chemical sciences or allied health technologies or equivalent: Required
Three years' clinical laboratory experience: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications

Valid Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) license in state of employment: Required in CA
Current certification from American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) or National Credentialing Agency for Labs (NCA): Preferred

Essential Functions

Employs positive patient identification procedures to ensure the integrity of each specimen for pre-analytical, analytical and post-analytical testing. Performs proper specimen collection (including phlebotomy procedures as necessary), labeling, handling, preservation or fixation, processing or preparation, transportation and storage. Adheres to Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and other patient confidentiality guidelines and regulations.
Prioritizes lab orders according to type (STAT, ASAP, routine and timed studies) and performs various testing (including chemistry, coagulation, hematology, special chemistry, urinalysis, blood bank, serology, immunology, bacteriology, microbiology, referral testing and more) following prescribed quality assurance policies and procedures. Takes strides to contain costs without sacrificing patient care.
Reviews and evaluates the validity and accuracy of test results, recognizing the interdependency of tests, the physiological conditions affecting results, patient age and normal values, controls, linearity errors, instrument codes, delta checks and more. Correlates test results with diagnoses and questions incompatible results. Documents and communicates test results, expediting all critical values and results to appropriate clinicians.
Performs equipment and instrumentation maintenance, troubleshooting and calibration as needed. Inventories reagents, calibrators, controls and supplies, noticing usage trends and stocking accordingly. Demonstrates working knowledge to troubleshoot and utilize laboratory instrumentation and equipment. Serves as technical consultant and mentor of laboratory personnel. At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

Here at Jacobs, we apply our expertise and knowledge as we look into the future with great optimism and focus. We don’t settle until we give our best and know that we’re making a difference.

We're seeking to hire an CSA
Walkdown/Turnover SME
for an onsite role at our data center project in Saint Francisville, LA
.

As a Civil, Structural, and Architectural Walkdown/Turnover Subject Matter Expert
, you will be responsible for coordinating and facilitating the field verification and documentation of civil, structural, and architectural work installed by Construction.

You will provide technical leadership during CSA walkdowns on an active construction site, guiding construction, subcontractor, field Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client personnel through defined areas, structures, buildings, rooms, equipment-support scopes, and facility boundaries.

You will collaborate with field Quality and CSA subcontractors to verify adherence to applicable inspection, testing, completion, and turnover-documentation requirements. The position will focus on confirming that permanent facilities are sufficiently complete to safely support equipment installation, system testing, startup, commissioning, occupancy, access, weather protection, and final turnover.

You will use ACC for CSA punch-list entry and tracking, condition documentation, readiness visibility, closure review, and assembly of applicable construction turnover packages.

In coordination with Project Controls and Construction, you will help provide a planned and documented approach for the turnover of civil, structural, and architectural scopes in alignment with the P6 schedule and downstream system dependencies.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and facilitate CSA walkdowns with Construction, subcontractors, Quality, Turnover, CQV, and client representatives.
Serve as the primary CSA technical resource for walkdown preparation, field verification, punch development, and turnover-package review.
Confirm that each CSA walkdown has a clearly defined building, area, room, structure, foundation, or facility boundary.
Participate with Construction and CQV in establishing logical completion and turnover boundaries that support equipment installation, system turnover, startup, and commissioning.
Read and interpret civil and grading plans, underground utility and drainage drawings, concrete and foundation drawings, structural steel drawings, architectural plans, building sections, roofing details, door and hardware schedules, finish schedules, firestopping details, and equipment-foundation drawings.
Verify roads, paving, grading, drainage, concrete foundations and slabs, structural steel, access systems, building envelopes, roofing, walls, ceilings, doors, firestopping, finishes, equipment clearances, egress, and permanent safety features against approved scope.
Review the availability and traceability of survey and as-built records, soil compaction records, concrete placement and strength records, anchor-bolt and embed records, structural bolting records, welding and NDE records, coating records, roofing and waterproofing records, and firestopping inspection records.
Identify conditions that could affect safety, access, weather-tightness, fire rating, equipment installation, system testing, startup, commissioning, or facility turnover.
Enter and track CSA punch-list items in CxAlloy using clear descriptions of the exact location, observed condition, affected scope, and required correction.
Coordinate with Construction and field Quality to resolve issues and support assignment of punch ownership and target dates.
Review submitted closure evidence and coordinate reinspection when required.
Review CSA turnover packages for completeness, organization, traceability, and alignment with the defined scope.
Coordinate CSA readiness forecasts with the P6 schedule, equipment-installation milestones, access requirements, weather-tightness needs, and downstream testing activities.
Identify temporary conditions or incomplete permanent work that could affect system turnover or construction-to-CQV handoff.
Participate in CSA readiness reviews, turnover planning, construction-completion discussions, and facility handoff activities.
Promote a positive, collaborative, and problem-solving culture among project participants.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree.
At least 5 years of civil, structural, architectural, Quality, inspection, or turnover experience, including at least 2 years supporting walkdowns, systems completion, or facility turnover.
Experience on data center, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial, power, commercial, or other major capital projects.
Ability to lead CSA walkdowns with subcontractors, Quality personnel, CQV representatives, and clients.
Ability to read and interpret civil, structural, architectural, concrete, steel, roofing, and equipment-foundation drawings.
Knowledge of CSA inspection, testing, completion, and turnover-documentation requirements and their relationship to downstream readiness.
Strong organization, issue tracking, field documentation, and communication skills.
Ability to spend continuous hours on an active construction site and remain onsite for the duration of the assignment.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Experience with CxAlloy and Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC).
Familiarity with Good Documentation Practices and P6 turnover milestone planning.
Working knowledge of ACI, AISC, AWS, ICC, NFPA, firestopping, roofing, or coating requirements.
Experience with data-center buildings, substations, equipment yards, concrete foundations, structural steel, roofing, fire-rated assemblies, and mission-critical facilities.
OSHA 30
Relevant ACI, ICC, AWS-CWI, firestop, coating, or construction-inspection certification.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has a U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $140,200.00 to $192,800.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on November 17, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

Qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered for employment

Onsite employees are expected to attend a Jacobs Workplace on a full-time basis, as required by the nature of their role.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

jobs.title: Civil Engineer
jobs.description:
Join Amgens Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like youre part of something bigger, its because you are. Our shared missionto serve patients living with serious illnessesdrives all that we do.

Since 1980, weve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the worlds toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, youll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, youll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Civil Engineer

What you will do

Lets do this. Lets change the world. In this vital role you will provide technical leadership and engineering expertise for the planning, design, renovation, and delivery of civil and structural infrastructure supporting facilities, utilities, and capital projects. This role ensures designs are safe, compliant, constructible, reliable, and aligned with operational, business, and site requirements.

The Project Engineer partners with engineering disciplines, architects, project managers, facilities teams, EHS professionals, contractors, and external design firms throughout the project lifecycle. This position requires travel to project sites and organizational locations to support project development, design reviews, field assessments, construction activities, commissioning, and stakeholder engagement.

Serve as the technical lead for civil and structural engineering requirements, design standards, specifications, and project execution.

Develop and review civil and structural design criteria, calculations, drawings, specifications, scopes of work, and engineering studies.

Support projects involving site development, grading, drainage, stormwater management, roads, parking areas, underground utilities, foundations, structural steel, concrete, and building modifications.

Evaluate existing site and structural conditions; identify constraints, risks, and required remediation or reinforcement measures.

Review engineering design packages for technical quality, code compliance, constructability, maintainability, safety, and alignment with project requirements.

Coordinate with architectural, mechanical, electrical, process, environmental, and facility engineering disciplines to ensure integrated project solutions.

Lead technical aspects of capital projects from feasibility and concept development through detailed design, construction, commissioning, and turnover.

Travel as needed to support site assessments, project meetings, design workshops, construction reviews, inspections, commissioning, and operational-readiness activities.

Provide technical support during construction, including field observations, resolution of design issues, review of contractor submittals, and evaluation of change requests.

Ensure projects comply with applicable building codes, structural standards, civil design requirements, permitting obligations, and environmental regulations.

Support the development and maintenance of civil and structural engineering standards, specifications, guidelines, and standard details.

Identify design risks, recommend practical mitigations, and support risk assessments associated with facility modifications, infrastructure reliability, and site conditions.

Support commissioning and turnover activities to confirm civil and structural systems meet intended-use and operational requirements.

Monitor industry practices, codes, standards, and emerging technologies; incorporate relevant improvements into engineering standards and project delivery practices.

Provide technical mentoring and subject matter support to project teams and less-experienced engineers.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek is a leader with these qualifications.

Basic Qualifications

Doctorate degree

OR

Masters degree and 2 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

Bachelors degree and 4 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

Associates degree and 8 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

OR

High school diploma / GED and 10 years of civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related engineering experience

Preferred Qualifications

Professional Engineer (PE) license in civil or structural engineering.

Advanced degree in civil engineering, structural engineering, or a related discipline.

Experience supporting industrial, manufacturing, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, research, or other regulated facility environments.

Experience with structural assessments, seismic evaluations, existing-building modifications, and infrastructure renewal projects.

Familiarity with stormwater management, site permitting, geotechnical engineering, and construction-phase engineering support.

Experience with relevant engineering software for structural analysis, civil design, or site-development planning.

What you can expect from us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, well support your journey every step of the way.

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

In Addition To The Base Salary, Amgen Offers a Total Rewards Plan, Based On Eligibility, Comprising Of Health And Welfare Plans For Staff And Eligible Dependents, Financial Plans With Opportunities To Save Towards Retirement Or Other Goals, Work/life Balance, And Career Development Opportunities That May Include

A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts

A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan

Stock-based long-term incentives

Award-winning time-off plans

Flexible work models where possible. Refer to the Work Location Type in the job posting to see if this applies.

Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team.

careers.amgen.com

In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

Application deadline

Amgen does not have an application deadline for this position; we will continue accepting applications until we receive a sufficient number or select a candidate for the position.

Sponsorship

Sponsorship for this role is not guaranteed.

As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease.

We provide reasonable accommodations to applicants and employees with disabilities, consistent with legal requirements. Please contact us to request accommodation.

Job Details

Job Details

Join a manufacturing team where your data expertise will help drive smarter decisions, stronger operations, and continuous improvement. In this permanent IT role, you will transform manufacturing and business data into actionable insights, build reporting solutions, and support the systems that keep production moving.

You will partner with stakeholders across production, supply chain, inventory, finance, and IT to improve data visibility, streamline reporting, and uncover opportunities to enhance performance.

Responsibilities

Develop, maintain, and optimize SQL queries, stored procedures, and data extracts to support reporting and analysis.

Design and deliver dashboards that make manufacturing KPIs, trends, and operational performance easy to understand.

Develop SSRS reports, including parameter-driven and scheduled reports, to meet business requirements.

Analyze data from Syteline ERP and related systems to support production planning, inventory management, purchasing, costing, and financial reporting.

Develop and maintain VB.NET applications and VBA automation to streamline workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve reporting efficiency.

Collaborate with business users to gather requirements and translate operational challenges into practical technical solutions.

Validate data accuracy, investigate discrepancies, and improve consistency across reports and dashboards.

Troubleshoot reporting and application issues, optimize performance, and document solutions.

Support testing, deployment, and adoption of reporting enhancements and ERP-related changes.

Qualifications

5+ years of relevant experience in data analysis, IT reporting, business intelligence, or a similar role, with experience supporting manufacturing operations.

Strong hands-on experience with SQL, including complex queries, stored procedures, and performance optimization.

Proven ability to build dashboards using business intelligence tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent platforms.

Experience developing and maintaining SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) reports or equivalent enterprise reporting solutions.

Working knowledge of Syteline ERP, also known as Infor CloudSuite Industrial, or an equivalent manufacturing ERP system.

Practical development experience with VB.NET and VBA, or equivalent programming and automation technologies.

Understanding of manufacturing processes and data, including production, inventory, supply chain, and costing.

Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills, with close attention to data quality.

Ability to communicate technical information clearly and collaborate with both technical teams and business stakeholders.

Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver reliable solutions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

A degree in information technology, computer science, data analytics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

jobs.title: Engineering Laboratory Technician, College of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics
jobs.description:
Job Overview

The Laboratory Technician I provides hands-on instructional laboratory and technical support mainly for the Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISE) and Bioengineering (BIOE) programs in CSTEM and may help with other engineering programs as needed. Working with faculty, program leads, and campus service units, the technician prepares, commissions, operates, maintains, and documents instructional equipment and computing environments; supports safe and effective laboratory demonstrations, design projects, and student use; and maintains equipment readiness.

For ISE, the role supports computer-aided design, human factors and ergonomics, discrete-event systems simulation, and capstone prototyping. For Bioengineering, it supports bioinstrumentation, physiological measurement, biomedical imaging, fluid mechanics and transport, biomechanics, bioreactor-based instruction, and medical-device design. Laboratory Technician I operates under the lead direction of the lead engineering technician, ISE/BIOE program directors and the direct supervision of the Associate Dean. The technician will receive the required instructions for lab preparations from the faculty with the approval of the respective program directors. The performance will be evaluated regularly by the Associate Dean, with input from faculty members to ensure their needs are met, and tasks are completed satisfactorily.

Position Summary

Engineering Laboratory Technician (Instructional Support Technician I)

This is a full-time, non-exempt position, which will lead toward permanent status following the successful completion of a probationary period.

For a complete list of responsibilities and required qualifications, please review the position description linked at the top of the page.

Pay, Benefits, And Work Schedule

Anticipated Hiring Salary Range: $4,184 to $4,353 per month (Steps 1-3)

CSU Classification Salary Range: $4,184 - $6,096 per month

Salary is commensurate with the background and experience of the individual selected.

This position is eligible for a broad range of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurances, retirement (CalPERS), tuition waiver, vacation and sick leave. In addition, 15 paid holidays are offered each year; 14 scheduled on specific days and a Personal Holiday that may be taken any time during the year.

A comprehensive benefits summary for this position is available online by visiting our Benefits Portal . The CSU Total Compensation Calculator demonstrates the significance of the benefits package.

This position is required to work in person on campus.

jobs.title: Clinical Lab Scientist (CLS) - Part Time Nights - Green
jobs.description:
Located on the Torrey Pines Mesa near I-5 and Genesee Avenue in La Jolla, Scripps Green Hospital has served the greater San Diego community since 1977. We provide some of the region’s best care, including several nationally ranked specialty programs.

Scripps Green Hospital is attached to Scripps Clinic Torrey Pines. Together we offer dozens of medical and surgical services, including cancer care, orthopedic surgery and organ transplantation.

This is a benefited, part time position working varied night, generally 2300-0730, at Scripps Green Hospital in Torrey Pines with rotating weekends and on call. Training will primarily be during day shifts for the first 3 or so months. Includes $5k retention incentive for eligible new hires.

Why join Scripps Health?

At Scripps Health, your ambition is empowered and your abilities are appreciated:

Nearly a quarter of our employees have been with Scripps Health for over 10 years.
Scripps is a Great Place to Work Certified company for 2026.
Scripps Health has been consistently ranked as a top employer for women, millennials, diversity, and as an overall workplace by various national publications.
Becker's Healthcare ranked Scripps Health on its 2026 list of 150 top places to work in health care.
We have transitional and professional development programs to create a learning environment that enables you to thrive in your specific field as well as in your overall career.
Our specialties have been nationally recognized for quality in areas such as cardiovascular care, oncology, orthopedics, geriatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, and gastroenterology.

Why join Scripps Green CLS Team?

Join a close-knit, highly experienced laboratory team at Scripps Green Hospital—one of our busiest transfusion medicine sites—where quality patient care is at the heart of everything we do.
Gain diverse, meaningful experience supporting complex hematology/oncology, urgent care, and rare cases within a clinic- and treatment-focused patient population.
Build your expertise in a dynamic environment where your clinical laboratory skills directly contribute to exceptional patient outcomes.

This position is eligible for up to $5k in New Hire Retention Incentives.

The Following Are Not Eligible For Hiring Incentives

Internal candidates
Rehires that left Scripps less than 3 years ago
Candidates with less than 1 year of experience

In order to remain eligible for your retention incentive the following criteria must be met:

Must remain in original hired FTE Status and Shift (if specified in offer letter)

Position Summary

We are seeking a diligent and detail-oriented Incoming Quality Control Technician to support incoming material inspection, microscopy-based evaluation, process development, quality control, and failure analysis activities. This technician will perform visual and dimensional inspections of purchased parts, materials, assemblies, and samples to verify conformance to approved drawings, specifications, procedures, and inspection plans before release for production use. · Prepare samples and inspection fixtures; enter, review, and upload inspection data, images, and supporting documentation into approved quality, laboratory, or ERP systems.
· Record inspection results, maintain inspection history files, and support material release or hold transactions according to established procedures and authorization levels.

· Communicate inspection findings to engineers, quality partners, and operations personnel.
· Maintain clear shift passdowns, laboratory notebooks, equipment logs, calibration-status awareness, and organized work areas.

· Support changing Manufacturing, R&D, and laboratory priorities while meeting quality, throughput, and turnaround expectations.

· High school diploma or equivalent required; associate degree or technical certificate in engineering technology, metrology, manufacturing, materials science, laboratory science, or a related field preferred.

· Experience reading technical drawings, specifications, tolerances, and inspection instructions.

· Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with engineering, quality, manufacturing, purchasing, and supplier-facing teams.
· Practical problem-solving skills and willingness to learn new inspection, microscopy, and metrology techniques.
· Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a collaborative team environment.
· Demonstrated reliability in meeting commitments, maintaining traceability, and protecting product quality.
· Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, initial training schedules, or overtime to cover business needs and shift gaps.

NOTE: The following are the duties performed by employees in this classification. However, employees may perform other related duties at an equivalent level. Not all duties listed are necessarily performed by each individual in the classification.

CLINICAL TRIALS: Responsible for assisting in the selection and administration of appropriate clinical research trials by reviewing studies, adhering to federal regulations and ICH Guidelines, with an emphasis on good clinical practice and clinical Safety Data Management. Administers informed consent, enrollment of participants into clinical trials.

INSTITUTIONAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB): Acts as departmental representative at Institutional Review Board’s Human Subject Committee meetings. Presents all new research projects to the committee. Modifies, renews and closes out all appropriate research projects. Reports all serious adverse events and protocol violations. Submits drug and/or device safety reports to the IRB.

REGULATORY: Organizes research team and meets as needed. Maintains current CVs and licenses for all study investigators. Updates regulatory binders for each research study. Provides central protocol and drug information to departments. Educates hospital personnel regarding protocols and screening requirements. Reports serious adverse events to study sponsor and FDA, when appropriate. Ensures compliance with all federal and state laws regarding research and confidentiality. PRESENTATION AND PUBLICATIONS: Assists investigators in the preparation of manuscripts and the design of posters and oral presentations for annual conventions, conferences and trainings, when appropriate. Performs searches through existing medical literature.

Acts as the point person for budgetary and administrative issues. When appropriate, prepares and negotiates study budget. Monitors and accounts for all study related income and expenses. Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

Our lab is based in both the UCI School of Medicine and its Department of Emergency Medicine. Our work bridges together researchers from across the U.S. as well as across University of California campuses to study traffic and transportation safety, motor vehicle driver behavior, socioecological factors that influence safe/risky driving behaviors, and related prevention policy. While our work is focused on traffic and road safety, most of our day-to-day work is focused on individual/population health, medicine, and primary as well as secondary prevention of motor vehicle crash injury.

UCI's Department of Emergency Medicine is committed to advancing clinical care, education and research to help patients with diverse emergency conditions. We offer patient-centered care, apply cutting edge skills to combat serious illness and injury. In addition, our physicians conduct innovative research aimed at preventing injury and disease.

Under the direction of the Principal Investigator, the Staff Research Associate (SRA) will be responsible for day-to-day operations of assigned data analysis for research projects and writing briefs and manuscripts related to research. The person will conduct statistical analyses on the current and future research projects, and write up the research results into manuscripts, briefs, and grant applications. To successfully address these tasks on time, the SRA must have a broad set of intelligence, be extremely diligent and task-oriented, and an efficient worker. Excellent communication and writing skills are required.

The SRA will be supervised by the Principal Investigator, with the ultimate goal of progressive independence once the SRA has demonstrated the ability to carry out the PI and project related plans.

Proficiency in hypothesis testing, including no mistakes in use of t-tests, regressions, ANOVA, mixed effects modeling, chi-square, and other common tests.
