jobs.title: Research Assistant (Medicinal Chemistry)
jobs.description:
Company Description
RiboForge is a stealth biotechnology startup focused on advancing RNA-targeted drug discovery at the cutting edge of the field. The team is dedicated to developing innovative therapeutic approaches that leverage RNA biology to address unmet medical needs. As an early-stage company, RiboForge offers opportunities to contribute directly to foundational research and platform development. Team members can expect a highly collaborative, science-driven environment that values curiosity, rigor, and creativity.

About the Role

We are seeking a motivated laboratory assistant to work on-site, part-time or full-time, with our
medicinal chemistry team. This is a great opportunity for someone with a passion for
science who is interested in pursuing a career in biotechnology or the pharmaceutical
industry. For the right candidate, there is potential to transition into a full-time position as
the company grows. The role centers on the synthesis, purification, and characterization of novel small molecules to aid hit-to-lead optimization discovery efforts. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys organic synthesis, detailed characterization work, and is eager to translate those skills into future therapeutics. 

Key Responsibilities

Multi-Step Organic Synthesis:
Execute the synthesis of novel target molecules, intermediates, and focused chemical libraries across parallel and multi-step reaction sequences (milligram to gram scale).
Purification & Isolation:
Utilize modern purification techniques, including liquid-liquid extraction, crystallization, flash chromatography (normal/reverse-phase), and preparative HPLC.
Compound Characterization:
Characterize intermediates and final compounds using analytical instrumentation, including 1D/2D NMR (1H, 13C, 19F), LC-MS, HPLC, and HRMS, ensuring high purity (>95%) for biological evaluation.
Data Interpretation & Troubleshooting:
Analyze analytical data, troubleshoot challenging synthetic routes, optimize reaction conditions, and propose alternative synthetic strategies.
Documentation & Compliance:
Maintain precise, timely laboratory notebook records, adhere to chemical hygiene plans and standard operating procedures, and handle hazardous materials safely in compliance with OSHA/EHS guidelines.

Requirements

Education:
B.S. in Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Medicinal Chemistry, or a closely related discipline.
2–4 years of laboratory experience in synthetic organic or medicinal chemistry (academic or industrial setting).
Technical Skills:

Demonstrated command of standard organic chemistry reaction mechanisms, reagent handling (including air-/moisture-sensitive reagents, inert atmospheres, and cryogenic conditions).
Hands-on proficiency in operating and interpreting data from LC-MS, NMR spectrometers, and automated chromatography systems (e.g., Biotage, Teledyne ISCO).
Working knowledge of chemical drawing and informatics software (e.g., ChemDraw, SciFinder, Reaxys).

Preferred Qualifications

Extensive synthetic experience; Prior experience in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry drug discovery environment. 
Foundational understanding of drug discovery principles, physicochemical properties (LogP/LogD, solubility, PSA), and basic in vitro ADME assays.
Familiarity with PyMOL

Compensation and Benefits

Anticipated full-time compensation is $70,000 per year, with flexibility to increase based on experience and qualifications. Part-time compensation and benefits eligibility will be discussed based on the position and schedule. Health coverage and benefits are included for full-time positions. Relocation assistance may be considered based on the candidate’s qualifications and circumstances.

How to Apply

Submit your resume, cover letter, and references to careers@riboforge.com with the subject line “Research Assistant – Medicinal Chemistry”

In your application email, include two to three sentences describing your hands-on experience with organic synthesis (academic or industrial).

Please also indicate whether you are interested in a part-time position, full-time position, or either, along with your availability. Please indicate if you are open to relocate.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer – Python Backend & Manufacturing Systems
jobs.description:
Diamond Foundry Inc. is solving the thermal limitation at the foundation of today's most exciting tech industries -- AI & cloud compute, electric-car power electronics, and 5G/6G wireless. We have managed to produce the world's first single-crystal diamond wafers and are now on a mission to put a diamond behind every chip. We are the rare unicorn that has grown fast and profitably. We received $515m in funding and are executing a multi-$B expansion plan for one of the greenest forms of tech manufacturing: converting greenhouse gas into diamond wafers using zero-emission energy.

We are looking for an experienced, communicative Senior Software Engineer to own the data pipelines, internal systems, and APIs that power our real-time manufacturing and R&D operations. What we need from you is deep, production-grade Python expertise and the ability to own a project end-to-end: partnering directly with material engineers, technicians, and hardware engineers to turn ambiguous operational challenges into working production software.

This role will be on-site 5 days a week in either our South San Francisco office or our Fremont, CA office.

Responsibilities

Own technical initiatives from inception to delivery: translate operational needs into technical roadmaps, architectural specs, and deployable code.
Architect and scale end-to-end Python backends, spanning high-throughput event pipelines, internal REST APIs, and automated data processing tools.
Interface directly with internal clients (production technicians, metrology specialists, and R&D engineers) to diagnose workflow bottlenecks and validate solutions on the floor.
Optimize database performance and schema design for high-frequency telemetry, process metrics, and traceability data.
Partner with our front-end engineers to define clean API contracts and data models for operator-facing UI’s.

Requirements

4+ years of software engineering experience with production Python as your primary language (experience with industrial protocols like MQTT, Modbus, OPC-UA, or PLCs is a strong plus).
Proven end-to-end project ownership with the ability to define roadmaps, write specs, and execute code independently (experience working in manufacturing, hardware-in-the-loop, or physical R&D environments is a plus).
Full-lifecycle Python backend expertise across REST APIs, event/data pipelines, and automation scripts (hands-on experience with FastAPI, Flask, or async processing is a plus).
Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills to run discovery directly with non-software stakeholders like scientists, technicians, and operations teams (experience scoping technical requirements directly from physical shop-floor workflows is a plus).
Strong querying skills with schema design fundamentals.

$150,000 - $175,000 a year

The position is eligible for company shares. Actual compensation may be higher or lower in the range based on various factors, including, but not limited to a candidate’s job duties, experience, and location. We will also consider higher-level candidates and salary will be adjusted accordingly.

Diamond Foundry believes in supporting our employees from the workplace to their personal and home life. We provide eligible employees with an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs, generally including health insurance, flexible spending accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and a number of programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work. Perks include employee discounts to VRAI. Our benefits begin as early as your first day of employment. Medical and vision coverage are retroactive to your start date, while dental and voluntary benefits take effect once you’ve completed your enrollment.

Diamond Foundry is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected factor under federal, state or local law.

Diamond Foundry Inc. is committed to operating in full compliance with all applicable state and federal laws. Our commitment extends to ensuring that our manufacturing and engineering departments adhere to the highest standards of legal and regulatory compliance. Additionally, these departments may have specific physical requirements to ensure the safety and efficiency of our operations. We prioritize the well-being of our employees and strive to create a work environment that promotes both legal compliance and the optimal functioning of our manufacturing and engineering processes.

Manufacturing and Engineering Departments Physical Requirements:

Use appropriate PPE and follow all safety policies, practices, and procedures.
This position will often: Sit, stand for long periods, walk, grasp, reach with hands and arms, lift below and above shoulders, bend, twist at the waist, climb, balance, stoop, squat, kneel, crawl, talk, hear, see, use fine finger manipulation, and complete repetitive motions.

jobs.title: Flatiron Research Fellow - Biomolecular Design, Center for Computational Biology
jobs.description:
Description
The Center for Computational Biology (CCB)
, of the Simons Foundation ’s Flatiron Institute
is actively seeking enthusiastic, full-time post-doctoral Flatiron Research Fellows to join its Biomolecular Design Group
. The start date is flexible, with the Fellow expected to begin no later than September 2027.  Applications will be reviewed beginning in Fall 2026 and considered on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Candidates with strong backgrounds in computational biology/biochemistry/biophysics, applied and computational mathematics, computer science/engineering, machine learning, and related fields are particularly encouraged to apply.

ABOUT THE CENTER FOR COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY:
CCB has a twofold mission: to develop the rigorous modeling tools and theory needed for understanding biological processes, and to create computational frameworks that will facilitate the analysis of the large, complex data sets being generated by quantitative experimental technologies. To accomplish this, CCB brings together experts in various biological domains (including genomics, molecular, cellular, and developmental biology) whose approaches are informed by the modern computational tools of applied mathematics, statistical inference, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), biophysics, and computer science. The goal: to enable CCB to undertake ambitious, long-term research projects that transcend conventional disciplinary boundaries and that lead to a quantitative and predictive understanding of biological phenomena; and to develop high-quality, well-tested, versatile and extensible software across its research areas.  

CCB currently comprises more than 50 scientists at career stages from Ph.Ds through senior scientists, as well as visiting scientists and guest researchers, affiliated graduate students and interns. Together, the CCB scientific staff are pioneering an approach to biology in which theory,computation, and experimentation are integrated, from problem conceptualization onwards. This approach enables CCB to tackle not only recognized, fundamental problems in biology that have so far eluded solution, but also, because of the value placed on curiosity-driven research, to find and develop new areas of biological inquiry.

ABOUT THE BIOMOLECULAR DESIGN GROUP:
The Biomolecular Design Group (BmD) develops and applies computational tools to design natural polymers and synthetic heteropolymers built from noncanonical chemical building blocks. These molecules — including heterochiral cyclic peptides and peptoid foldamers — can adopt structures inaccessible to natural proteins and perform new functions, with potential applications as therapeutics, nanomaterials, and catalysts. By designing molecules beyond the scope of natural proteins, we both test our understanding of protein folding and function and push the boundaries of computational molecular design.

BmD is also part of the Collaboration on Molecular Physics and Sampling Strategies (COMPASS), which brings together research groups across the Flatiron Institute to advance computational methods for understanding molecular motion and designing molecules with specific dynamic properties. Together, we address challenges in the accuracy and computational tractability of molecular modeling.

The successful candidate will pursue a research project that advances these goals. Potential research directions include:

Developing open-source software infrastructure to analyze macromolecular motion and design motile macromolecules.

Integrating physics-based simulation with machine learning methods.

Developing improved approximation methods, including implicit solvation and coarse-graining, to make computationally expensive calculations more tractable.

Developing molecular modeling and design methods that use current and next-generation gate-based quantum computers and quantum annealers.

Designing molecules with potential medical applications.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

Flatiron Research Fellows in CCB are individuals at the postdoctoral level with backgrounds in one or more of the following areas: applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biochemistry, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines.

Reporting to the Group Lead(s), Fellows are expected to carry out an active research program that can be independently directed and/or involve substantial collaboration with other members of CCB or the Flatiron Institute. In addition to their research, Fellows help build the rich scientific community at CCB and the Flatiron Institute by participating in seminars, colloquia, and group meetings; developing their software, mathematical and computational expertise through internal education opportunities; and sharing their knowledge through scientific publications, presentations, and/or software releases, with the financial support of the Institute. Fellows have access to the Flatiron Institute’s powerful scientific computing resources. 

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Performing theoretical and computational research

Developing, implementing and maintaining scientific software

Participating in the organization of CCB and Flatiron-wide collaborative activities including seminars, workshops and meetings

Participating in the preparation of manuscripts for publication and of presentations at scientific conferences

Assisting in student mentorship

Sharing expertise and providing training and guidance to CCB staff and visitors as needed.

Fellows will be based, and have a principal office or workspace, at the Simons Foundation’s offices in New York City.  The initial appointments for Flatiron Research Fellows are generally for two years, with the possibility of renewal for a third year, contingent on performance. FRFs may be eligible for subsidized housing within walking distance of CCB. 

The start date is flexible, with the Fellow expected to begin no later than September 2027. 
Qualifications
EDUCATION

Ph.D. in a relevant field (applied mathematics, statistics, computational biology, biochemistry, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines)

REQUIRED SKILLS & OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

Demonstrated abilities in mathematical modeling, analysis and/or scientific computation, scientific software and algorithm development, data analysis and inference, and image analysis

Ability to do original and outstanding research in computational biology, and expertise in computational methods, data analysis, software and algorithm development, modeling machine learning, and scientific simulation 

Ability to work well in an interdisciplinary environment, and to collaborate with experimentalists

Strong oral and written communication, data documentation, and presentation skills

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

The full-time annual compensation for this position is USD $95,000. In addition to competitive salaries, the Simons Foundation provides employees with an outstanding benefits package.
Application Instructions
To apply, please submit the following via the application portal:

Cover Letter, which should include a summary of applicants’ most significant contributions in graduate school

Curriculum vitae with publications list and, if relevant, links to software 

Research statement of no more than three (3) pages describing the applicant’s past important results, current and future research interests which may include both scientific topics and algorithm and software development, and potential synergies with activities at CCB

Two (2) letters of recommendation 

Applications for available positions that begin in 2027 will be reviewed beginning November 2026 and considered on a rolling basis until the positions are filled. For full consideration, application by November 30, 2026 is recommended. 

SELECTION CRITERIA

Applications will be evaluated based on: 

past research accomplishments

the proposed research program

the synergy of applicant’s expertise and research proposal topic with existing CCB staff and research programs, and potential to cross boundaries between CCB groups and/or the Flatiron Institute’s other research centers.

Any queries about the application process or about CCB should be directed to ccbjobs@flatironinstitute.org. Queries about CCB may also be directed to scientific staff at CCB. 

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Application Materials

The Flatiron Institute values authenticity, originality, and transparency throughout the application and hiring process. Applicants are expected to submit application materials that reflect their own original work, experiences, ideas, writing, and scientific or professional judgment. The use of AI-based tools may be appropriate for limited purposes during the hiring process, such as editing, formatting, or code review. However, application materials, including research statements, cover letters, personal statements, and other writing samples, should not be substantially authored or generated by AI systems.

Applicants are encouraged to disclose any significant or material use of AI tools in the preparation of their application materials or throughout the hiring process. The Flatiron Institute does not use AI-based tools to screen applicants.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Our Commitment to Expanding Pathways to Science & Opportunities for All:

Many of the greatest ideas and discoveries come from a diverse mix of minds, backgrounds, and experiences. The Simons Foundation is committed to advancing basic science and mathematics to benefit humankind and expand our collective understanding of our world. As part of our mission, we support partners, programs, and initiatives that seek to broaden the scientific community and open pathways to science and mathematics careers.

One of the first human genetics departments in the country, the Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics at Indiana University (IU) School of Medicine has a rich history of training geneticists and genetic counselors and providing genetic consultation and counseling services. jobs.description:
The Position

Why Genentech

We advance science so that we all have more time with the people we love.

We seek a highly motivated candidate for a joint postdoctoral fellowship position in the laboratories of Dr. Xiaosai Yao in the Computational Sciences Center of Excellence and Dr. Frederic de Sauvage in the Department of Research Oncology at Genentech. The Yao lab develops and applies computational tools to understand chromatin changes in cancer biology and drug response. The de Sauvage Lab explores mechanisms by which cancer signaling pathways drive tumor growth, metastasis and resistance to treatment with targeted therapies. The Genentech scientific community and postdoctoral program provide access to generous state-of-the-art resources and training opportunities.

The Opportunity:

This hybrid computational and wet lab based postdoctoral position will investigate the interactions between oncogenic pathways and lineage factors, specifically how the underlying chromatin landscape in tissues affects the oncogenic properties of the same driver mutations in different tissues and cells of origin. Mechanisms derived from in vivo cancer models will be used to interpret patient responses to cancer therapeutics across various indications.

Utilize in vivo cancer models to understand changes in the chromatin after the acquisition of driver mutations and/or treatment with cancer therapeutics.
Analyze single cell and bulk omics datasets to form hypotheses and derive biological insights.
Learn best practices in data analysis and potentially software development
Collaborate effectively within an interdisciplinary team of quantitative, experimental, and clinical scientists.
Present complex results clearly and concisely to diverse audiences.

Who You Are:

Ph.D. in Cancer Biology, Computational Biology or related field
Experience with in vivo cancer models (e.g. GEMM, xenograft) and in vitro cancer assays.
Experience with bulk and/or single-cell omics data analysis (e.g. bulk RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq and single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC-seq)
Proficiency in R or Python is required
Demonstrated ability to drive at least one key research project, as evidenced by first-author publications in high-impact journals
Strong communication skills and ability to work in a team environment.

Scientist to leverage AI to support the automation, optimization, and integration of manual computational procedures used in scientific research, engineering, and laboratory operations. This position will work within an interdisciplinary research and development environment and collaborate with scientists, engineers, technicians, software developers, and industrial partners. jobs.description:
Role Title:
German AI Evaluator (Remote)
Role Type
: Full-time
Location

Role Overview:

As an AI Quality Analyst, you will evaluate a new personalization feature for Gemini. You will assess how well the model uses information from your past Gemini conversations, Gmail, Google Search, and YouTube activity to make responses more relevant and helpful. This role requires a unique blend of creativity and analytical rigor. You will actively design prompts from the perspective of your own personal experiences. You will then use your analytical skills to assess the quality of the model's personalized responses, evaluating dimensions like Grounding, Integration, and Helpfulness.

Key Qualifications

1. German Proficiency: Ability to read and write in German with a high degree of comp, as German is the focus language for this project.
2. Personal Account Usage: Willingness to use your primary personal Google account (not a testing account) and enable personal data sources for a genuine assessment.
3. Schedule Flexibility: Full-time availability in your local time zone is required. We are staffing a global, 24-hour operations team.
4. Exceptional Analytical Thinking: Demonstrate ability to evaluate nuanced and ambiguous AI responses, specifically assessing personalization quality.
5. Creative Prompt Engineering: Experience in designing creative, multi-turn starting prompts based on personal context to thoroughly test the model's capabilities.
6. Strong Evaluation Acumen: Understanding of personalization concepts, including the ability to identify incorrect personalization, poor inferences, and forced connections.
7. Meticulous Attention to Detail: The ability to review Side-by-Side (SxS) model responses and spot subtle differences in naturalness and overnarrating.
8. Excellent Written Communication: Superior ability to write clear, concise, and structured rationales for model rankings, explicitly referencing specific turn numbers.
9. Feedback: Ability to provide constructive feedback and detailed annotations.
10. Communication: Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
11. Independence: Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote setting.
12. Technical Setup: Desktop/Laptop set up with a good internet connection.

Description:

1. In this role, you will be part of a dynamic team focused on evaluating the quality of personalized AI interactions. Your day-to-day work will involve:
2. Designing and executing multi-turn conversational prompts (typically 1-5 turns) that require the AI to utilize your personal information and experiences.
3. Evaluating model responses based on your intent from the starting prompt, checking if the personalization was appropriately applied.
4. Analyzing responses for Grounding issues, ensuring claims about you are supported by evidence and not flawed inferences or hallucinations.
5. Assessing Integration quality to ensure personal data is woven naturally into the response without robotic "overnarrating".
6. Rigorously evaluating and stack-ranking two model responses side-by-side (SxS) to determine which is overall more helpful, easy to use, and enjoyable.
7. Writing clear, defensible rationales for your comparisons, explicitly referencing where issues or positive aspects occurred in the conversation.

Education & Experience

Clinical Laboratory Science (CLS) - Lecturer

Overview of clinical biochemistry and renal function. Proper specimen collection, instrumentation, quality assurance, physical and chemical analyses of samples. Case histories and laboratory practice emphasize correlation of laboratory findings and clinical conditions.

Identification of blood cells, pathophysiology, hemostasis mechanisms, and disease states of hematological and hemostasis conditions. Theory and application of hematology procedures with emphasis on detection of abnormalities. Interpretation of clinical cases.

including Parasitology, Mycology and Molecular diagnostics): The principles of diagnostic microbiology that apply to bacteria, fungi, parasites and viruses, including phenotypic and genotypic detection, identification and susceptibility testing using slide and culture evaluation. Correlation of principles with case studies. Molecular diagnostic theory and clinical practice.

Theory and practice of serology and blood banking, including immune system, autoimmune diseases, red blood cell antigens, compatibility testing, transfusion reactions, current serological methodologies such as ELISA and immunofluorescence. Correlation of laboratory findings with pathophysiology. Interpretation of case studies

: Clinical training in a clinical laboratory required for licensure in California and certification by ASCP. Evaluation of this clinical course includes document tracking and student guidance throughout the course.

jobs.title: Account Executive - Healthcare & Life Sciences
jobs.description:
Outset invented a better way to do research: AI-powered user interviews.

Global brands like Hubspot, Microsoft, Uber and Nestle use Outset to achieve deeper, qualitative insights about their users at unprecedented speed and scale.

The research industry is massive (>$140B and growing) and ripe for disruption. Incumbents are outdated, slow, and burdened by high-cost services. That's our opportunity.

Outset is backed by top Silicon Valley investors and raised a $30M Series B in December 2025—less than six months after our Series A—led by Radical Ventures with participation from M12 (Microsoft’s venture arm), 8VC, Y Combinator, and Adverb Ventures.

The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people.

We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises.

We’re looking for an Account Executive, Healthcare & Life Sciences
to lead Outset’s growth with health plans and payer organizations.

This is a quota-carrying individual contributor role reporting to the VP of Sales
, responsible for selling Outset into healthcare organizations and growing those accounts over time. You’ll own the full sales cycle—from prospecting and pipeline development through closing and expansion—across a named set of accounts, working with both net new logos and existing customers
.

Your primary buyers are Market Research and Insights & Analytics teams
at pharmaceutical, biotech, and life sciences companies, as well as health insurers. Life sciences companies need to understand patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals across the product lifecycle, from early concept and messaging work through launch and brand tracking. Health insurers need to understand why members choose, stay, and leave, and how to improve the experience scores that drive ratings and revenue. Outset gives both groups that depth at a speed and scale traditional research can’t match. Your job is to make Outset the standard for how these teams understand their customers, landing with one brand, therapeutic area, or line of business and expanding across the organization. There’s also a significant opportunity to expand into UX Research, Product, CX, and Patient and Member Experience teams.

You’ll partner closely with Marketing, Product, Security, and Customer Success teams, and you’ll bring a deep understanding of how life sciences companies and health insurers operate, govern patient, HCP, and member data, and buy.

Responsibilities

Own the full sales cycle for a named set of healthcare and life sciences accounts, from prospecting to close.
Land new logos and grow existing customers across brands, therapeutic areas, and markets in life sciences, and across lines of business at health insurers (Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, commercial, and individual).
Build trusted relationships with Market Research and Insights & Analytics leaders as your primary buyers, and expand into UX Research, Product, CX, and Patient and Member Experience teams within each account.
Lead discovery and demos that connect Outset to healthcare research workflows. In life sciences, that means HCP and patient research, patient journey mapping, concept and message testing, launch readiness, and brand tracking. At insurers, it means member research, plan selection and switching, retention, benefit design, and enrollment marketing. For UX, Product, and CX teams, it means digital and experience research.
Build account plans that map brands, therapeutic areas, lines of business, regions, buying centers, research budgets, and whitespace across each account.
Navigate complex enterprise sales processes, including HIPAA, GDPR, PHI handling, adverse event reporting, HCP compliance, information security, and vendor risk reviews, in partnership with our Security and Legal teams.
Maintain accurate forecasting and pipeline visibility in Salesforce.
Partner with Marketing and outbound teams to build targeted healthcare and life sciences plays (events, content, and references that resonate with each segment).
Collaborate with Customer Success and Research teams to drive adoption and identify expansion opportunities post-sale.
Bring healthcare and life sciences market feedback back to Product and GTM, and become Outset’s go-to expert on the vertical.

Qualifications

5+ years of quota-carrying B2B SaaS sales experience, with a strong track record of exceeding quota.
Demonstrated experience and expertise selling into and growing Healthcare accounts—you’ve owned commercial relationships with these customers and know how they buy.
An established network across Market Research and Insights & Analytics leadership at health firms; relationships with UX Research, Product, or CX leaders are a plus.
Proven ability to run full-cycle enterprise sales, including prospecting, managing complex multi-stakeholder deals, and closing new business.
A track record of growing existing accounts through expansion and cross-sell across lines of business.
Working knowledge of healthcare and life sciences research, from HCP and patient research in pharma to member experience and plan ratings at insurers, and the privacy and compliance requirements (HIPAA, adverse event reporting) that govern it.
Exceptional communication, executive presence, and relationship-building skills.
Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced startup environment.
Willingness to travel up to 40% for customer meetings and industry events.
Bonus: experience selling research, CX, analytics, or AI solutions into healthcare.

Compensation Range: $200K - $300K

jobs.description:
Meta is seeking a lead CAD and integration engineer to shape the methodology and physical implementation infrastructure for our custom silicon programs. Working at the intersection of circuit design, digital implementation, and physical verification, you will define and own the CAD flows that take designs from RTL and schematic intent through to foundry-ready GDS deliverables. You will establish best practices across synthesis, place-and-route, analog mixed-signal integration, and physical signoff, while building automation frameworks and integrating AI-assisted design tools to accelerate engineering velocity across the silicon team.

CAD and Integration Engineer, Silicon Responsibilities:

Define and own end-to-end digital implementation methodology including RTL-to-GDS flows, synthesis, place-and-route, DFT insertion, and multi-corner physical signoff
Lead analog mixed-signal physical integration strategy, establishing constraint authoring, floorplanning guidelines, and interface protocols between custom and digital domains
Develop and maintain CAD automation infrastructure using Python, SKILL, and Tcl to reduce manual effort across implementation, tapeout, and regression workflows
Integrate AI and LLM-assisted coding tools into CAD methodology to improve design automation productivity across the silicon engineering organization
Drive physical signoff convergence across timing, power, noise, and design rule checks to produce foundry-ready deliverables on schedule
Establish 3D integration and heterogeneous packaging flows including die-to-die interface planning, cross-die timing closure, and bump/interposer constraint management
Partner with foundry contacts on PDK qualification, design rule interpretation, and process design kit updates for leading-edge technology nodes
Define low-power implementation methodology including multi-voltage domain integration, UPF-based power intent authoring, and power analysis signoff
Provide technical direction to other engineers on CAD methodology decisions, flow architecture, and implementation best practices across multiple concurrent tapeout programs
Communicate implementation status, methodology decisions, and risk assessments to circuit designers, layout engineers, and program leadership

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
8+ years of industry experience in VLSI CAD, physical implementation, or silicon design methodology across multiple technology nodes and tapeouts
Expertise in full RTL-to-GDS digital implementation flows including synthesis, place-and-route, DFT, and multi-corner physical signoff using industry-standard EDA tools
Experience with analog mixed-signal physical integration including constraint authoring, floorplan coordination, and interface management between custom and digital design domains
Proficiency in scripting and automation using Python, SKILL, Tcl, or equivalent languages to build and maintain CAD flow infrastructure
Experience communicating methodology decisions, tapeout risk, and implementation status to cross-functional partners including circuit designers, layout engineers, and foundry contacts

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with 3D stacking or advanced packaging flows including die-to-die interface planning, cross-die timing analysis, and heterogeneous integration methodology
Experience with PDK qualification and design rule development in direct collaboration with foundry partners on leading-edge process nodes
Background in low-power design methodology including UPF-based power intent, multi-voltage domain integration, and power signoff for mobile or wearable silicon applications
Familiarity with AI-assisted design tools or LLM-based coding assistants applied to CAD automation or implementation flow development

jobs.description:
Visual Designer, AI Trainer (Remote, Flexible Hours)

100% Remote | Work When You Want | Part-Time or Full-Time | Freelance Contract | $40 to $125 per hour

Fully remote. Work when you want. Get paid for what you already know. Applying takes just a few minutes with your resume.

We are partnering with DataAnnotation to find experienced visual designers to work as remote AI trainers and evaluate how frontier AI models handle real design work: interfaces, layouts, typography and visual systems. You bring the eye you have built over a career of shipping design. You design a realistic brief from your own practice, such as a landing page, a pitch deck, a data visualization, a poster or a motion piece, run it through frontier AI design tools and judge what comes back against a professional standard. This is project-based, 100% remote work you do from home on your own schedule, alongside a current job, including evenings and weekends.

Already have a DataAnnotation account?
This opportunity runs through our partnership with DataAnnotation. If you have already taken a DataAnnotation starter assessment, you are not eligible to apply through this posting. If you created an account but never took the assessment, you can still apply.

What the Work Involves

Design challenging, realistic design briefs drawn from your own professional work
Run those briefs through frontier AI design tools and evaluate the output against the standard you would hold a colleague to
Compare two model versions on the same prompts and assets, decide which performed better and where each fell short
Critique model-generated interfaces, mockups, layouts, slides, infographics, illustrations and motion
Flag concrete failures with evidence: alignment and spacing, content overflow and cutoff, typography, visual hierarchy, SVG and illustration quality, ignored assets, off-brief interpretation

Areas of Expertise

The work spans these areas; depth in at least one is what matters:
UI/UX, web and product design
Office and presentation design
Graphic design and branding
Technical illustration and data visualization
Motion and new media

Who This Is For

Professional background in UI/UX design, web design, product design or graphic design
Strong understanding of visual hierarchy, layout, typography, interaction design and user flow
Able to articulate why a design fails, not only that it does
Comfortable with AI design tools, or able to pick them up quickly
A current, in-progress or completed bachelor's degree is preferred but not required
Fluent written English at a native or bilingual level
Comfortable working independently, following detailed written instructions and incorporating feedback

Pay, Hours and Location

Pay:
$40 to $125 per hour, depending on project and expertise. Bonus rates are available on some projects. Paid via PayPal on a regular schedule. You are paid for every step you complete
Hours:
Work whenever it suits you, including evenings and weekends. Minimum 10 hours per week with no maximum; full-time hours are available. Choose which projects you work on and when
Location:
100% remote, work from home. Must be based in the United States, Canada, or the UK
Tools:
Access to the AI models you will evaluate is provided; no personal subscription needed

How to Apply

Apply here with your resume. It takes just a few minutes, and there are no interviews
We review your background against the role
If it's a fit, we send you a link to take DataAnnotation's skills assessment. It's unpaid, takes about 1 to 2+ hours and tests domain judgment and careful reading. The assessment must be entirely your own work; AI-assisted submissions are detected and rejected

If you pass, you complete onboarding and a short training project, then propose and build tasks from your own professional experience, with expert review and written feedback at each stage

Job Description

Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a well-qualified Postdoctoral Research Associate in chemical, mechanical, or agricultural engineering, materials science, chemistry, or related fields for the Bioenergy Feedstock Technologies Department. Our team works a 9x80 schedule located out of the Energy Systems Laboratory in Idaho Falls with every other Friday off.

The postdoc will provide hands-on experimental support across closely related efforts, such as:

Investigating mechanically, thermally, and chemically assisted preprocessing of crops at a range of intensities, and quantifying the effects on size-reduction energy, particle size and shape, ash and inorganic content, and composition.
Studying the drying, heating, and carbonization behavior of biomass and blended feedstocks, including how moisture removal, heat-up dynamics, and mass loss govern the formation and properties of chars.

The candidate will work alongside staff engineers and scientists in a multi-laboratory research environment, with exposure to pilot-scale preprocessing equipment. The role also offers opportunities to develop independent research ideas and gain experience in proposal development and funding pursuit.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a laboratory and light-industrial setting, is organized and careful with data and sample tracking, and communicates effectively. Candidates should have hands-on experience with thermal processing, wet-chemistry sample preparation, and/or standard analytical characterization methods.

The candidate is expected to be a strong asset to our interdisciplinary R&D team and work effectively both alone and as a team member. The candidate must be self-motivated but also take direction from other team members and peers.

The position entails writing scientific manuscripts for journal publication, and presentation of research results at national and international conferences and meetings.

Required

PhD in chemical, mechanical, agricultural, or materials engineering, chemistry, or comparable disciplines.
PhD requirements must be completed by commencement of appointment and within the previous 5 years.
Demonstrated oral and published written communication skills in English

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

Hands-on experience with thermochemical processing (e.g., torrefaction, pyrolysis, hydrothermal carbonization, biochar production) of biomass or other waste feedstocks, including operation of bench-scale furnaces, tube or batch reactors, or thermogravimetric systems is preferred.
Experience with chemical pretreatment or leaching of solid materials (e.g., alkaline/caustic, acid, or water washing) and the associated solid-liquid separation, rinsing, filtration, and drying steps.
Familiarity with drying and heat-transfer behavior of porous or granular solids, including moisture determination and interpreting heating and mass-loss curves.
Familiarity with carbon-based materials such as biochar and graphite.
Experience with mechanical processing and physical characterization of particulate materials: milling or grinding, sieving and size fractionation, particle size and shape analysis, bulk density, and moisture content.
Experience with design of experiments, careful laboratory record-keeping, and basic data analysis, statistics, and visualization (Excel, Python, MATLAB, or similar)

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, bend, and work in an office and laboratory environment. The job requires hand/finger dexterity to keyboard or type, handle materials, manipulate tools, and reach with hands and arms. The job requires operation of job-related equipment. jobs.title: NGS Laboratory Technician I (Entry-Level)
jobs.description:
NGS Laboratory Technician I (Entry-Level)

Location:
San Diego, CA (on-site, Sorrento Valley)
Type:
Full-time, hourly (non-exempt)
Starting Pay:
$26.44 to $31.25 per hour, based on experience

Company description
AUGenomics is a women-owned next-generation sequencing laboratory based in San Diego. Beginning in 2023, we provide sequencing services and custom method development for academic, biotech, government, conservation and agricultural partners, with a focus on complex, tailored projects. We are deeply client-centric. We work as true partners to the researchers we support, staying in close contact throughout every project, troubleshooting alongside them, and treating their goals as our own. 
Job description
We are seeking a Laboratory Technician to lead a recurring high-volume DNA and RNA processing for agriculture and animal health, from weekly sample intake, extraction, library preparation, and Next Generation sequencing, with full responsibility for sample integrity and traceability. As an early member of a growing company, you will see directly how your work shapes the business and will have clear opportunities to expand your scope over time. Because this role works directly with our clients, including face-to-face, we are looking for someone who takes initiative and ownership of their projects as if they were their own, provides thoughtful and responsive customer service, genuinely cares about our clients and their research, and represents AUGenomics with professionalism, class and authenticity.
We are looking for a self-directed team player who takes pride in their work and brings strong attention to detail to every sample. The ideal candidate contributes to a positive, collaborative lab culture and is eager to learn across many areas, from bench work and sample tracking to SOP development. 
We are committed to protected time off and sustainable workloads, because balance and the prevention of burnout are central to how we operate. If you are excited by the opportunity to grow with a small, founder-led company, we encourage you to apply.
What you'll do
Sample intake:
receive weekly kit shipments, check them against tracking, inspect samples, and log every one with metadata. Flag anything missing, damaged or mislabeled the same day.
Batching and tracking:
organize samples into prep batches and keep our sample log and kit tracking sheets accurate and current. Every sample needs a clean chain of custody from box to data.
DNA extraction:
extract genomic DNA or RNA from complex environmental matrices, following our SOPs closely and consistently across high sample volumes.
Quality control:
measure DNA and/or RNA concentration and integrity (fluorometric quantification, DIN/RIN), record results, and make or escalate pass/fail calls.
Library preparation:
prepare NGS libraries, including adjusting steps like fragmentation based on sample QC, and hand off pooled libraries for sequencing.
Special handling and banking:
carry out client requests such as holding, freezing for RNA, or shipping backup samples to collaborators, and keep the banked-sample record up to date.
Lab upkeep:
manage reagent and consumable inventory for the program, maintain equipment, and keep the bench audit-ready.
Improve the process:
help refine SOPs, spot bottlenecks, and support new method work for this program (for example, viability testing and long-read sequencing).

What we're looking for
Bachelor's degree in biology, microbiology, molecular biology, biochemistry or a related field, or equivalent hands-on lab experience
Experience with core molecular techniques: pipetting, DNA extraction, PCR, and DNA quantification
Comfortable with repetitive, high-volume bench work without letting quality slip
Organized and detail-oriented.
Comfortable in Google Sheets or Excel, and willing to learn and help improve our Notion-based sample tracking and project portal systems
Comfort working with databases and structured data.
Clear communicator who flags problems early
Able to stand for extended periods and lift boxes up to 35 lbs

Nice to have
NGS library prep experience (Illumina, Element AVITI or similar)
Experience with environmental, soil, fecal or agricultural samples
Liquid handling robots or other automation
Work in a regulated or quality-focused lab (CLIA, GLP, ISO)
Programming or computer science experience (for example Python, R, SQL or scripting), and an interest in automating lab and data workflows

Benefits
Pay:
$26.44 to $31.25 per hour, based on experience, with a review at 6 months
Paid time off:
15 days PTO per year (with an additional 5 days Sick Leave). When you're out, you're out. No emails expected.
Paid holidays:
18 company holidays in 2026
Retirement:
401(k) with Roth option and a company match of up to 3.5% of salary (100% of the first 1% you contribute, plus 50% of the next 5%). Eligible after 3 months.
Training and growth:
hands-on training in NGS sample prep, library prep and lab operations, with a written growth plan and a clear path toward a Research Associate role
Location:
a lab in Sorrento Valley, San Diego, close to the biotech community

How to apply
To apply, email your resume to info@augenomics.com with "Laboratory Technician Application" in the subject line. Please include written responses to the following questions, a short paragraph each:
1. Tell us about a specific moment, class, project or experience that made you want to work in a lab. What happened, and why did it stay with you?
2. Where do you want your career to be in three to five years? Describe one concrete step you have already taken toward that goal.
3. Tell us about any specifics you’ve learned through education and any lab, technical or work experience that you believe have prepared you for this role.
4. Describe a previous lab or job you especially enjoyed. What made it a great experience, and what role did you play on that team?
Applications without responses to these questions will not be considered. We read every application thoughtfully and will reach out to candidates selected for an interview.

AUGenomics is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background, and we don't believe a traditional resume is the only path into science. We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in line with the California Fair Chance Act.

Develop complex analysis datasets, specifications, and summary outputs (tables, listings, figures, and graphs) for inclusion in clinical study reports, regulatory submissions, and internal presentations.
Create, modify, and maintain SAS programs that meet regulatory and company standards to ensure efficient programming, reporting, review, and traceability.

OR
Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a related field with 6+ years of relevant statistical programming experience
Demonstrated experience performing statistical programming in a clinical trials environment (pharmaceutical and/or medical device).

Required Technical Skills

Strong hands‑on experience with SAS programming for clinical trial data including SAS Base, SAS/STAT, and SAS Macros.
Proven experience developing and validating:
Analysis datasets
Tables, listings, and figures

High attention to detail and commitment to data quality.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to collaborate effectively with cross‑functional stakeholders, including statisticians and data managers.
Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast‑paced project environment.

Nice‑to‑Have Skills

Prior participation in regulatory submissions or submission‑related deliverables.
Experience reviewing or validating programming deliverables from CROs or vendors.
Development of SAS macros or tools that improve programming efficiency.
Ability to program in other statistical languages such as R or Python.

Additional Information

This role is an individual contributor contract position and does not include formal people‑management responsibilities.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Staff Data Engineer, Applied Data Science III based in the United States.

The Staff Data Engineer will support the development of advanced data engineering and applied data science solutions for clients across the utility and energy sectors. This hands-on role combines data pipeline development, data architecture, statistical modeling, and machine learning to turn complex utility data into actionable intelligence. You will work with diverse datasets, including smart meter readings, grid operations, geographic information systems, and customer information. Collaborating with client teams and senior technical experts, you will design reliable data workflows and contribute to scalable analytical solutions. Your work will help utilities improve forecasting, operational insights, and data-driven decision-making. This is an opportunity to contribute to modernizing energy infrastructure and building a more resilient, efficient, and sustainable power grid.

Accountabilities

You will deliver technical workstreams across data engineering, architecture, and applied data science, translating client requirements into reliable data solutions and analytical models while ensuring quality, scalability, and clear technical communication.

Explore and assess utility datasets, including advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) interval data, SCADA, GIS, asset information, customer programs, and billing records.
Design, develop, test, and maintain repeatable ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest, transform, reconcile, and deliver data from databases, files, APIs, and other approved sources.
Build reusable Python and SQL components for data cleansing, standardization, aggregation, validation, and feature preparation.
Profile source data and implement automated quality checks covering completeness, validity, consistency, uniqueness, and freshness.
Develop record-matching and entity-resolution logic to reconcile customer, asset, device, program, and operational records.
Troubleshoot pipeline failures, data inconsistencies, and performance issues, documenting findings and corrective actions.
Translate business, analytical, and operational requirements into documented data architecture and integration designs.
Develop conceptual, logical, and physical data models, entity relationship diagrams, schemas, data dictionaries, and source-to-target mappings.
Design data flows connecting source systems, staging and storage layers, analytical datasets, models, and downstream applications.
Evaluate and document architectural trade-offs involving relational databases, warehouses, lakehouses, batch processing, APIs, scalability, performance, maintainability, and cost.
Incorporate client requirements for data ownership, access controls, sensitive information, retention, lineage, and auditability into solution designs.
Develop and validate forecasting models, classification approaches, anomaly detection, clustering methods, and prioritization models using utility datasets.
Address modeling challenges such as overfitting, class imbalance, sampling bias, and time-dependent validation.
Monitor model performance and support documented recalibration, retraining, and ongoing model updates.
Connect analytical models to reliable data pipelines and reproducible datasets, coordinating with client deployment teams where appropriate.
Clearly communicate model assumptions, uncertainty, limitations, and the distinction between observed, inferred, and predicted results.
Participate in requirements workshops, technical interviews, architecture reviews, and client working sessions.
Prepare technical reports, process maps, architecture documentation, and analytical presentations.
Deliver assigned work within agreed scope, schedules, budgets, and quality expectations.
Identify and escalate data-access constraints, technical dependencies, methodological limitations, and delivery risks.
Contribute to peer reviews, reusable technical methods, and guidance for less-experienced colleagues.
Use AI-assisted development tools responsibly, validating generated outputs and protecting confidential client information.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines practical data engineering expertise with applied statistical and machine learning experience, a solid understanding of utility-sector data, and the ability to communicate technical solutions effectively to diverse stakeholders.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a closely related quantitative discipline.
4–5 years of relevant professional experience, including experience in the utility sector, with hands-on contributions to data engineering, applied data science, and data architecture or integration design.
Demonstrated experience building and maintaining repeatable data pipelines and integrations beyond one-time data preparation or exploratory notebooks.
Experience designing data models, schemas, relationships, and source-to-target mappings, with the ability to explain architectural decisions.
Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, including maintainable programming, complex queries, data transformation, and troubleshooting.
Experience with pipeline testing, scheduling or orchestration, logging, data-quality validation, and failure investigation.
Practical experience with at least one cloud or distributed-data platform, such as Databricks, Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.
Strong understanding of probability, sampling, statistical inference, regression, confidence and prediction intervals, and uncertainty.
Experience developing and evaluating statistical or machine learning models using appropriate validation methods and interpretation techniques.
Familiarity with Git, code reviews, software testing, technical documentation, and reproducible analytical workflows.
Ability to explain technical designs, analytical findings, assumptions, and limitations to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Databricks, Spark/PySpark, or comparable distributed-data technologies.
Knowledge of dimensional modeling, data warehouse or lakehouse architecture, metadata management, or data catalogs.
Experience with workflow orchestration, CI/CD, model versioning, experiment tracking, or model monitoring.
Experience with time-series or probabilistic forecasting, Bayesian methods, simulation, or optimization.
Familiarity with machine learning frameworks and tools such as XGBoost, LightGBM, PyMC, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.
Experience working with utility datasets, distributed energy resource (DER) registries, load forecasting, sensor analytics, or engineering automation.
Master's degree in a relevant quantitative or technical discipline.

ABOUT OLIVO SCIENCES

Olivo Sciences is a precision medicine company focused on helping patients with brain disorders live longer, healthier lives by bringing AI-driven precision to therapeutic development and personalized care.

Today, valuable healthcare data is fragmented across hospitals, clinics, laboratories, and research institutions, making it difficult for researchers and biopharma companies to access and use effectively.

Olivo is solving this problem by building a large-scale multimodal data library focused on neurology, neuro-oncology, psychiatry, and neurosurgery. Its platform brings together clinical, imaging, molecular, and other healthcare data and uses AI to help improve drug discovery, clinical trial design, patient enrollment, and real-world evidence generation.

Olivo has already established relationships with leading healthcare and research organizations and is building a growing network of hospital, clinic, laboratory, and research partners.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Olivo Sciences is seeking accomplished life sciences executives to join its Strategic Advisory Board and help guide the company’s work across neuroscience and clinical trials.

This role is designed for leaders who understand how therapies move from research through clinical development and commercialization. Advisory Board Members will provide strategic guidance as Olivo expands its multimodal data platform, clinical research capabilities, biopharma partnerships, and AI tools for trial design and patient enrollment.

We are particularly interested in executives with experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, CRO, clinical operations, business development, research partnerships, or commercialization.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Provide strategic guidance to Olivo's leadership team on life sciences growth and clinical development
• Advise on neuroscience clinical trials, development strategy, and evidence generation
• Help shape relationships with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, CRO, and research organizations
• Provide perspective on clinical operations, commercialization, partnerships, and business development
• Advise on the application of real-world data, multimodal data, and AI to clinical trials
• Make introductions to relevant life sciences and clinical research leaders where appropriate
• Participate in periodic Advisory Board meetings and strategic discussions

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Senior leadership experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, CRO, or other life sciences organizations
• Experience in clinical development, clinical operations, R&D, medical affairs, commercialization, or business development
• Strong understanding of clinical trials and the life sciences development ecosystem
• Experience in neuroscience, precision medicine, real-world data, biomarkers, or AI-enabled research is highly valuable
• Established professional network across life sciences, clinical research, healthcare, or investment communities

WHY JOIN OLIVO SCIENCES

Life sciences companies need better data and better tools to make clinical development faster, more precise, and less risky. Olivo is building a neuroscience-focused multimodal data platform designed to improve trial design, patient identification, and evidence generation across the drug development lifecycle.

Advisory Board Members can help shape how Olivo works with life sciences companies to improve clinical trials and advance more effective therapies for brain disorders.

About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About The Role

Gusto is looking for an experienced, hands-on people manager to lead a data science and analytics team supporting Growth product initiatives. This role sits at the heart of how we use data — and increasingly AI — to understand, shape, and scale Gusto's products. You’ll both manage a team of data scientists and analysts as well as personally get in-the-weeds to work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, Sales, and Finance to deliver insights and frameworks that inform strategy, optimize user experiences, and accelerate business growth.

We're looking for a leader who can balance strategic influence with hands-on craft — someone who can guide senior Gusto leaders through data and AI strategy, coach data scientists on impactful problem solving, and dive in to drive forward statistically rigorous analyses when needed.

Here’s What You’ll Do Day-to-day

Lead and develop a team of data scientists – hire, empower, and coach team members; set a high bar for analytical quality and career growth.
Shape product and business strategy through data – partner with Product and cross-functional leaders to identify opportunities, prioritize investments, and influence long-term product roadmaps.
Develop and scale measurement frameworks – define key metrics, design monitoring systems, and ensure product initiatives — including AI-powered features — are rigorously tracked and evaluated.
Support experimentation and decision-making – support inferential analyses and experimentation (e.g., A/B tests, segmentation, funnel analysis), including designing evaluations for AI and ML-driven systems, ensuring findings are actionable and aligned to strategic goals.
Partner on AI-powered product development – collaborate with ML Engineering and Product to bring intelligent features to life (personalization, predictions, intelligent automation), ensuring they're grounded in customer insight and measured for real-world impact.
Balance strategic and hands-on impact – dive deep into data, review and refine analyses, and ensure insights are both technically sound and business-relevant.
Influence senior leadership – communicate insights and recommendations clearly, framing trade-offs and shaping executive decision-making.

Here’s What We're Looking For

10+ years of experience in data science or related fields, with at least 4 years managing and scaling high-performing data science teams.
Deep expertise in product analytics – experience with user acquisition, activation, retention, engagement, or expansion in SaaS or product-led environments.
Technical fluency – advanced coding skills, strong statistical reasoning, and familiarity with experimentation frameworks; ability to mentor data scientists on best practices.
AI product intuition – experience working at the intersection of data science and AI product development; comfort reasoning about model behavior, evaluation design, and the tradeoffs of deploying AI in customer-facing contexts.
Strategic and business acumen – demonstrated ability to connect insights to product and business goals, and to influence roadmaps through data.
Executive communication skills – proven experience presenting insights to senior stakeholders, turning complex data into clear and actionable recommendations.
Cross-functional collaboration – history of working closely with Product, Engineering, and go-to-market teams to drive decisions and deliver impact.
Hands-on experience with ML applications in product contexts (e.g., personalization, churn prediction, customer segmentation, or LLM-powered features) is strongly preferred.
Familiarity with multi-product SaaS ecosystems and customer lifecycle analytics is desirable.

Our cash compensation amount for this role is targeted at and $185,000 - $217,000 in Denver, and $218,000 - $255,000 in San Francisco and New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence:
We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. jobs.title: Research Associate I, Process Development
jobs.description:
BlueRock Therapeutics, a wholly-owned and independently operated subsidiary of Bayer AG, is a leading engineered cell therapy company pioneering a new generation of cellular medicines. Utilizing our proprietary CELL+GENE™ platform, we direct cellular differentiation and genetically engineer cells to create transformative therapies for patients suffering from neurological and ophthalmological diseases.

Founded in 2016, BlueRock is at the forefront of the convergence of cell biology and genetic engineering. Our mission is to harness pluripotent stem cell technology and gene editing to deliver authentic, functional cell therapies that address the root causes of disease and offer hope to millions of patients worldwide.

What Are We Doing?

Our foundational science enables the generation and directed differentiation of universal pluripotent stem cells into authentic, functional cells for allogeneic cellular therapies.

We are passionate about realizing the promise of cell and gene therapy, shaping the future of regenerative medicine, and delivering new therapies to patients with limited or no treatment options.

Who is BlueRock?

BlueRock Therapeutics, a wholly-owned and independently operated subsidiary of Bayer AG, is a leading engineered cell therapy company using its unique cell+gene
 platform to direct cellular differentiation and genetically engineer cells to create a new generation of cellular medicines that address large patient populations suffering from neurological, cardiovascular, and immunology diseases.

The convergence of cell biology and genetic engineering is creating fundamental new ways to impact disease. Founded in 2016 to capitalize on these technological breakthroughs, we are advancing our novel  cell+gene
 platform to develop, manufacture, and deliver an entirely new generation of authentic and engineered cell therapies across three therapeutic areas: neurology, cardiology, and immunology.

What Are We Doing?

Our foundational science harnesses the ability to create and then direct the differentiation of universal pluripotent stem cells into authentic, functional cells that can be used as allogeneic cellular therapies to treat a broad array of diseases. We can also further engineer these cells, enabling them to produce enzymes, antibodies, and other proteins for additional therapeutic benefit.

We are passionate about delivering on the promise of cellular and gene therapy, shaping the future of cellular medicine, and delivering new therapies to millions of patients with treatment options.

We are seeking individuals who are collaborative, thrive in a fun and dynamic culture, and are steadfast in the commitment to advance cutting-edge cellular therapies to impact patients’ lives.

Description Of Position

BlueRock Therapeutics is seeking a Research Associate I, Process Development in New York City, NYC
. As a central development resource at the company, the Process Development team works closely with research, non-clinical, analytical, manufacturing, and quality teams. The successful candidate will be a key technical contributor to a dynamic and progressive team focused on development, scale up, and tech transfer of end-to-end manufacturing processes for authentic and engineered cellular products. The ability to communicate complex topics and assume a broad range of responsibilities is critical. Collaboration with a highly motivated, world-class team of scientists and engineers promises an exciting and engaging work environment for a talented and highly motivated individual. Hands-on experience with mammalian cell culture (ideally PSCs and differentiated cell products) is essential.

Responsibilities

Participate in the execution of in vitro experiments to develop, optimize, and characterize scalable processes for phase appropriate manufacture of pluripotent stem cells, and differentiated cellular products working within your team
Ability to follow provided standard operating procedures, batch records and other process documentation 
Perform process analytics to monitor the process performance, improve process understanding and characterize pluripotent stem cells and differentiated cellular products 
Conduct assigned routine tasks in the laboratory with minimal supervision
Analyze and document experimental data in electronic laboratory notebooks in a timely and accurate manner in accordance with the company quality management system. 
Attend and participate in internal and external meetings as required.

Minimum Requirements

Minimum of a Bachelors degree in a relevant field, including but not limited to: biological sciences, biomedical sciences, bioengineering, biochemistry, neurology
Basic wet lab skills, including mammalian cell culture and basic aseptic technique is required
Familiarity with cell characterization methods and technologies, such as flow cytometry, qPCR, immunoassays, and microscopy is required
Understanding of, or experience with, bioreactor systems is desired
Demonstrated ability to follow experimental plans and independently execute complex tasks
Strong English written and verbal communications skills
Able to work independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment.
Excellent organizational skills are required.

Work Environment

In this position you will work in a controlled laboratory environment
On-site work after-hours and weekends is routinely required.
