jobs.title: Lab Technician - Food And Bev
jobs.description:
Hiring a Lab Technician for a great food lab in Stockton, CA!! Must have similar experience and looking for long term growth within a company and team.

Swing shift - 3 pm to 11:30 pm, flexible to weekends if needed. Very team oriented environment.

Mid shift - 10 am to 6:30 pm M-F with open to weekends if needed.

Job Description

The Laboratory Technician plays a key role in supporting snack processing operations by conducting chemical and physical analyses and providing technical support to leadership. This position is based in Stockton, California and focuses on ensuring product quality, food safety, and consistent processing conditions within a dynamic, plant-based food environment.

Responsibilities

Perform a full range of laboratory analyses related to snack processing, demonstrating strong technical competency and accuracy.
Maintain familiarity with all laboratory equipment, chemicals, and reagents, and use them safely and effectively.
Collect, prepare, label, and organize raw material and product samples for analysis in accordance with established procedures.
Inspect and sample raw materials for each lot prior to processing, ensuring materials meet quality specifications.
Conduct allergen inspections of equipment in the assigned area after cleanup and changeovers to prevent cross-contamination at start-up, and document findings on checklists for the HACCP Manager.
Organize daily work, schedule and conduct analyses, and ensure all testing is completed on time with clear, professional reporting.
Perform necessary calculations, organize test data, and enter results into SPC charts and graphs to build a data set that supports operational decision-making.
Interpret laboratory data, understand how data is generated, and provide timely feedback on snack processing conditions to supervisors and other team members.
Make informed decisions regarding products that are out of specification, determine when additional sampling is needed, and recommend product holds to the Laboratory / Quality Services Manager when appropriate.
Monitor inventory levels of laboratory supplies, raw materials, and finished goods, and report status to the Laboratory / Quality Services Manager and/or Snack Processing Supervisor.
Maintain a clean, neat, and organized laboratory and work area to support efficient and safe operations.
Ensure safety when working with chemicals and reagents by following Good Laboratory Practices and all safe work procedures.
Design and deliver training related to laboratory procedures and quality assurance, demonstrating leadership in implementing QA-related training programs for the facility.
Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support laboratory, quality, and production objectives.

Essential Skills

Demonstrated knowledge and familiarity with laboratory operations and quality control functions in a food or related manufacturing environment.
Ability to perform chemical and physical analyses accurately and consistently, following established procedures and Good Laboratory Practices.
Strong capability to organize work, manage multiple analyses, and meet testing schedules and deadlines.
Competence in collecting, preparing, and organizing samples for analysis with attention to detail and documentation.
Ability to interpret laboratory data, understand processing conditions, and communicate findings clearly to management and production teams.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Outlook for data entry, charting, reporting, and communication.
Bachelors degree in Biology, Chemistry, or a related science discipline.
Minimum of one year of laboratory work experience and/or experience in a quality-related field.
Awareness of food safety and allergen control practices, including familiarity with HACCP-related documentation and procedures.
Ability to work effectively as part of a team and to collaborate with quality, laboratory, and production personnel.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Experience working in a food processing, snack manufacturing, or plant-based product environment is beneficial.
Experience in applying Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and standard operating procedures (SOPs) in a production or laboratory setting.
Understanding of statistical process control (SPC) and experience creating and interpreting charts and graphs for process monitoring.
Ability to take initiative in monitoring inventory, identifying needs, and supporting continuous improvement in laboratory operations.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for documenting results, preparing reports, and delivering training.
Leadership potential demonstrated through the ability to design and implement quality assurance training programs.
Detail-oriented mindset with a focus on accuracy, safety, and compliance with quality standards.
Comfort working with food-related allergens and implementing controls to prevent cross-contamination.

Work Environment

This role is based in a laboratory setting within a snack processing facility in Stockton, California. The Laboratory Technician works closely with production and quality teams in a plant environment focused on nuts and other plant-based snack products. The position involves regular use of laboratory instruments, chemicals, and reagents, as well as computer systems and software such as Excel, Word, and Outlook for data analysis and reporting. Work is performed on-site, with an emphasis on Good Laboratory Practices, Good Manufacturing Practices, and food safety standards including allergen control and HACCP-related procedures. The environment requires adherence to safety protocols, cleanliness, and organization, and may involve standing for extended periods and moving between the lab and production areas. Pre-employment drug testing and BG checks are part of the hiring process. The organization follows equal employment opportunity principles and promotes a professional, collaborative culture that supports growth in the plant-based food sector.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: EDA & CAD Engineer
jobs.description:
About Lumilens

At Lumilens we are building the critical photonics infrastructure that powers tomorrow’s AI supercomputing. From chip-to-chip optical interconnects to scalable photonic engines, Lumilens is unlocking a new era of computing faster, cooler, and massively more efficient.

We’re a well-funded startup backed by Mayfield and led by industry’s veterans who’ve built and scaled some of the most transformative technologies in the industry. This isn’t incremental innovation, it’s a ground-floor opportunity to rethink the optical layer from the silicon up. You’ll work alongside a team of world-class engineers solving some of the hardest challenges in optics, systems, and scale. Every line of code, every design decision, every breakthrough you help deliver will shape the infrastructure of tomorrow.

If you're looking for mission, momentum, and the chance to make an outsized impact jump on the rocket ship. We’re just getting started.

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced EDA & CAD Manager
to build and manage a robust design environment that supports multiple disciplines of IC designers across Lumilens. This role will own critical EDA methodology, CAD flows, design infrastructure, tool administration, and automation that enable faster, more reliable silicon development. You will partner closely with IC design, IT, and engineering leadership to strengthen our foundation, scale our tool environment, and improve the pace and quality of development across multiple programs.

What You'll Do:

Support IC design and IT leadership with EDA tool upgrades, infrastructure improvements, and methodology enhancements across analog, mixed-signal design, layout and verification, and digital design and verification environments.
Manage repositories for PDKs, internal and external IP, design data, and tools from multiple vendors, ensuring configuration control, reliability, and ease of adoption for engineering users.
Advise design and IT leadership on future planning, EDA methodology improvements, design environment scalability, and infrastructure investments that support rapid growth.
Develop, deploy, and maintain custom tools, scripts, automation, and plug-ins that improve designer productivity and are easily adopted across teams.
Support CAD flows integrating tools such as Cadence Virtuoso, Spectre, Pegasus, Genus, Innovus, Xcelium, Synopsys IC compiler, Siemens EDA, Calibre and related verification and signoff infrastructure.
Maintain and troubleshoot EDA infrastructure, including Linux and Unix environments, compute-farm integration, environment modules, tool-version management, license servers, and interactions between EDA applications and engineering infrastructure.
Build and support automated regression, validation, build, and deployment pipelines for EDA tools, design flows, and CAD environments.
Stay current with advancements in EDA tools, CAD methodologies, license management, IP management, and design infrastructure relevant to Lumilens’ technical goals.

What You'll Bring:

Deep understanding of Cadence/Synopsys tool flows, including analog and mixed-signal design tools such as Virtuoso, AMS, and Spectre.
Hands-on experience with layout and signoff tools such as PVS, Pegasus, and Calibre, as well as synthesis, APR, and physical design tools such as Genus, Innovus and Fusion Compiler.
Experience supporting multiple PDKs simultaneously, with familiarity with Intel, TSMC and GlobalFoundries preferred.
Strong experience with revision control, repository administration, and methodology recommendations using systems such as Perforce, VersIC, Git, or similar tools.
Experience managing internal and external IP, design data, PDK releases, and tool environments across multiple vendors and engineering teams.
Strong scripting and automation skills using Python, Perl, Tcl, Bash/Shell, and SKILL, including automation of EDA flows, tool setup, regression runs, log parsing, environment configuration, and design-data processing.
Experience administering and troubleshooting FlexNet/FlexLM license environments, including license-server configuration, lmstat/lmutil diagnostics, feature availability, checkout failures, queueing, utilization monitoring, and vendor-daemon issues.
Strong Linux and Unix troubleshooting skills, including LSF, Slurm, or Grid Engine compute-farm integration, environment modules, tool-version management, and debugging interactions between EDA tools, compute infrastructure, and license servers.
Demonstrated history of solving complex problems for EDA users and improving the reliability, usability, and scalability of design environments.

Nice-to-Haves:

Experience supporting remote computing environments such as ETX.
Experience supporting engineering teams across multiple international locations.
Some degree of systems administration ability across Linux, storage, compute, and engineering infrastructure environments.
Experience with build systems such as Make, GNU Make, CMake, and custom Makefile-based flows, including build dependencies, environment setup, and reproducible EDA/CAD workflows.
Experience with CI/CD and regression infrastructure such as Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, or GitHub Actions, including automated regression, validation, build, and deployment pipelines for EDA tools and design flows.

Why Join Us?

Competitive salary commensurate with experience
Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance
Professional development opportunities and certification support
Access to cutting-edge technology and cloud platforms
Collaborative work environment with cross-functional teams

At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. We believe water is more than a resource, it's a shared responsibility. As part of our Water Business Group, you’ll help shape how communities manage water for generations to come. From delivering safe drinking water and treating wastewater responsibly to developing sustainable water supplies and protecting lives and property through flood control, your work will directly support public health, environmental sustainability, and infrastructure resilience. We bring together experts across disciplines to solve complex challenges with bold thinking and technical excellence. Whether you're modernizing aging systems or pioneering innovative approaches, your contributions will make a meaningful difference in people’s lives. This isn’t just a job, it's a chance to lead change, drive progress, and leave a lasting legacy.

Civil Engineer (Water Resources Focus) – Northern California

HDR’s Northern California Civil Design Section is seeking a mid-level, Licensed Civil Engineer who is passionate about water resources and environmental resilience to help deliver impactful, water-focused infrastructure projects. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to meaningful work that supports flood protection, ecosystem restoration, and sustainable water systems across the region.

You’ll collaborate with and be mentored by experienced & highly reputable Senior Engineers while taking on increasing responsibility in the design and delivery of complex water infrstructure projects. If you’re driven by protecting communities, restoring natural systems, and shaping resilient water infrastructure, this role is for you.

Projects you’ll work on:

Levees, dams, and flood risk reduction systems
Wetland and habitat restoration projects
Water conveyance and hydraulic infrastructure
Nature-based and multi-benefit water solutions

In this role, you will:

Lead or support the development of construction documents for water resources projects, including plans, specifications, and design reports
Collaborate across disciplines to deliver integrated solutions for complex hydraulic and civil systems
Develop innovative, sustainable solutions to address unique water resource challenges, including projects with limited prescriptive guidance
Prepare engineering calculations, cost estimates, bid schedules, and technical documentation
Manage and contribute to projects within budgets and schedules
Coordinate design efforts with AutoCAD/Civil 3D designers and drafters; perform design work directly as needed
Conduct site visits and field assessments to verify existing conditions and inform design decisions
Mentor junior engineers and contribute to a collaborative team environment
Support projects from concept through construction, gaining exposure to real-world implementation

What makes this role unique:

Work on mission-driven water projects that improve community resilience
Be part of a team shaping California’s water future through both traditional and nature-based solutions
Gain hands-on experience across a diverse portfolio of civil design projects
Learn directly from industry leaders in water resources and infrastructure design

Preferred qualifications:

Experience in water resources and civil infrastructure design projects
Field experience supporting construction of water or civil infrastructure projects
Familiarity with levees, dams, stormwater systems, or restoration projects

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering or equivalent field
Previous experience in water resources engineering projects
Professional Engineer (PE) license
Excellent oral and written communication skills
An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Founded in 1965, UC Irvine
is a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities and is ranked among the nation’s top 10 public universities by U.S. News & World Report. The campus has produced five Nobel laureates and is known for its academic achievement, premier research, innovation and anteater mascot. Led by Chancellor Howard Gillman, UC Irvine has more than 36,000 students and offers 224 degree programs. It’s located in one of the world’s safest and most economically vibrant communities and is Orange County’s second-largest employer, contributing $7 billion annually to the local economy and $8 billion statewide.

To learn more about UC Irvine, visit www.uci.edu.

The Department of Anatomy and Neurobiology is a world-leading neuroscience department where discoveries at the molecular, anatomical, and physiological levels are seamlessly integrated to the development of new treatments for neurological diseases.

The Jung laboratory studies neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration, and related neurological disorders in mouse models, integrating animal experimentation, molecular and cellular assays, behavioral testing, imaging, and data analysis.

Your Role on the Team

Under the general supervision of the Principal Investigator, Dr. Kwang-Mook Jung, the Staff Research Associate I (SRA I) will provide technical support for research projects investigating neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration, and related neurological disorders using mouse models. The incumbent will assist with animal experiments, tissue collection and processing, molecular and cellular assays, behavioral testing, imaging, and data analysis. The position requires careful experimental documentation, adherence to established laboratory protocols, and collaboration with other laboratory members.

Required

What It Takes to be Successful

Basic knowledge of biological laboratory techniques and experimental procedures.
Ability to follow established protocols and maintain accurate experimental records.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to work independently under general supervision.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and Word and familiarity with basic scientific data analysis.
Ability to work effectively with laboratory personnel and comply with institutional safety and animal care requirements.
Bachelor's degree in biological sciences, neuroscience, biochemistry, or a related discipline, or equivalent education and research experience.
Hands-on experience with basic biological laboratory techniques gained through academic coursework or research training.

Preferred

Familiarity with mouse behavioral testing and ANY-maze or similar behavioral analysis software.
Experience with RNA extraction, qPCR, ELISA, Western blotting, immunofluorescence microscopy, or flow cytometry.
Experience using GraphPad Prism for basic statistical analysis and scientific graph preparation.
Prior research experience with laboratory mice and molecular/cellular assays.
Previous research experience in neuroscience, neuroimmunology, or related biomedical fields.
Previous experience handling laboratory mice and performing routine injections and tissue collection.

Work involves handling live laboratory mice, including injections, euthanasia, and tissue collection, under approved animal care and use protocols.
Must complete required institutional animal care and use, laboratory safety, and biosafety training, and comply with associated regulations.

jobs.title: Life Science Research Professional 2 (12-Month Fixed-Term)
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Department of Radiology is committed to excellence in patient care and inventing the future of Medical Diagnostics, Biomedical Imaging, and minimally invasive therapies. The people and programs comprising Stanford Radiology are world-renowned. Stanford Radiology continues to push the boundaries of innovation in physics and engineering to develop innovative methods for enhanced anatomic and functional imaging. Our diverse multidisciplinary teams of scientists, together with industry collaborators, are creating new methods for the early detection of cancer using molecular imaging, nanotechnology, and systems biology. They also continue to develop improved and more targeted methods for least invasive and compassionate cancer patient care. Ultimately, Stanford Radiology increasingly plays a very important role in the development of personalized medicine by moving advances from the laboratory to the clinic for improved patient centric care.

Stanford University is seeking a Life Science Research Professional 2 to perform more complex functions and activities involved in defined research projects, and independently conduct a portion of the research project(s).

Desired Qualifications

Equivalent working experience or Ph.D. in stem cell biology, immunology, or related field.
Post-doctoral experience is preferred in stem cell biology, cancer biology, immunology, or related field.
Extensive experience with molecular biology, mouse handling and procedures, flow-cytometry analysis and cell sorting, mammalian cell culture, RNA-sequencing, and microscopy.
Additional experience in computational biology is welcome.
Ability to independently design and troubleshoot experiments.
Excellent communication and organization skills.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Adobe Illustrator, GraphPad Prism, R, and other related software.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:

Frequently stand, walk, twist, bend, stoop, squat, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, perform desk-based computer tasks, use telephone, write by hand, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing over 40 pounds.
Occasionally sit, kneel, crawl, reach and work above shoulders, sort and file paperwork or parts.
Rarely climb, scrub, sweep, mop, chop and mix or operate hand and foot controls.
Must have correctible vision to perform duties of the job.
Ability to bend, squat, kneel, stand, reach above shoulder level, and move on hard surfaces for up to eight hours.
Ability to lift heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work in a dusty, dirty, and odorous environment.
Position may require repetitive motion.
Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of his or her job.

Working Conditions

May require working in close proximity to blood borne pathogens.
May require work in an environment where animals are used for teaching and research.
Position may at times require the employee to work with or be in areas where hazardous materials and/or infectious diseases are present.
Employee must perform tasks that require the use of personal protective equipment, such as safety glasses and shoes, protective clothing and gloves, and possibly a respirator.
May require extended or unusual work hours based on research requirements and business needs.

Work Standards

Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations.
Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors bases on training and lessons learned.
Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University’s Administrative Guide, http://adminguide.stanford.edu .

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s). Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to principal investigator.
Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project.
Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols.
Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required.
Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools.
Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols.
Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. Present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences.
Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager.
Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings.
Supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff.
Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in related scientific field and two years of relevant work experience; or Master’s degree in a related scientific field.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Comprehensive understanding of scientific principles.
General computer skills and ability to quickly learn and master computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance is essential.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.

Recruiting for this role ends on November 17, 2026

As an AI and Data Science Engineer I on the Advertising, Marketing & Commerce team, you will be responsible for...  

* Translating business goals into machine learning use cases and model design approaches.
* Performing exploratory data analysis to identify relationships, opportunities to influence outcomes, and cross-channel attribution patterns.

* Building proofs of concept, interpreting model results, and validating that solutions perform as intended.

* Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team

* Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
* Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
* Ability to lead projects or workstreams
* Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
* Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
* Ability to meet deadlines
* Ability to provide clear guidance to others

Deloitte's Advertising, Marketing & Commerce team creates content and experiences that inspire action. We design and implement technology platforms for personalized marketing across all digital touchpoints, specializing in customer-centric B2B and B2C solutions. Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management is a multidisciplinary program that recognizes the urgency of today's environmental challenges, and the enormous opportunities that may lead to transformative change. We have award-winning faculty in climate science, biodiversity, environmental policy, land use, and community outreach, all driven by a collective interest in our environmental future.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
In this position, the Soil Health Research Associate works on a study to assess the effects of solar panels on soil health and microclimate at various sites across the continental USA. The Soil Health Research Associate performs soil sampling, field measurements, laboratory analyses, data processing, and report writing to support a multi-site investigation comparing soils below solar panels with adjacent control areas. This position operates within established policies and procedures, or by referring to the supervisor's guidelines, and contributes to quality control, laboratory safety, and task prioritization for the project.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
The First Review Date for this job is November 23, 2026. For full consideration, please apply by the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
**Lab measurements:** The position will analyze the soil samples collected at 13 study sites/time points. More specifically, various physical, chemical, and biological indicators of soil health will be measured, such as: soil texture, soil aggregate stability, and soil porosity; concentrations of macronutrients (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) and micronutrients (B, Mn, Zn, Cu, Fe); soil cation exchange capacity, soil pH, soil organic matter content, soil C/N ratio, soil microbial biomass, pools of particulate organic carbon and mineral-associated organic carbon, dissolved organic and inorganic carbon, and soil respiration rates.
  
  
**Soil sampling:** The incumbent will run 13 field campaigns to collect soil samples.
  
  
**Field measurements:** During each field trip, air temperature , soil temperature, and moisture will be measured.
  
  
**Data analysis:** Field and laboratory data will need to be processed.
  
  
**Report writing:** At the end of the project, the SRA will summarize the project's measurements, results, and conclusion in a report.
  
  
Required Qualifications
  
  
Demonstrated experience in soil sampling
  
Demonstrated experience in soil analyses (field and lab)
  
Demonstrated experience in data analysis

jobs.title: Subject Matter Expert, Legal
jobs.description:
About The Team

We are building AI systems that help people tackle complex, consequential work in the legal industry. Law demands careful reasoning, precise language, and sound judgment: understanding the facts, identifying the right questions, weighing competing interpretations, and helping clients decide what to do next. We see an opportunity for AI to help legal professionals work with greater rigor and focus more of their time on the problems that matter most.

Our team works across Research, Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market to build AI capabilities and products for legal work. Our customers include the top law firms in the world as well as in-house legal departments of some of the largest businesses in the world. We translate the realities of practice into evaluations, training signals, and useful tools, with the ambition of making AI a trusted part of how lawyers research, analyze, draft, and advise.

About The Role

We are looking for a Subject Matter Expert in Law who brings the judgment and practical experience developed in a law firm to shaping the next generation of AI. You will help define what excellent legal work looks like, test where our models meet that standard, and turn your findings into better model behavior and product experiences.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of legal practice and AI development. You will work directly with legal materials, model outputs, evaluation rubrics, and product prototypes. Your expertise will help us tackle some of the hardest questions in legal AI, including how to assess reasoning when there is no single correct answer.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In This Role, You Will

Define the quality bar for what top-notch legal work looks like, drawing on real matters and the standards lawyers apply to research, analysis, drafting, document review, and client advice.
Design challenging, realistic AI model evaluations with representative facts, source materials, constraints, and deliverables, including cases that test ambiguity, competing arguments, and professional judgment.
Create and review reference work such as research memoranda, contract analyses, redlines, diligence findings, and draft legal documents that demonstrate strong reasoning and practical usefulness.
Develop rubrics that assess legal accuracy, issue spotting, factual grounding, citation validity, jurisdictional context, and the appropriate treatment of uncertainty.
Evaluate model outputs and complete legal workflows, identify recurring failures, and give researchers and engineers specific, actionable feedback supported by examples and corrected work.
Partner with Research on datasets, grading methods, and training tasks or environments that strengthen legal reasoning. Test whether model changes address the underlying problems and improve performance on new cases.
Work with Product and Engineering to identify valuable use cases, prototype workflows, and translate lessons from evaluations into experiences that fit how lawyers actually work.
Collaborate with legal professionals and design partners to refine our standards and test usefulness in practice, applying sound judgment around confidentiality, privilege, data permissions, and professional responsibility.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have practiced law at a law firm, with substantial experience producing and reviewing work for real client matters. We care more about demonstrated judgment and quality of work matter over title or firm pedigree.
Bring deep expertise in one or more practice areas, such as commercial transactions, corporate law, litigation, or regulatory work, and curiosity about workflows beyond your specialty.
Are an excellent legal researcher and writer who can assess authorities, distinguish strong arguments from plausible ones, and explain how facts and context affect a conclusion.
Can make expert judgment explicit: explain why an answer is incomplete, a clause creates risk, or an analysis misses the central issue, and describe what better work would look like.
Enjoy working directly with AI tools, exploring their limits, and testing ideas systematically. You can collaborate closely with technical teams and communicate clearly across disciplines.
Take ownership in ambiguous settings and are willing to build the first version of an evaluation, reference document, rubric, or workflow, then improve it through feedback.
Care deeply about the quality and consequences of legal work, and are motivated by the opportunity to help shape how AI supports the profession.

Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have

Experience designing evaluations, benchmarks, datasets, or review frameworks for legal work or frontier AI systems.
A track record of improving legal workflows through technology, knowledge management, automation, or new ways of working.
Experience training or supervising lawyers, developing practice guidance, or translating complex legal concepts for different audiences.

Description

Alta Planning + Design

.

This is a unique opportunity for somebody passionate about sustainable transportation and positively impacting our communities who's ready to take the next step in their career with a rapidly growing company in Oakland. In this role, you will provide technical leadership on the design of a variety of sustainable transportation projects, with a focus on making a positive impact on communities around the Bay Area and Northern California.

If you are looking for a mission-focused company that is an industry leader in active transportation design, TDM, roadway safety, greenways, and sustainable mobility, apply with us today!

About Alta

Alta is a mission-driven company working to mitigate climate change and advance safety and social justice by shaping sustainable, people-centered communities. We bring together expertise across planning, design, engineering, education and encouragement programs, and community engagement to help communities thrive. Our work is grounded in the belief that how places are designed and experienced has a profound impact on equity, health, and opportunity—and that people should always be at the heart of those decisions.

Founded in 1996, Alta was at the forefront of the active transportation movement and has spent nearly 30 years partnering with communities to imagine a more connected, resilient, and inclusive future. Today, with more than 225 staff across the United States and beyond, we are a global leader in creating environments that support everyday life, strengthen human connection, and respond to the challenges of a changing world. Alta offers the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines, contribute to meaningful work at every scale, and be part of a team committed to making lasting, positive change for people and the places they call home.

Our Senior Civil Engineering Associate will help foster livable communities across the Bay Area and Northern California. Projects range from natural surface trails to large arterial multi-use paths, and from Complete Streets to regional and multi-state bicycle and trail networks.

**Caltech**

**Job Category:** Fulltime Regular  
**Exempt Overtime Eligible:** Overtime Eligible

Caltech is a world-renowned science and engineering institute that marshals some of the world's brightest minds and most innovative tools to address fundamental scientific questions. We thrive on finding and cultivating talented people who are passionate about what they do. Join us and be a part of the diverse Caltech community.  
  
**Job Summary**  
  
The Zernicka-goetz Lab at Caltech is looking for a highly motivated and detail-oriented Research Technician to support lab projects and operations. This is a full-time position.  
  
**Essential Job Duties**  

* Assist with general laboratory organization and set-up.
* Generate and maintain common laboratory reagents.
* Ability to use different confocal microscopy systems to capture images as well as long-term video images of cell and embryo cultures.
* Assist postdocs and graduate students with cell culture experiments, data and image analysis (using IMARIS).
* Perform Immunohistochemistry on mammalian cells and embryo cultures.
* Identify routine issues with cell cultures and communicate observations to senior laboratory personnel; assist with troubleshooting under guidance.Occasionally require alternative work schedule, with the possibility of weekend work to meet project deadlines, media change or address unexpected issues.
* A highly motivated and qualified candidate may develop independent projects.
* Other duties as assigned.

  
**Basic Qualifications**  

* Bachelor's degree in science with an educational emphasis in biology or embryology.
* Must have a minimum of 2 years of good practical experience in all basic molecular biology techniques, especially the techniques related to the essential job duties.
* Experience in stem cell and tissue culture.
* Experience with mammalian tissue culture, mammalian embryos, and iPSC lines under BSL2 conditions.
* Experience with immunohistochemistry and confocal microscopy
* Must have hands-on wet lab experience.
* Must work productively and efficiently under minimal supervision.
* Must understand basic workflow and operations of laboratory research processes.
* Ability to work as part of a team.
* Eager to learn new techniques and methodologies.
* Excellent problem solver, strong organization and communication skills are required.

  
**Preferred Qualifications**  

* A background in embryology..
* Data analysis experience and demonstrable quantitative skills.

* Resume.

As an electronics team technician, you will leverage expertise in the assembly of mechanical and electrical devices and their testing to reliably assemble everything from bespoke electronics prototypes to production electronics.. You will also leverage strong written and oral communication skills, as well as detail-oriented diligence, to assist engineering and research staff with everything from soldering PCBs, designing and implementing the test procedures to validate the functionality of the assembled devices, to helping put together electronics test-setups, assisting in data collection, and handling logistics such as equipment inventory and lab organization.

- Support deployment and operation of technologies developed by the electronics team that serves the greater organization.

- Experience with and ability to use UNIX-based command-line interfaces

Adventist Health Tehachapi Valley has been providing high-quality healthcare services since 1934. We are comprised of a 25-bed hospital, wide range of outpatient services, emergency department, rural health clinics and medical offices. Tehachapi is located just north of Southern California's highly populated areas, with a mountain locale known for its outdoor living. Residents enjoy the scenic beauty, extreme sports and wildlife. Tehachapi is a nice balance of a small-town community within an epicenter of shopping, retail, arts and culture.

Job Summary:

Collects blood specimens, as well as receives, handles and processes specimens for Laboratory testing. Receives, sorts and accessions specimens, assigning to appropriate pre-analytic and analytic workflow. Completes computerized tasks related to patient registration and/or test order entry, specimen collection, receiving and processing. Performs basic post-analytic tasks, including distributing reports, storing and/or retrieving specimens. Completes quality-related tasks such as documentation of work, maintaining a clean, stocked and safe work area, and monitoring pending work, as well as escalating priority work. Operates and/or uses basic pre-analytic lab equipment. Adheres to all local/state/federal regulations, codes, policies and procedures to ensure privacy and safety while delivering optimal patient care.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

* High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI
* Associate’s/Technical Degree or equivalent combination of education/related experience: Preferred
* Experience in Phlebotomy in acute care environment: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

* Certified Phlebotomy Technician I (CPTI) license: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI

Facility Specific License/Certifications:

* Phlebotomy Tech (CPT) or Certified Phlebotomy Technician II (CPTII): Required

Department Specific License/Certifications:

* Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from approved vendor per AH policy: Required

Essential Functions:

* Collects blood specimens for a variety of Laboratory tests using age-appropriate techniques; handles/transports Lab specimens and provides post-phlebotomy care to patients. Receives specimens for testing; assesses specimens upon receipt according to established criteria to determine acceptability and takes action according to protocol including escalating to licensed or certified personnel for direction. Handles and processes a variety of specimen types to prepare them for analysis; adheres to protocols to maintain specimen integrity at all times.
* Completes computerized tasks as appropriate for affiliate to ensure complete patient registration and/or test order entry into the lab information system, as well as generation of collection lists and/or labels. Prepares and/or packages specimens for transport to another Adventist Health or outside reference laboratory and may complete computer steps necessary for processing referred specimens.
* Maintains an adequate inventory of supplies in work area and/or on phlebotomy cart. Maintains required records by completing basic documentation of pre-analytic and post-analytic work, as well as quality-related tasks. Participates in managing the laboratory workflow by performing duties such as monitoring pending work, escalating priority work, locating specimens, and coordinating specimen recollections.
* Verbally communicates released/reported results. Routes, distributes and retransmits released/reported results. Stores and retrieves specimens.
* Receives incoming calls for the laboratory and assists the caller as appropriate or transfers these calls to the appropriate laboratory section or person. Communicates with customer to clarify ambiguous, unclear or duplicate test orders.
* Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

jobs.description:
Nestled between Burbank and Pasadena, Adventist Health Glendale is one of the area's leading healthcare providers. We are comprised of a 515-bed hospital, two urgent cares, home care services, comprehensive cardiology care and a vast scope of services located in the San Fernando Valley. Glendale is known for its urban living, with easy access to dining, entertainment, shopping, amusement parks and outdoor recreation. Adventist Health Glendale is proud to be part of the thriving, diverse community since 1905.

Job Summary:

Prioritizes and performs a wide variety of clinical laboratory tests on various biological specimens. Reviews, evaluates, documents and reports results. Preserves confidentiality of patients and follows lab safety and maintenance protocols. Serves as technical consultant upon delegation by the medical director and mentor to laboratory personnel and trains and supervises trainees, laboratory assistants and clerks as needed.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

* Bachelor’s Degree in medical technology, clinical laboratory science, biological sciences, chemical sciences or allied health technologies or equivalent: Required
* Three years' clinical laboratory experience: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

* Valid Clinical Laboratory Scientist (CLS) license in state of employment: Required in CA
* Current certification from American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) or National Credentialing Agency for Labs (NCA): Preferred

Essential Functions:

* Employs positive patient identification procedures to ensure the integrity of each specimen for pre-analytical, analytical and post-analytical testing. Performs proper specimen collection (including phlebotomy procedures as necessary), labeling, handling, preservation or fixation, processing or preparation, transportation and storage. Adheres to Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and other patient confidentiality guidelines and regulations.
* Prioritizes lab orders according to type (STAT, ASAP, routine and timed studies) and performs various testing (including chemistry, coagulation, hematology, special chemistry, urinalysis, blood bank, serology, immunology, bacteriology, microbiology, referral testing and more) following prescribed quality assurance policies and procedures. Takes strides to contain costs without sacrificing patient care.
* Reviews and evaluates the validity and accuracy of test results, recognizing the interdependency of tests, the physiological conditions affecting results, patient age and normal values, controls, linearity errors, instrument codes, delta checks and more. Correlates test results with diagnoses and questions incompatible results. Documents and communicates test results, expediting all critical values and results to appropriate clinicians.
* Performs equipment and instrumentation maintenance, troubleshooting and calibration as needed. Inventories reagents, calibrators, controls and supplies, noticing usage trends and stocking accordingly. Demonstrates working knowledge to troubleshoot and utilize laboratory instrumentation and equipment. Serves as technical consultant and mentor of laboratory personnel. Orients, instructs and supervises laboratory assistants and clerks as needed.
* Performs inventory checks/correlation studies/CAP survey testing as scheduled or assigned by Department Supervisors. Performs quality control checks. Works to resolve quality control issues as necessary. Notifies Department Supervisor of suggested procedural changes and/or policy improvements that would better the productivity and efficiency of the laboratory as a whole.
* Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Organizational Requirements:

Adventist Health is committed to the safety and wellbeing of our associates and patients. Therefore, we require that all associates receive all required vaccinations as a condition of employment and annually thereafter, where applicable. Medical and religious exemptions may apply.
  
  
Adventist Health participates in E-Verify. Visit https://adventisthealth.org/careers/everify/ for more information about E-Verify. By choosing to apply, you acknowledge that you have accessed and read the E-Verify Participation and Right to Work notices and understand the contents therein.

The laboratory of Dr. Jeannie Chen at the Zilkha Neurogenetic Institute, Keck School of Medicine of USC, is seeking a highly motivated Research Associate to study phototransduction in rod and cone photoreceptors and the mechanisms underlying retinal degeneration and blindness. This NIH-funded laboratory uses rodent models and cell culture to investigate photoreceptor function, calcium signaling, inherited retinal diseases, GPCR biology, and protein misfolding and aggregation.

The successful candidate will develop and conduct independent research projects under the PI’s guidance, including designing and performing experiments and analyzing and interpreting data. Responsibilities also include presenting research findings, taking a leading role in writing manuscripts for publication, contributing to grant proposals, and supporting laboratory quality control, safety standards, and animal protocols.

The ideal candidate will be a creative and self-motivated researcher with experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including PCR or qRT-PCR, Western blotting and protein analysis, retinal tissue preparation under light- and dark-adapted conditions, *in vitro* and *in vivo* experiments (mouse), cell culture, immunohistochemistry (IHC) and immunocytochemistry (ICC), calcium imaging, fluorescence and confocal microscopy, and image analysis. Experience in photoreceptor biology, phototransduction, calcium signaling, retinal degeneration, protein trafficking, or protein misfolding is particularly valuable. The candidate should work well in a collaborative environment and may have opportunities to mentor junior laboratory members. Applicants should hold a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree in neuroscience, molecular or cellular biology, biochemistry, vision science, or a related field.

jobs.title: Research Associate, iPSC and Brain Organoid Culture
jobs.description:
Member of Technical Staff — Contract Position Engram Biosciences | San Francisco, CA | On-site
Expecting 9-12 months, with the opportunity to move to full-time. Hours: 8 hours a day, but can flex.
Hourly rate: $26-48 hourly About Engram Biosciences (https://www.engram.co/)

Engram Biosciences is building an autonomous brain organoid platform to improve how neurological diseases are studied and how potential therapies are discovered. Our long-term vision is to dramatically increase success in neurology by generating more informative, reproducible data from human biology.
We combine human iPSC-derived brain models with automation, high-content imaging, electrophysiology, and single-cell and spatial measurements. Consistent, well-characterized brain organoids are central to that work.

About the contract role

We are seeking a hands-on Research Associate for an on-site contract position focused primarily on producing and characterizing 3D human brain organoids, including forebrain and other region-specific models. You will maintain the stem cell cultures that support organoid production, monitor organoids through development, and help improve consistency between batches.
You will also support related neural cell models and assays, working closely with colleagues in biology, imaging, and automation. This is a bench-focused Research Associate role suited to someone with a bachelor’s degree and strong practical experience; a master’s degree is welcome but not required.

What you’ll do

Maintain human iPSCs and neural stem or progenitor cells, including passaging, banking, cryopreservation, and routine quality checks.
Generate and maintain forebrain and other region-specific brain organoids using established differentiation protocols.
Monitor organoid morphology, health, maturation, and variation within and between batches.
Induce and work with glial lineages, such as astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocytes, to support neural model development and characterization.
Prepare cultures and organoids for staining, imaging, and other downstream assays.
Document cell lines, organoid batches, culture conditions, deviations, and results clearly; help troubleshoot and refine protocols.
Support 2D neuronal cultures where they contribute to development or evaluation of the 3D models.

What you bring

A bachelor’s degree in neuroscience, stem cell biology, cell biology, bioengineering, or a related field. A master’s degree is also acceptable.
Hands-on experience with human iPSC culture and 3D brain organoid differentiation or maintenance, ideally including forebrain or other region-specific models.
Must have hands-on iPSC cell culture experience; brain organoid experience is ideal.
Experience maintaining neural stem or progenitor cells and strong aseptic technique.
Hands-on glial lineage induction experience with at least one of astrocytes, microglia, or oligodendrocytes.
Careful experimental execution, clear documentation, and the ability to recognize and troubleshoot culture variability.

Additional experience we value

Inhibitory neuron induction; single-cell library preparation using 10x Genomics, Parse Biosciences, or Fluent BioSciences workflows; experience with using high-content imagers like Molcular Device’s ImageXpress; and exposure to laboratory automation.

On-site amenities and contract terms

On-site amenities include delivered lunch, snacks, and complimentary access to a state-of-the-art gym. The contract duration, pay rate, and eligibility for insurance or retirement benefits should be stated once the engagement terms are set.

The Materials and Fuels Complex (MFC) is seeking nuclear facility research technicians. MFC is hiring for multiple facilities with multiple shift opportunities.

INL’s Materials and Fuels complex (MFC) empowers the next generations of nuclear energy advanced and hosts a unique combination of personnel, facilities and infrastructure and offers the ability to perform research and development of nuclear fuels and materials from fuel design, development, new fuel fabrication, post irradiation analysis, and advanced treatment and disposition.

This is an exciting time of innovation for nuclear energy, and MFC has multiple openings for Nuclear Research Facility Technicians to work in nuclear and radiological facilities including work in an analytical chemistry laboratory. Nuclear Research Facility Technicians perform a variety of work activities to support research, such as research experiment assembly and disassembly, material preparation using an Electro Discharge Machine (EDM), experiment or sample preparation, operating remote handled equipment, working in hot-cells, gloveboxes, or with shielded casks.

Nuclear Facility Research Technicians perform maintenance of facility systems and equipment, fuel and waste handling, processing, and treating nuclear fuel, radioactive and hazardous material, tracking, packaging, transferring, receiving, and storing fissionable materials.

Senior Research Associate / Scientist

Location: San Diego, CA
(Onsite, Monday–Friday)
Employment Type:
Full-Time
Anticipated Salary Range:
$80,000–$135,000 DOE

About Telesis Bio

Telesis Bio is a biotechnology company advancing synthetic biology through innovative DNA synthesis, assembly, and automation technologies. Our mission is to accelerate biological discovery by enabling researchers to design, build, and test biological systems with greater speed, precision, and flexibility.

As we expand our synthetic biology and automation capabilities, we are focused on connecting computational design with experimental execution and continuous learning.

Predict. Build. Learn.

Our multidisciplinary team brings together expertise in molecular biology, enzymology, engineering, and software to develop solutions that help scientists move from biological concepts to experimental results more efficiently.

Position Summary

Telesis Bio is seeking a Senior Research Associate or Scientist to join our Research & Development team in San Diego, CA. This hands-on laboratory role will develop and optimize enzymatic workflows for enzymatic oligonucleotide generation, DNA preparation, and DNA assembly.

The role will focus on improving reaction performance, DNA recovery, product quality, and reproducibility through controlled experimentation and systematic troubleshooting. The successful candidate will work with scientists and automation engineers to translate emerging methods into reliable, scalable workflows.

Both levels require substantial hands-on laboratory work. Hiring level will reflect relevant experience and demonstrated responsibility for experimental strategy and technical decisions.

Key Responsibilities

Design, execute, and analyze experiments for oligonucleotide generation, preparation, and DNA assembly.
Develop and optimize workflows involving PCR, restriction digestion, ligation, magnetic bead capture, nucleic acid purification, and DNA recovery.
Develop assays using gel electrophoresis and quantitative nucleic acid analysis to evaluate size distribution, yield, purity, unwanted products, and reaction efficiency.
Design controlled experiments to distinguish problems in substrate preparation, enzymatic conversion, purification, and downstream amplification.
Optimize reaction conditions, substrate concentrations, and processing steps; assess reproducibility across independent preparations and runs.
Interpret experimental data, distinguish observations from mechanistic hypotheses, and communicate conclusions and recommended next steps.
Collaborate with scientists, automation engineers, and software developers to integrate molecular biology methods with automated workflows.
Document reproducible methods and support transfer into product development and manufacturing.
Prepare multicomponent reactions, dilutions, and pools accurately; maintain source and destination plate maps and sample traceability.
Maintain complete experimental records, protocols, reagent and sample identities, and QC results to support data integrity and knowledge transfer.
Establish appropriate controls and measurable performance criteria to determine whether workflow changes improve product quality and reliability.
Contribute to experimental priorities and project planning at the selected level.
Share technical knowledge and provide guidance to laboratory colleagues, as appropriate to experience.
Follow laboratory safety procedures and maintain high standards of experimental quality

Level Expectations

Senior Research Associate:
Independently execute experiments within an agreed strategy; propose controls, troubleshoot workflows, and recommend next experiments with the project lead.
Scientist:
Develop the research strategy for defined technical problems; prioritize competing hypotheses and design experiments that distinguish among them.
Scientist:
Lead defined projects through execution and interpretation; own technical recommendations, scientific decisions, and milestones and demonstrate reproducible performance.
Scientist:
Provide scientific guidance and mentorship and communicate project progress, technical risks, and recommended priorities.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's, master's, or PhD in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Bioengineering, Genetics, or a closely related scientific discipline.
Relevant experience appropriate to the level. Typical experience pathways are:
Senior Research Associate: Typically 4+ years of relevant industry experience with a bachelor's degree, or equivalent experience with an advanced degree, with demonstrated independent execution and troubleshooting.
Scientist: Typically 5+ years of relevant industry experience with a bachelor's degree, 3+ years with a master's degree, or a PhD with applicable research experience and demonstrated ownership of experimental strategy and technical recommendations.
Strong hands-on molecular biology experience, including PCR, DNA manipulation or assembly, gel electrophoresis, and quantitative nucleic acid analysis.
Experience developing and troubleshooting multistep laboratory workflows using appropriate positive, negative, and process controls.
Understanding of enzymatic DNA reactions and how substrate structure, reaction conditions, and carryover can affect performance.
Ability to analyze data, evaluate alternative explanations, and recommend experiments that resolve technical uncertainty.

jobs.description:
Job Description

Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a well-qualified Postdoctoral Research Associate in Computational Geoscience for the Department of Critical Minerals & Geothermal Energy in the Energy and Environment Science and Technology (EES&T) directorate. This postdoctoral researcher will advance reactive transport and coupled thermal–hydraulic–mechanical–chemical (THMC) simulations emphasizing interactions among fluid flow, heat transfer, geochemical reactions, geomechanics, and evolving rock properties. Simulations will be developed using FALCON (Fracturing And Liquid CONvection) and MOOSE (Multiphysics Object-Oriented Simulation Environment), or similar tools. Research will address geological hydrogen (geohydrogen) production, electrofracturing stimulation for critical mineral recovery, enhanced geothermal systems (EGS), and carbon mineralization. Our team works a 9x80 schedule with every other Friday off.

Key Responsibilities

Develop reactive transport models using FALCON/MOOSE or similar tools, coupling advection, diffusion, dispersion, aqueous speciation, and mineral dissolution and precipitation with thermal, hydraulic, and mechanical processes.
Implement reaction kinetics and reactive surface area, porosity, permeability, and fracture–matrix exchange conditions; quantify species transport and elemental mass balances. Evaluate transport-limited versus reaction-limited behavior and represent mineralogical heterogeneity and evolving fluid chemistry across laboratory and reservoir scales.
Model hydrogen generation through water–rock reactions, critical mineral mobilization and recovery, and carbon mineralization; evaluate how fluid chemistry and operating conditions influence reaction progress and recovery.
Couple electrofracturing and electrohydraulic stimulation with reactive transport to assess fracture connectivity, fluid access, and mineral accessibility; simulate circulation and heat extraction in EGS.
Verify numerical implementations, calibrate and validate models against laboratory or field observations, and assess convergence, parameter sensitivity, and uncertainty.
Automate computational workflows, improve parallel performance, collaborate with experimental teams, publish findings, and contribute to research proposals.

The candidate is expected to be a strong asset to our interdisciplinary R&D team and work effectively both alone and as a team member. The candidate must be self-motivated but also take direction from other team members and peers.

jobs.description:
About Us

Scripps Research is a nonprofit biomedical institute ranked as one of the most influential in the world for its impact on innovation. We celebrated our 100-year legacy in 2024. This significant milestone marks a century of seminal discoveries in immunology, infectious diseases (such as COVID-19, flu, HIV), neuroscience, heart disease, cancer, and more. Located in La Jolla, California, the institute houses six research departments, multiple Nobel laureates, a top-ranked graduate school and a leading postdoctoral training program. Scripps Research encompasses two elite and highly innovative institutes, the Calibr-Skaggs Institute for Innovative Medicines and Scripps Research Translational Institute, which merge foundational studies in biology, chemistry and computer science with translational science to produce pioneering drugs and advances in digital and precision medicine. Together, we cultivate new scientific leaders and expand the frontiers of knowledge to deliver medical breakthroughs impacting human health around the globe. If you have a passion for making a difference, this could be your opportunity to join our transformative team.

POSITION TITLE:
Postdoctoral Associate

Position Summary

The Xiang-Lei Yang Lab at Scripps Research seeking a motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate how a tRNA synthetase links nutrient sensing to translational control in pancreatic β-cells. The project aims to define the mechanisms of translational control that enable cells to adapt to metabolic stress, with a focus on pancreatic β-cells and insulin-responsive tissues. By integrating mouse models, primary cells and tissues, and multi-omics approaches, the research seeks to uncover fundamental mechanisms underlying metabolic regulation and diabetes.

Responsibilities

Investigate cellular responses to metabolic stress, with a focus on pancreatic β-cells and insulin-responsive tissues, using mouse models and primary cells.
Define the molecular mechanisms of translational regulation through biochemical assays, polysome profiling, and integrated omics approaches.
Design and lead experiments, analyze data, publish findings, present at scientific meetings, and contribute to mentoring junior researchers.

Include a cover letter, CV, and contact information for three references on your application.

Postdoctoral Associates are appointed positions for the purpose of developing scholarly competence, working under the supervision of a Scripps Research Faculty member. These appointments are normally not renewed beyond a total of five years.

Scripps Research adheres to the National Institutes of Health (“NIH”) and National Science Foundation (“NSF”) definition of a Postdoctoral Scholar
: An individual who has received a doctoral degree (or equivalent) and is engaged in a temporary and defined period of mentored, advanced training to enhance the professional skills and research independence needed to pursue their chosen career path.

Make Scripps Research your next step to advance and develop your career. Click here to learn more about our Postdoctoral Program and Services: https://education.scripps.edu/postdoctoral/

The Yang Laboratory
, in the Department of Integrative Structural and Computational Biology at Scripps Research, investigates the diverse functions of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (aaRSs) beyond their canonical roles in protein synthesis. Our research explores how these essential enzymes regulate cellular signaling, metabolism, and human physiology, and how their dysfunction contributes to diseases, including neurological, metabolic, and autoimmune disorders. By integrating structural biology, biochemistry, cell biology, and animal models, we aim to uncover fundamental biological mechanisms and identify new opportunities for therapeutic intervention.

Requirements

Must possess a PhD in molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, or a related field , or equivalent degree from a recognized institution of higher learning. A pending doctoral degree may be considered with approval of the Principal Investigator and Human Resources.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with mouse models, primary tissues, or metabolic phenotyping
Experience with islet biology, diabetes, or metabolism research
Experience with tRNA synthetases, RNA biology, or translational control
Experience with translation assays, including polysome or ribosome profiling
Experience with or interest in transcriptomic and proteomic data analysis.

COMPENSATION:
Postdoctoral Associates will be hired following the National Institute of Health and California’s exempt salary guidelines, which provide for a starting range of $70,304- $75,353. Consideration will be given to experience that exceeds the listed requirements.

Comprehensive Benefits Include

jobs.title: Research Associate / Senior Research Associate, Evidence Base (Applications Development)
jobs.description:
Themis Bios is building the measurement layer for modern biology. Our single-cell RNA-seq technology is designed to make transcriptomic readouts routine, quantitative, and scalable — so scientists can ask harder questions and trust the answers.

We are looking for a Research Associate or Senior Research Associate to join Applications Development and own the cell biology at the front of our workflows. This is a hands-on, bench-first role: you will grow the cells, build the models, and turn living systems into single-cell samples that read cleanly on our platform. Your first focus is the Evidence Base: running the drug-perturbation experiments behind a growing atlas of how human primary cells and organoids respond to compounds. You will work alongside our Product Development team, and your culture work and sample prep will be the foundation the rest of the applications work is built on.

It is a good fit for someone who takes real pride in cell culture and technique, wants their bench work to feed a product, and brings hands-on drug screening experience they want to build on with single-cell readouts.

What you'll do
Cell culture.
Culture primary human PBMCs (thaw, rest and T-cell activation, e.g. anti-CD3/CD28) and gut organoids, with iPSC-derived models as needed — covering media preparation, plating, passaging, expansion, and cryopreservation, all under strict sterile technique.
Model quality.
Monitor culture health, morphology, and consistency; run routine checks and keep cultures to documented, reproducible standards so downstream results are trustworthy.
Sample preparation.
Prepare single-cell and single-nucleus samples from cells, organoids, and tissue — dissociation, viability and debris management, counting, and input QC — tuned for compatibility with the Themis scRNA-seq technology.
Experiment execution.
Execute cell-culture and sample-prep experiments, and run drug-perturbation studies (drug and molecule treatments across dose and time), under the direction of senior team members.
Drug plate preparation.
Prepare compound stocks in DMSO, serial dilutions, dose–response and combination layouts, and randomized plate maps with vehicle and control wells; keep compound inventory, storage and lot records current.

Program and run liquid handlers (e.g. Agilent Bravo) for plate stamping, dilution and sample handling, and keep run logs.
Screening cadence.
Deliver about two drug plates a week on schedule, from cells to single-cell libraries, with QC at each step.
Data and records.
Generate high-quality, reproducible data and keep detailed, well-organized experimental records.
Protocols and QC.
Help turn working procedures into clear protocols and SOPs, and contribute to input-QC and sample-acceptance methods as workflows mature.
Lab operations.
Keep the lab running — inventory, reagent and consumable stocks, equipment upkeep and calibration — so experiments start on time and run clean.

What you'll bring
Bachelor's or Master's degree in cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, bioengineering, or a related field.
2–5 years of relevant industry or advanced academic laboratory experience (toward the upper end for the SRA level).
Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture skills and disciplined sterile technique — together with drug screening, this is the core of the role.
Hands-on drug or compound screening in mammalian cells — dose–response or plate-based assays, including preparing drug plates from stocks.
Experience with primary immune cells (PBMCs preferred) and one or more of: 3D / organoid culture, or iPSC culture and differentiation.
Sample-prep experience — dissociating cells, organoids, or tissue into high-quality single-cell suspensions, or a clear aptitude to learn it quickly.
Careful technique with complex biological workflows, and a track record of generating reproducible data and troubleshooting experiments.
Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and clear documentation habits.
Comfortable in a dynamic startup environment with evolving priorities.

Strongly preferred
Experience with single-cell genomics workflows (e.g. scRNA-seq, droplet or bead-based systems, barcoding / cell-hashing methods).
Experience writing or adapting liquid-handler methods (e.g. Agilent Bravo, Hamilton, Echo) or other high-throughput sample handling.

Nice to have
Experience with NGS library prep and QC methods (Bioanalyzer, TapeStation, Qubit, fragment analysis).
Basic data-analysis skills (e.g. Python, R, or standard analysis tools) for exploring experimental results.
Prior work in an assay-development, applications, or product-development lab.

What success looks like
Cultures and models are healthy, consistent, and ready when the team needs them.
Single-cell samples go into the workflow at high quality, with QC that holds up run to run.
Data is reproducible and records are clear enough that others can build on the work.
Throughput and reliability of the applications team go up because of how you run the bench.
Drug plates go out on schedule, about two a week, with plate-map and dosing errors near zero and vehicle-control variability within spec.
Each new model and plate workflow has an SOP someone else can run from.
You operate with growing independence, flag issues early, and reinforce a culture of rigor and accountability.
