Looking to join a passionate team dedicated to developing and manufacturing life-saving biopharmaceuticals? Avid Bioservices is a leading clinical and commercial biologics CDMO focused on creating innovative solutions to meet the needs of our clients and improve patient outcomes.

**Your Role:**

We're currently seeking a talented **Research Associate** to join our Analytical Development team as we develop innovative analytical methodologies for protein biologics. As a Research Associate in Analytical Development, you'll have the opportunity to work closely with experienced analytical Scientists to identify and characterize protein biologics. Your focus will be to develop Cell-based, ELISA, HPLC, CE, PCR and/or SDS-PAGE methods, and you'll have the chance to interface with Quality Control as methods are transferred into that group for cGMP testing. This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of a dynamic team that's making a difference in the world of biologics. Join us and take your career to the next level!

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Perform laboratory tasks to support the development, optimization, validation and routine testing of protein therapeutics via protein characterization techniques.
* Demonstrate proficiency in one or more of the following: ELISA, Cell-Based Assays, HPLC, CE, icIEF, PCR, SDS-PAGE
* Document method development and validation activities according to current practices.
* Assist in training analysts on new methods and transfer methods to cGMP Quality Control lab, as necessary.
* Work in a fast-paced team environment, meet deadlines, and prioritize work.
* Provide regular updates to Process Development department and other functional teams as necessary.
* Other tasks as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in the Biological or Physical Sciences with 2+ years of relevant experience and demonstrated working knowledge of scientific principles.
* Experience with analytical method development using bioanalytical techniques
* Should have experience with at least one of the following: ELISA, Cell-Based Assays, HPLC, CE, icIEF, PCR, SDS-PAGE

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience in assay validation/ qualification as well as industry regulations that apply to job functions are a plus!

**Position Type/Expected Hours of Work:**

This role is a full-time onsite position. Days and hours of work are either Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Sunday to Wednesday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; or Wednesday to Saturday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. unless otherwise stated by Supervisor. Ability to work overtime as necessary.

**Compensation:**

We offer competitive compensation packages for this role, including a base salary, performance-based bonuses, and comprehensive benefits such as health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) matching, and paid time off.

The compensation range for this role is $31.15 - $38.94 hourly depending on experience and qualifications. Additionally, we offer opportunities for career growth and development as well as a supportive and inclusive work environment.

**Who you are:**

* You have a "bring it on!" team player approach and an unshakable positive attitude, always ready to tackle anything that comes your way.
* Your written and verbal skills are out of this world, and you communicate with clarity and confidence.
* You have exceptional multitasking skills and an unparalleled attention to detail that ensure the smooth running of everything.
* You are a master at building relationships, capable of establishing connections with anyone, be it team members, clients, vendors, or suppliers.

In this dynamic role, expect a blend of regular activities like sitting, standing, and walking, with occasional physically engaging tasks such as lifting objects up to 25 pounds. Pay: $27/hr and up, based on experience  
  
About the role  
Steel Traditions builds custom steel windows and doors for high-end homes. As our Final Assembly & QC Technician, you are the last set of hands and eyes before a unit leaves the shop. You stand each unit up on our QC wall and fully install it as it will go in on site, including sliders, French doors and bifolds. You glaze, seal, put on the hardware and check every part. Then you wrap, package and load it to ship. Nothing ships until you've passed it. There is room to grow into a QC Wall lead role.  
  
What you'll do  

* Review the prints and shop drawings for every unit before hanging it.
* Stand up and install finished units on the shop QC wall, including French doors, sliders and bifolds, following the manufacturer's install order.
* Glaze units by setting the glass and running silicone on both sides, then clean the units.
* Install hardware: handles, hinges, sweeps, cylinders, shoot bolts and hardware boxes. Adjust parts and make small fixes when something doesn't fit.
* Hold the line on quality: no unit ships with damage, scratches or paint defects. If it isn't right, tag it HOLD and tell the fab lead and the office the same day.
* Check every part thoroughly: function, operation, finish/color against the order, glass, seals and hardware. Fill out the QC form for every unit.
* Diagnose operation problems (binding, sag/deflection, misaligned tracks or bifold supports) and track down problems on doors and frames that won't pass, working with the fabrication lead, and log any rework and its cause.
* Make lists of missing or wrong parts and send them to the office so they get ordered.
* Wrap, package and label passed units, and help load them for delivery. Occasionally help with site service or pickups.
* Keep the QC area organized: store oversized units, lay out the floor, set up the wall and restock supplies.
* Submit The Daily every workday before leaving: units worked, hours per unit, QC result, materials needed and roadblocks. This is part of the job, not extra.

  
What we're looking for  

* 2+ years in window/door installation, glazing, millwork, cabinet or metal fabrication, or similar hands-on assembly.
* Comfortable with hand and power tools (drills, die grinders, sanders, knives, silicone guns).
* Can read shop drawings, a tape measure to 1/16\", and installation guides.
* A detail-oriented, \"it's not done until it's right\" attitude, and the ability to explain clearly what's wrong.
* Asks questions early and goes back to the lead whenever something is unclear.
* Reliable attendance and on-time starts. Can fill out simple phone or tablet forms every day.
* Bilingual English/Spanish is a plus. Experience with steel/aluminum systems or bifolds is a plus.

  
Physical demands  

* Standing, bending, kneeling and reaching for most of the shift.
* Lifting and moving heavy, oversized glass and steel units with a team and lifting equipment. Lifting up to 75 lbs on your own.
* Working with sealants and sanding, using provided PPE (respirator, gloves, eye protection).
* Indoor shop environment, with occasional job-site visits.

  
Schedule and location  
Monday–Friday, 6:30 AM–3:00 PM, at our shop in Vista, CA.  
  
Steel Traditions is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description:
Company Overview
At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects.
Position Overview
Join Skild AI’s manufacturing team to help ensure robots, accessories, and incoming materials meet design requirements and quality standards. In this hands-on role, you will perform in-process and final inspections, verify incoming material conformity, and complete visual inspections of returned robots and accessories. You will document findings, identify nonconforming products, and work with manufacturing and engineering to resolve quality issues.
Responsibilities
Inspect incoming components, materials, and subassemblies against engineering drawings, specifications, approved samples, and applicable inspection criteria to verify design conformity and quality.
Perform in-line and in-process inspections at designated assembly checkpoints. Verify workmanship, component placement, hardware installation, cable routing, connector seating, labeling, and other defined acceptance criteria.
Complete final inspections of manufactured robots and accessories before release. Verify required inspection and test records are complete and products meet documented acceptance criteria.
Perform visual receiving inspections of all incoming return material authorization (RMA) robots and accessories. Document physical condition, visible damage, missing components, identification labels, and other observed discrepancies.
Record RMA inspection findings and photographs, as appropriate, and communicate observations to repair personnel. Distinguish observed conditions from suspected causes requiring further evaluation.
Use appropriate measuring instruments, inspection tools, and visual inspection methods to check dimensions, fit, finish, and assembly quality. Verify equipment calibration status before use.
Identify, label, and segregate nonconforming material or products according to established procedures. Document discrepancies and escalate issues for authorized disposition.
Maintain accurate inspection records, checklists, and quality data, including part numbers, serial numbers, inspection results, and supporting evidence as required.
Communicate recurring defects and quality trends to manufacturing, engineering, and quality personnel. Support root-cause investigations, corrective actions, and improvements to inspection processes.
Coordinate inspections with production and receiving priorities while maintaining consistent acceptance standards. Follow safety, material handling, and 5S practices and perform other assigned quality duties.

Preferred Qualifications
At least 5 years of experience in quality control, quality inspection, or a similar role supporting electro-mechanical manufacturing.
Experience performing incoming, in-process, and final inspections of mechanical parts, electrical components, or assembled products.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, dimensions, tolerances, specifications, bills of materials, and inspection instructions.
Hands-on experience using calipers, micrometers, and other inspection or measuring equipment appropriate to the product.
Ability to evaluate electro-mechanical assembly workmanship, including hardware installation, PCBA placement, cable routing, connector engagement, and labeling.
Strong attention to detail and sound judgment when comparing inspection results with documented acceptance criteria.
Experience documenting defects, maintaining traceable inspection records, and handling nonconforming material through established procedures.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to describe defects objectively and work effectively with production, receiving, repair, and engineering teams.
Ability to organize inspection priorities, work independently within defined procedures, and escalate unclear requirements or quality concerns.
Comfort using Google Docs, Google Sheets, email, and electronic quality or production systems to record and communicate inspection results.

Additional Experience We Value 
Experience inspecting robots, automated equipment, or similar complex electro-mechanical products.
Experience documenting the condition of RMA products and supporting repair or failure-analysis teams.
Familiarity with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, sampling plans, and applicable workmanship standards.
Experience with ERP or product lifecycle management systems, such as Rootstock and Arena, and supporting corrective actions or continuous improvement.

Physical Requirements 
The role involves regular sitting, standing, and walking in a manufacturing environment, as well as close visual inspection and hands-on use of inspection tools. Handling components and accessing inspection points on robots and accessories may require bending and reaching. Essential job functions may be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

jobs.title: Bioinformatics Scientist / Senior Bioinformatics Scientist — cfDNA-Based Cancer Screening
jobs.description:
Position Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated Bioinformatics Scientist or Senior Bioinformatics Scientist to develop, optimize, validate, and maintain bioinformatics pipelines for a cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-based colorectal cancer (CRC) screening assay.

The successful candidate will work at the interface of computational biology, next-generation sequencing (NGS), molecular diagnostics, and statistical modeling. This individual will be responsible for transforming raw sequencing data into reliable analytical outputs and developing robust computational methods to identify cancer-associated molecular signals in plasma-derived cfDNA.

The role will support analytical validation, algorithm development, assay performance optimization, and preparation for clinical and regulatory submissions. The candidate will collaborate closely with molecular biology, assay development, laboratory automation, clinical, quality, and regulatory teams to establish a reproducible, scalable, and well-documented bioinformatics workflow.

Key Responsibilities

1. NGS Bioinformatics Pipeline Development

Develop, optimize, and maintain end-to-end bioinformatics pipelines for cfDNA-based targeted sequencing assays.
Process and analyze raw sequencing data, including FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, and VCF or other assay-specific intermediate files.
Implement quality control metrics for sequencing quality, mapping, coverage, library complexity, molecular error rates, and sample-level performance.
Develop methods for low-frequency variant detection, error suppression, background-noise characterization, and identification of cancer-associated molecular features, as appropriate to the assay design.
Optimize computational workflows for throughput, reproducibility, scalability, and efficient processing of high-volume sequencing data.
Integrate bioinformatics outputs with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), automated laboratory workflows, and downstream reporting systems as needed.

2. Algorithm and Biomarker Development

Develop and evaluate computational methods to identify cancer-associated signals in cfDNA, including genomic alterations and other molecular features supported by the assay design.
Collaborate with molecular biologists and assay scientists to investigate biological and technical sources of background noise.
Develop statistical models and classification algorithms to distinguish cancer-associated signals from non-cancer background.
Evaluate feature selection, model training, cross-validation, threshold optimization, and generalizability using appropriate study designs.
Assess the effects of cfDNA input, sequencing depth, tumor fraction, sample quality, and pre-analytical variables on algorithm performance.
Maintain clear separation between model development, parameter tuning, and independent performance evaluation to minimize overfitting and data leakage.

3. Bioinformatics Analytical Validation

Design and execute bioinformatics validation studies in collaboration with assay development and analytical validation teams.
Establish and document software and algorithm performance characteristics, including:
Analytical accuracy and reproducibility.
Detection performance across relevant signal levels.
False-positive and false-negative analytical calls.
Robustness to sequencing depth, input variability, and technical noise.
Sample-level quality control and failure criteria.
Computational precision, deterministic behavior, and reproducibility across software versions.
Evaluate the impact of sequencing errors, contamination, sample mix-ups, batch effects, and other potential confounders.
Define acceptance criteria, validation datasets, statistical analysis plans, and validation reports before study execution.
Support investigations of discrepant results, pipeline failures, and unexpected assay performance.

4. Software Engineering and Computational Infrastructure

Develop maintainable, modular, and version-controlled bioinformatics software using Python, R, and/or other appropriate programming languages.
Implement workflow management using tools such as Nextflow, Snakemake, or WDL.
Use Git-based version control, automated testing, continuous integration, containers, and reproducible software environments.
Deploy workflows in cloud or high-performance computing environments, as appropriate.
Establish automated quality checks, audit-friendly execution logs, data lineage, version tracking, and monitoring.
Develop unit, integration, regression, and end-to-end tests to ensure reliable pipeline performance.
Collaborate with software engineering and IT teams to maintain secure and reliable computational infrastructure.

5. Clinical Performance and Translational Research Support

Support retrospective and prospective studies evaluating cfDNA-based cancer screening algorithms.
Collaborate with biostatisticians and clinical scientists to assess sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and other clinical performance measures.
Support the development of independent training, tuning, and test datasets for algorithm development and evaluation.
Analyze discordant cases and investigate associations between molecular features, clinical findings, and reference-standard outcomes.
Support clinical study data analysis, technical documentation, and preparation of scientific publications and presentations.

6. Regulatory, Quality, and Documentation

Prepare technical documentation for analytical validation, software verification and validation, design controls, and regulatory submissions.
Work with Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs to ensure compliance with applicable requirements for clinical laboratory testing and in vitro diagnostic software.
Maintain traceability between software requirements, risk controls, test cases, validation evidence, and software releases.
Contribute to change-control procedures, risk assessments, deviation investigations, and corrective and preventive actions when applicable.
Support the development of controlled procedures for pipeline deployment, updates, maintenance, and release approval.

7. Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner with assay development, molecular biology, laboratory operations, automation engineering, biostatistics, clinical development, and regulatory teams.
Translate biological and clinical questions into computational analyses and actionable technical requirements.
Communicate complex bioinformatics findings clearly to scientific and non-computational stakeholders.
Contribute to experimental design, assay optimization, troubleshooting, and strategic development of the cancer screening platform.

Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genomics, Biostatistics, Computer Science, or a related discipline; alternatively, an M.S. with substantial relevant industry experience.
Strong experience analyzing NGS data, preferably from targeted sequencing assays or liquid biopsy applications.
Proficiency in Python and/or R, including experience developing reusable, well-tested analytical code.
Demonstrated understanding of NGS data processing, sequencing quality control, alignment, variant calling, and statistical analysis.
Experience with Linux/Unix environments, shell scripting, Git, and reproducible computational workflows.
Strong knowledge of statistical methods, experimental design, data quality assessment, and performance evaluation.
Ability to independently troubleshoot complex computational problems and communicate results across multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with cfDNA, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), liquid biopsy, or blood-based cancer screening assays.
Experience with ultra-low-frequency variant detection, molecular barcodes or unique molecular identifiers (UMIs), error-corrected sequencing, and sequencing background suppression.
Familiarity with machine learning, predictive modeling, classification algorithms, and evaluation of clinical biomarkers.
Experience developing or validating bioinformatics pipelines for oncology or clinical diagnostics.
Knowledge of analytical validation concepts, including limit of blank, limit of detection, precision, interference, reproducibility, and robustness.
Experience with Nextflow, Snakemake, Docker, Singularity/Apptainer, cloud computing, or high-performance computing.
Familiarity with regulated software development, design controls, software risk management, and relevant FDA and CLSI guidance.
Experience integrating sequencing workflows with LIMS, laboratory automation platforms, or clinical reporting systems.
Experience supporting clinical studies, regulatory submissions, or commercialization of molecular diagnostic assays.

Key Deliverables and Measures of Success

During the first 6–12 months, the successful candidate is expected to:
Establish or improve a reproducible end-to-end NGS bioinformatics pipeline for the cfDNA-based CRC screening assay.
Implement documented sample-level and sequencing-level quality control metrics and failure criteria.
Develop or optimize the assay-specific molecular signal detection and classification workflow.
Complete a bioinformatics verification and analytical validation plan with predefined acceptance criteria.
Demonstrate reproducibility, robustness, and traceability across representative datasets, runs, and software configurations.
Deliver controlled technical documentation, automated testing, and versioned software releases.
Collaborate with assay development and clinical teams to support performance optimization and future clinical validation.

Core Competencies

Scientific rigor and critical thinking.
Strong programming and statistical problem-solving skills.
Attention to detail and data integrity.
Ability to work with complex, high-dimensional biological datasets.
Effective cross-functional communication.
Ownership of technical deliverables and timelines.
Commitment to reproducible research, software quality, and patient safety.

jobs.title: Research Associate II/Senior Research Associate - Discovery Biology
jobs.description:
Research Associate II / Senior Research Associate - Discovery Biology

Position Summary:

We are seeking a highly creative, passionate, and motivated individual to join us in developing the next generation of CRISPR-based therapeutics. This role is for a Research Associate II / Senior Research Associate I to join the XTID screening team within the Discovery Biology department, where you will support the advancement and scaling of gene-editing platform workflows through high-quality assay execution, optimization, and data generation.
In this position, you will apply strong hands-on expertise in cell-based and molecular assays to support arrayed screening workflows that characterize gene-editing molecules across relevant cell types and therapeutic contexts. You will execute and optimize experiments in plate-based formats, troubleshoot assay workflows, maintain rigorous documentation, and help improve assay robustness, throughput, and reproducibility.
The ideal candidate brings substantial bench experience in mammalian cell culture, plate-based assay execution, molecular biology, and quantitative data analysis. You should be comfortable working independently on defined experiments, organizing and prioritizing day-to-day activities across multiple concurrent projects, and maintaining exceptional attention to detail in sample tracking, documentation, and experimental execution. Success in this role requires strong organizational skills, effective time management, and the ability to consistently deliver high-quality data in a fast-paced environment.
Above all, you should have a genuine passion for developing next-generation CRISPR therapeutics and bring curiosity, scientific rigor, ownership, and a practical problem-solving mindset to help move these technologies from the bench toward the clinic.

Key Duties / Responsibilities:
Support the design, development, optimization, and validation of fit-for-purpose arrayed screening assays in 96-well and 384-well formats to characterize gene-editing molecules across multiple cell types and therapeutic contexts.
Execute high-throughput cell-based and biochemical assays with attention to robustness, reproducibility, and assay quality metrics such as CV, linearity, and signal window.
Produce mRNA via in vitro transcription to generate gene-editing materials for screening, ensuring quality, consistency, and scalability to meet program needs.
Formulate and produce lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for delivery of gene-editing cargo, optimizing formulation and process parameters for potency, reproducibility, and throughput.
Contribute to screening campaigns from experimental setup and sample processing through data capture, quality control, analysis, and interpretation of results.
Communicate experimental results, technical observations, and key findings to the team through presentations, and participation in team discussions.
Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot mammalian cell culture workflows, including immortalized, primary, iPSC-derived, and engineered cell models relevant to therapeutic programs.
Operate, help troubleshoot and refine laboratory automation and liquid-handling workflows to improve screening throughput, consistency, and scalability.
Maintain rigorous documentation in Benchling / LIMS systems and contribute to team best practices for assay robustness, reproducibility, sample tracking, and data quality.
Collaborate cross-functionally with scientists to ensure efficient coordination of experiments, sample processing, and data delivery.
Identify and troubleshoot assay or workflow issues, escalating risks appropriately and contributing practical improvements in performance, cost, and turnaround time.
Maintain strong organizational practices for sample management, reagent inventory, experiment scheduling, and data recording to ensure accurate execution of multiple concurrent projects.

Knowledge Requirements (Background/Skills/Experience):

BS/MS in Biology, Bioengineering, Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, or a related discipline, with typically 4+ years of relevant hands-on experience supporting molecular and cell-based assay workflows
Strong hands-on experience executing and optimizing arrayed assays in plate-based formats (96-/384-well), including quantitative readouts such as NGS-based assays, fluorescence reporters, high-content imaging, ELISA, viability assays, RT-qPCR, or ddPCR.
Strong mammalian cell culture skills, including aseptic technique and experience with immortalized, primary, iPSC-derived, or engineered cell systems.
Working familiarity with core molecular biology methods such as cloning, CRISPR/gene editing, stable cell line generation, RT-qPCR, ddPCR, flow cytometry, and sample preparation for sequencing-based readouts.
Ability to clearly summarize experimental results, flag technical risks, and present decision-enabling data to scientific stakeholders while managing multiple experiments and timelines.
Demonstrated scientific rigor, strong organizational skills, and ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, interdisciplinary team.
Preferred: familiarity with CRISPR therapeutic approaches, laboratory automation and liquid-handling platforms.

jobs.title: Data Analyst, Client Insights
jobs.description:
About RK Media

RK Media is a dynamic organization representing Christian non-profit ministries who use radio, television, podcasts and digital media to reach their audience. As a full-service agency, we serve our ministry partners through the production of top-quality Bible teaching, talk and inspirational broadcasts and podcasts that include strategic fundraising campaigns and promotions. We also serve as the direct liaison between non-profit ministries, the radio stations and other outlets that carry their programs.
RK Media offers a fast-paced, collaborative work environment with potential for both personal and professional growth. We value individuals who wish to make a direct impact in the mission of Christian non-profit ministries through the media industry. We believe that when team members find value and meaning in their work, they experience success and significance. Learn more at rkmedia.co.

The role

We're hiring a data analyst who loves digging into numbers, telling the story behind the numbers, and wants to help ministries understand what's working.

Most of your time (~ 70%) goes to analysis: building and owning reporting for our ministry partners, managing our internal data, and creating cross-ministry benchmarks. Approximately 20% is working with the people behind the requests. That means joining ministry partner calls when needed, finding out why someone is asking for a report, and coming back with more than they asked for.
This is a role for a self-starter. We're looking for someone who takes initiative, solves problems without waiting to be told exactly what to do, brings a "yes, and" attitude, and keeps everyone clear on expectations.

What you'll do

Reporting and analysis (about 70%)

Take over and improve RK's current reporting for ministry partners, including monthly financial reports, station data requests, and social media analytics reports.
Turn one-off client reports into a consistent RK reporting service that partners can rely on.
Fully own RK's cross-ministry benchmarks, with feedback from senior leadership: what "good" looks like by channel, and how each ministry compares.
Build those benchmarks into partner reports, so every ministry understands their experience in a broader context.
Manage and organize RK's internal data: understand what data we have, where it lives, and how to keep it clean and usable.
Present data-backed recommendations across various channels.
As recurring reporting is automated, expect more of your time to shift toward analysis and projects across RK

Client insight (about 20%)

Join client calls as needed alongside the Media Services team.
Dig past the direct request: understand what led to it and where the ministry is headed.
Support the account lead in assessing how a report furthers a ministry’s impact.

Other (about 10%)

Take part in internal team meetings, planning sessions, and company-wide meetings.
Keep building your skills through training, new tools, and learning the ministry media landscape, with RK’s support.
As reporting becomes more automated, take on data projects for other RK teams, such as campaign performance analysis for Digital Marketing, station and affiliate data for Station Relations, or operational and financial analysis for leadership.
Help find other manual processes across RK that could be simplified or automated.
Other duties as assigned.

Who you'll work with

You'll work mainly with the Media Services team, which includes Station Relations and Digital Marketing. Over time there's room to grow into work with all of our teams.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days

You know our ministry partners, their goals, and the reports we provide each of them.
You've taken over the current reporting process, including the quarterly social media reports.
You've mapped what data RK has, where it lives, who owns it, and how it's collected.
You've joined client calls with the Media Services team and built working relationships with the account leads.

By 6 months

You've recommended how to elevate RK's reporting, and we've agreed on a plan.
You've proposed a standard set of metrics and a consistent report format across ministries.
You've set up how client data is organized and protected, so cross-ministry benchmarking can be done responsibly.
Account leads bring you into client conversations because your recommendations go beyond the original request.

By 1 year

Standardized reporting with benchmarks is running as a new service for our ministry partners, allowing them to see how their experience fits within a larger ministry context. 
RK's data and reporting processes are documented and repeatable.
You’ve elevated reporting both internally and for our clients.

What you bring

Required

3–5 years of experience in data analysis, marketing analytics, reporting, or a similar role.
Well versed in using AI tools, such as Claude, in your daily work. 
Comfortable in Excel: pivot tables, lookups, and cleaning and combining messy data. You genuinely enjoy working in spreadsheets.
A track record of presenting findings and recommendations to non-technical audiences.
Clear, concise writing — you can explain what the data means and what to do about it.
Initiative: you find answers and solve problems without needing step-by-step direction.
Strong communication and people skills, including asking good questions and setting clear expectations.
Sound judgment with confidential information.
A general understanding of Christian denominational and theological differences, and empathy for the mission of non-profit ministries.

Preferred

Bachelor's degree, or trade school or certificate training, in a related field.
Experience with nonprofit fundraising, direct response, media buying, or donor data.
Familiarity with radio, podcast, or social media metrics.
Experience with SQL, or with a BI tool such as Power BI or Tableau. Experience setting up or managing a database.
Experience working with multiple clients/accounts at once.

Work environment and pay

In our Westlake Village office Tuesday through Thursday. Monday and Friday you can work from home or come into the office. Hours are 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Pacific.

Description

UCSD Health Sciences is a $1 billion dollar plus organization encompassing 17 academic departments (15 clinical, 2 basic sciences), 2 preacademic/hospital departments, 2 professional schools (School of Medicine and Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences), 2 hospitals, and various other programs and units all dedicated towards fulfilling the Health Sciences missions. The UCSD Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (CMM) is one of two basic science units in the School of Medicine where world-class researchers study fundamental cellular processes and pathways using a variety of techniques from classical genetics and fluorescence microscopy to high throughput genomics, systems biology, and crystallography. Our 37 faculty and over 200 postdoctoral scholars, graduate students, and research staff work on the cutting edge of biology, cutting across fields from basic biochemistry and genetics to genomics, systems biology and stem cell biology. The faculty also play a major role in medical and graduate student training, providing educational and programmatic offerings that span several disciplines and provide diversity to meet the interests of a broad spectrum of students and scholars. The diverse mix of ages, backgrounds, and talents creates a robust work environment with challenging career opportunities and a commitment to continued growth potential. We constantly seek to recruit highly motivated, technologically advanced, and deeply interested individuals who are ready to become a part of our dynamic research and educational environment.

The Institute for Network Medicine [www.inetmed.ucsd.edu] is striving towards a goal of understanding the fundamental principles that allow eukaryotic cells to do their business, i.e., iteratively sense, decide, act, and learn/adapt. We hypothesize that they do so through an ad hoc molecular interaction network whose architectural principles and computational rules are like those used in the layered communication systems in the engineering world. These rules enable noise reduction, error minimization, shielding and encapsulation of breakdowns, control of delays and state explosion, etc. Success in decoding these fundamental rules should not only enable us to complete and 'clean up' the existing incomplete and messy biological networks, but also use these networks for simulating and predicting cell behavior. This will usher a new era in network-based diagnostic tools and network-resetting therapeutics for major diseases. On the flip side, knowing how a cell autonomously carries out its business will provide insights into designing new kinds of self-organizing networks (SON) and provide a novel paradigm (beyond artificial neural networks) for developing Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Under supervision, the incumbent will perform standard repetitive laboratory procedures including biochemistry and molecular biology assays, cell biology, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence, and immunoblotting to meet the needs of several ongoing research projects, providing ideas and rationale to help improve tests that are unsatisfactory. The Research Associate will perform general lab duties under guidance including but not limited to entering requests in lab ordering system, organizing, maintaining lab supplies, handling, and disposing biohazardous and chemical waste in an EH&S approved manner as well as maintenance, calibration, and operation of laboratory equipment. Performs other duties as assigned.

Theoretical knowledge of molecular and cellular biology or closely related field.
Working knowledge of DNA techniques.
Lab experience, knowledge and understanding of sterile techniques and mammalian cell culture practices. Knowledge and experience with numerous types of laboratory equipment related to uses, maintenance, and repair. Ability to learn new laboratory procedures quickly.
Knowledge of various computer software, hardware, standard office equipment and lab equipment
Acute attention to detail, resourceful, capable of handling the changing needs of the research lab.
Working knowledge and experience in bacteriology and bacteria cell competency.
Ability to use mathematical skills to analyze and develop statistical data.
Knowledge and experience in sterile cell culture techniques for culture of mammalian cells.
Experience performing repetitive and specialized laboratory experimental procedures. Experience following experimental protocols.
Strong organization skills. Attention to detail; self motivated. Ability to learn quickly and adopt lessons from one learning episode to similar situations. Ability to perform a variety of tasks in an extremely fast-paced environment. Use of good judgement relating to constantly changing priorities. Ability to work as part of a large, diverse group.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience using microscopy to perform experiments.

SPECIAL CONDITIONS

Employment is subject to a criminal background check.
Occasional evenings and weekends may be required.
Work in environment where biological (including infectious agents and blood borne pathogens) and chemical hazards are present.

Follow established test methods, standard operating procedures, specifications, and acceptance criteria.
Evaluate test results and promptly escalate unusual results, discrepancies, or potential quality issues.
Accurately document observations, activities, and test results in accordance with Good Documentation Practices.

Assist with investigations by gathering information, documenting findings, and preparing investigation summaries.
Perform routine operation, cleaning, and maintenance of laboratory equipment.
Verify equipment readiness and calibration status before use.
Assemble test parts, consumables, or other components as required.
Support troubleshooting activities, assay validation, and other special laboratory projects as assigned.
Collaborate cross-functionally to support product release and resolve testing or documentation issues.
Follow current Good Manufacturing Practices and Truvian’s Quality Management System, policies, procedures, and training requirements.
Help maintain a clean, organized, and safe laboratory environment.
Assist with restocking laboratory supplies and maintaining inventory.
Participate in process and operational improvement activities.
Manage multiple responsibilities and adapt to changing priorities.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, or a related scientific discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Minimum of 3 years of Quality Control, laboratory testing, manufacturing testing, or other directly related experience.
Familiarity with laboratory or quality testing methods.
Experience following standard operating procedures, test methods, work instructions, or established laboratory protocols.
Experience documenting laboratory observations and test results accurately and completely.
Strong organizational and prioritization skills.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to carefully follow written instructions.
Ability to recognize defects, discrepancies, and unusual test results.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a team.
Ability to manage multiple assignments and complete tasks by established deadlines.
Flexibility to respond to changing operational demands and priorities.
Ability to identify and distinguish between colors.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a medical device, diagnostics, biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or other regulated environment.
Experience working under current Good Manufacturing Practices.
Familiarity with Quality Management Systems and Good Documentation Practices.
Experience operating automated laboratory instruments or diagnostic platforms.
Experience with reagent, consumable, in-process, or finished-product testing.
Exposure to nonconformance investigations, troubleshooting, product release, or assay validation.

The benchmark requires a scientific degree with a minimum of 3 years of experience, while also allowing equivalent experience. Lift and move up to 5 pounds repeatedly and safely.

Bold thinkers, breakthrough makers: Join a team of curious minds who challenge the status quo, create what’s next in science and technology, and have the freedom to turn daring ideas into real breakthroughs.

The Center for Advanced Light Microscopy and Electron Microscopy (CALM-EM), housed within our Department of Research Pathology, is seeking an experienced and dedicated Scientist 3, Microscopy Specialist
to join our centralized microscopy hub. In this role, you will deliver world-class technical expertise in optical microscopy and advanced quantitative image analysis to propel scientific discovery and drug development initiatives across Genentech Research and Early Development (gRED). You will partner directly with project teams across diverse therapeutic areas—providing end-to-end guidance spanning experimental design, modality selection, sample preparation, and downstream computational image analysis.

Provide high-level technical consultation and experimental design across advanced imaging modalities, including confocal, live-cell imaging, organoids/complex in vitro models, tissue clearing, light sheet microscopy, and high-content screening (HCS) assays.
Collaborate cross-functionally with CALM-EM team members and gRED research scientists to design, optimize, and execute tailored imaging assays that address critical drug discovery questions.
Lead user onboarding and hands-on technical training on advanced light microscopy instrumentation, serving as a primary technical resource across the broader scientific community.
Develop, implement, and maintain robust digital image analysis workflows and computational pipelines using scientific software to extract meaningful quantitative metrics from complex imaging datasets.
Manage, maintain, and troubleshoot advanced microscope hardware platforms independently and in partnership with external service vendors.
Prepare quantitative imaging data and multi-dimensional visualizations for presentation in high-impact scientific publications, patent applications, and project team reviews.
Balance and prioritize multiple concurrent research projects in a dynamic, fast-paced discovery research environment.

Who You Are

You hold Ph.D. in a scientific discipline utilizing advanced optical microscopy as a primary research methodology with 3+ years of dedicated, hands-on microscopy core or shared resource experience will also be considered. Masters level candidates with 5+ years relevant experience may be considered.
Demonstrate a proven track record of teaching, mentoring, and onboarding users across advanced light microscopy hardware platforms and associated acquisition software.
Bring hands-on working knowledge of advanced microscopy instrumentation, such as laser scanning confocal, spinning disk confocal, light sheet, or high-content imaging systems.
Possess practical experience developing and applying quantitative digital image analysis workflows using platforms such as FIJI/ImageJ, Imaris, CellPose, or related computational tools.
Exhibit strong interpersonal and communication skills with a proven history of collaborative, team-oriented problem solving across diverse scientific teams.
Display exceptional time management, prioritization, and organizational skills with an established ability to rapidly adapt to and adopt emerging imaging platforms and methodologies.

Preferred

Direct prior experience operating within an academic or industry microscopy core facility or serving as the lead imaging technical specialist for a multidisciplinary research department.
Specialized expertise in multi-modal imaging workflows (e.g., correlative optical and electron microscopy, combined live-cell and high-content imaging,).
Experience with automated high-content screening hardware and software (e.g., ImageXpress Micro, IncuCyte, MetaXpress, InCarta).
Advanced scripting and automation skills for image analysis workflows Practical familiarity with 3D imaging techniques including complex in vitro models, NAMs or tissue clearing methodologies and 3D volumetric light sheet imaging acquisitions.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Data Science & Analytics - Global Marketing Services
jobs.description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

About the Job

Visa is a world leader in payments and technology, with over 259 billion payments transactions flowing safely between consumers, merchants, financial institutions, and government entities in more than 200 countries and territories each year. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable, and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses, and economies to thrive while driven by a common purpose – to uplift everyone, everywhere, by being the best way to pay and be paid.

Make an impact with a purpose-driven industry leader. Join us today and experience Life at Visa.

Job Description

Visa is searching for a Senior Manager, Data Science & Analytics - Global Marketing Services to build and own the data and intelligence layer for Marketing Services’ AI solutions and agents. This role spans analytics and data science, combining deep analytical skills with AI data readiness expertise to convert VisaNet transaction data, client profile data, and market context into ranked, actionable growth opportunities. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable conducting exploratory analysis to frame business opportunities and building the predictive models and data structures that make those opportunities actionable at scale.

This role will be part of the AI Transformation team within the Global Marketing Services organization. The Senior Manager will assess, structure, and prepare data assets for AI consumption, design the analytical frameworks and models that power opportunity detection and sizing, and own the opportunity scoring framework that surfaces ranked recommendations to business development teams. The role requires someone who can evaluate data readiness across multiple sources, identify gaps and quality issues, define the data preparation and enrichment needed to make content AI-ready, and then build the models that turn that data into intelligence.

The role requires a leader who can work across the full spectrum, from data assessment and readiness through analysis, model development, and stakeholder communication. It demands comfort navigating raw, messy, and fragmented data environments, building the structure and pipelines that make data usable by AI systems, and translating analytical outputs into clear business recommendations.

Reporting to the Senior Director, AI Transformation, Global Marketing Services, this leader will partner with Visa Consulting & Analytics (VCA), Global Insights & Analytics, Marketing Services regional teams, Visa Technology teams, and cross-functional partners across Finance, Legal, Privacy, Risk, and Compliance to build data solutions for the intelligence layer and ensure data foundations are AI-ready.

Key Responsibilities

Own the data and intelligence layer for AI solutions and agents: Design and build the end-to-end analytical solution that converts raw data into ranked, actionable client growth opportunities. Define the model architecture, feature engineering approach, and scoring methodology.
Assess and prepare data for AI readiness: Evaluate data assets across VisaNet transaction data, client CRM and profile data, Visa Analytics Platform, and market intelligence sources. Identify data gaps, quality issues, and structural barriers. Define the preparation, enrichment, and structuring needed to make data consumable by AI models and agents.
Build statistical and prediction models: Develop models for opportunity detection, root cause attribution, and opportunity sizing. Apply techniques spanning regression, classification, clustering, and machine learning to identify patterns across transaction data, client profiles, and market signals.
Own the opportunity scoring framework: Design and maintain the scoring framework that ranks and surfaces actionable opportunities for business development teams. Define score calibration, refresh cadences, and output formats that business users can act on.
Co-own data integration with VisaNet and enterprise data sources: Partner with Visa Technology, VCA, and Insights and Analytics teams to integrate VisaNet transaction data, Visa Analytics Platform data, and client CRM and profile data into the intelligence layer. Define data requirements, validate data quality, and ensure pipelines are reliable and scalable.
Ensure model documentation, validation, and governance: Partner with Responsible AI, Legal, Risk, Privacy, and Compliance teams to ensure models meet governance, regulatory, and Visa standards. Maintain comprehensive model documentation, validation records, and performance monitoring.
Communicate insights and recommendations to stakeholders: Translate analytical findings and model outputs into clear, actionable recommendations for business stakeholders. Present opportunity intelligence to Marketing Services, VCA, and regional teams in formats that drive commercial decision-making.

No visa sponsorship or relocation assistance will be provided for this position

Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

8 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s degree, or at least 6 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree, such as a Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics, or a related quantitative field.
Experience spanning both analytics and data science, including exploratory data analysis, business intelligence, statistical modeling, and building predictive models in a production environment.
Experience assessing data readiness for AI initiatives, including evaluating data quality, identifying gaps, defining data preparation requirements, and structuring data for AI consumption.
Proficiency in Python, R, SQL, or similar languages for data analysis and statistical modeling, including experience with libraries such as scikit-learn, pandas, etc.
Experience working with large-scale structured and unstructured datasets across multiple data sources, including transaction data, CRM data, and market intelligence.
Experience building scoring frameworks, recommendation systems, or opportunity detection models that translate data into ranked, actionable business outputs.
Experience with data governance, metadata management, data cataloging, or building data readiness frameworks for AI programs.
Strong ability to translate complex analytical findings into clear business recommendations and stakeholder communications.

Preferred Qualifications

10 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree, or at least 8 years of work experience with an Advanced Degree, such as a Master’s or PhD.
Experience with LLM-based solutions, generative AI, or natural language processing techniques applied to business intelligence or recommendation systems.
Familiarity with cloud data platforms and distributed computing frameworks.
Experience with model governance, documentation, and validation frameworks.
Familiarity with payments, banking, fintechs, or card products is a plus.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to operate in ambiguity, build structure in white space, and drive action across stakeholders and business units.

Additional Information

This role requires a leader who combines deep technical expertise with business acumen. The ideal candidate will have strong relationship-building skills, excellent written and verbal communication, personal presence, and the ability to clearly communicate complex analytical concepts and model outputs to both technical and business audiences. jobs.description:
We’re ALTEN Technology USA, an engineering company helping clients bring groundbreaking ideas to life—from advancing space exploration and life-saving medical devices to building autonomous electric vehicles. With 3,000+ experts across North America, we partner with leading companies in aerospace, medical devices, robotics, automotive, commercial vehicles, EVs, rail, and more.
As part of the global ALTEN Group—57,000+ engineers in 30 countries—we deliver across the entire product development cycle, from consulting to full project outsourcing.
When you join ALTEN Technology USA, you’ll collaborate on some of the world’s toughest engineering challenges, supported by mentorship, career growth opportunities, and comprehensive benefits. We take pride in fostering a culture where employees feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow.
Workplace:
On-site, 5 days per week
Location:
San Francisco, CA (Dogpatch neighborhood) 
Salary:
$90,000-$105,000
We are seeking a Robotics Lab Technician to be the versatile builder at the center of our prototype lab. You'll move fluidly between precision assembly, wiring and electrical integration, system bring-up, and acceptance testing to take robots from a kit of parts to a validated, working system. You'll install software and read logs, bridging the gap between hardware and software during bring-up, and you’ll troubleshoot and solve integration issues during testing and validation. We're looking for someone careful with their hands, organized about documentation, and comfortable collaborating with mechanical, electrical, controls, and software engineers in a fast-iterating environment.
Key Job Responsibilities

    • Assemble electromechanical robotic systems and subsystems (actuators, gearboxes, sensors, vision systems, wiring harnesses, PCBAs) from mechanical drawings, schematics, and work instructions, following torque specs and assembly procedures.
    • Kit parts against the BOM, stage hardware and fixtures, and set up assembly jigs and alignment rigs for each build.
    • Build first articles from prototype kits, provide engineering with actionable build feedback (DFx), and execute rework and engineering change orders (ECOs) as designs iterate.
    • Fabricate, route, and terminate wiring harnesses to documented pinouts with proper strain relief, bend radius management, and cable routing for moving assemblies.
    • Perform pre-power-on electrical verification (continuity, pinout, insulation, polarity) and board-level integration under ESD discipline.
    • Maintain build records, travelers, inspection checklists, and non-conformance reports (NCRs) ensuring full traceability. Redline and improve work instructions with each build.
    • Bring up newly built assemblies, verify actuator and sensor function, and run acceptance testing and performance characterization using standard and custom test equipment.
    • Use git and the Linux command line to install, configure, and run test and calibration software on robots; track software versions across the fleet.
    • Read logs and source code well enough to localize problems and provide engineering with actionable triage reports.
    • Collaborate with engineering to isolate integration issues, narrow root cause across mechanical, electrical, and software domains, and drive corrective actions into work instructions.
    • Keep the lab safe, organized, and ESD-compliant; track tooling, consumables, and inventory.
    • Drive continuous improvement and support prototype-to-production transitions by developing SOPs, assembly aids, and training materials.

Required Qualifications

    • 3-5+ years of hands-on experience assembling and testing electromechanical systems such as robotics hardware, precision mechatronic assemblies, aerospace/automotive hardware, or electronics assembly in a lab, prototype, or manufacturing environment.
    • Able to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and written work instructions to build and test complex hardware.
    • Proficient with hand and torque tools, basic crimping and soldering, and steady work with small fasteners and connectors.
    • Demonstrated ability to perform functional and acceptance testing using standard test equipment such as multimeters, oscilloscopes, and power supplies.
    • Experience performing quality inspections and maintaining detailed build records, including assembly travelers, inspection checklists, and non-conformance documentation.
    • Comfortable at a Linux command line running scripts, and willing to grow those skills.
    • Knowledge of ESD handling procedures and lab safety protocols for working with high-voltage electronics and heavy mechanical assemblies.
    • Clear communication, careful record-keeping, and safe work habits.

Preferred Qualifications

    • Associate's degree or technical certification in Electronics Technology, Mechatronics, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent hands-on experience.
    • Experience assembling and testing robotic systems with high degrees of freedom, including familiarity with actuators, force/torque sensors, IMUs, encoders, and vision/camera systems.
    • Wiring harness fabrication experience including building to a pinout, connector assembly, and cable routing on moving assemblies.
    • Background in a robotics research lab, hardware startup, aerospace, or advanced electromechanical environment where rapid prototyping and tight engineering collaboration are standard.
    • Mechatronics training/coursework or electromechanical troubleshooting experience.
    • Some scripting ability (Python or bash) for test and calibration; basic familiarity with git, Docker, or networking.
    • Experience with ERP systems, MES, PLM, or lab management tools for tracking inventory, build status, component traceability, and hardware/software revision control.
Work Environment & Physical Requirements

    • On-site lab role; standing, bench work, and hands-on assembly for extended periods, including work in awkward positions and tight spaces.
    • Fine motor precision and close-vision work with small fasteners, connectors, and board-level components.
    • Lifting and maneuvering heavy robotic assemblies; use of required PPE.
    • Work around high-voltage electronics, powered actuators, and moving machinery.

Salary Range

    • $90,000-$105,000
    • The actual salary offered is dependent on various factors including, but not limited to, location, the candidate’s combination of job-related knowledge, qualifications, skills, education, training, and experience

Multiply Labs
is a robotics company on a mission to solve a significant bottleneck in modern medicine: the manufacturing of life-saving advanced biologics, from gene and cell therapies to antibodies and more.

Today, these therapies are produced through manual, labor-intensive processes. Costs are extremely high—often $500K-$2M per patient—limiting access to only a small fraction of those who need them.

As product complexity increases and the cost of failure and scientific labor rises, the industry is shifting toward automation. Robotics and AI are making automated biologics manufacturing feasible, reliable, and economically scalable.

We believe the future of biomanufacturing is robotic—closed, automated, and scalable—ensuring critical therapeutics are accessible to every patient who needs them.

Great people, meaningful work, and a team that genuinely believes in what we're building.

Come build the world’s best robots—and help make life-saving therapies accessible to all.

Lycia Therapeutics (Nasdaq: LYCA) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company using its proprietary lysosomal targeting chimera (LYTAC) platform to discover and develop therapeutics that degrade extracellular and membrane-bound proteins. These proteins drive a wide range of difficult-to-treat diseases, including autoimmune, inflammatory, and allergic conditions. Lycia was established in 2019 in collaboration with academic founder and Nobel Laureate Carolyn Bertozzi, Ph.D., professor of chemistry and HHMI investigator at Stanford University. In October 2026, Lycia completed an initial public offering, and its common stock now trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “LYCA.” Lycia is headquartered in South San Francisco.

Visit https://lyciatx.com/ for more information.

The Role:

The Clinical Research Associate is responsible for monitoring clinical trial sites to ensure that studies are conducted ethically, safely, and in full compliance with the trial protocol, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines, and applicable regulatory requirements. The CRA will act as the primary bridge between Lycia and the clinical research sites.

Key Responsibilities

In-house

Site Management and Support: Assist with investigator recruitment, site selection activities, study startup, and close-out tasks. Provide ongoing operational support to investigative sites via phone and email
Document & Regulatory Tracking: Collect, review, and track essential regulatory documents and Investigator Site Files (ISF) to ensure audit and inspection readiness. Maintain the electronic Trial Master File (eTMF)
Data and Query Management: Review data points and findings within Electronic Data Capture (EDC) systems. Write, track, and follow up on clinical data queries with site personnel
Remote Monitoring & Collaboration: Support traveling CRAs by conducting remote monitoring activities, tracking site key performance indicators (KPIs), and updating Clinical Trial Management Systems (CTMS)
Compliance & Escalation: Ensure trial conduct aligns with Good Clinical Practice (GCP), International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, FDA/local regulations, and study-specific standard operating procedures (SOPs). Escalate site non-compliance or protocol deviations to Clinical Operations Management

Clinical Research Site Oversight

Site Monitoring Visits: Conduct qualification, site initiation, interim monitoring, and close-out visits in person or via remote monitoring tools
Data Verification: Review source documents, medical records, and Case Report Forms (CRFs/EDC) to verify data accuracy, completeness, and integrity
Protocol & Regulatory Compliance: Ensure site staff adhere to the study protocol, ICH-GCP guidelines, FDA regulations, and standard operating procedures (SOPs)
Issue Escalation: Identify, document, and track protocol deviations, adverse events, and data queries, working with site investigators to implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA)
Investigational Product (IP) Management: Check accountability, storage, dispensing, and return of investigational drugs or devices at study sites
Documentation & Reporting: Maintain comprehensive Trial Master File (TMF) documents and write detailed monitoring visit reports (trip reports) within required timelines
Site Support & Training: Train investigators and clinical research coordinators (CRCs) on study protocols, electronic data capture systems, and regulatory requirements

Required Qualifications & Skills

Education: Bachelor’s or advanced degree in a life science, nursing, pharmacy, or health-related field
Experience: 2+ years of clinical research experience (e.g., prior experience as a Clinical Research Coordinator, clinical data assistant, or junior CRA)
Regulatory Knowledge: Deep understanding of ICH-GCP guidelines, FDA regulations, EU, and local ethics/IRB processes
Technical Skills: Proficiency with Electronic Data Capture (EDC) systems, Clinical Trial Management Systems (CTMS), and remote data review tools
Core Competencies:
Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
Effective verbal and written communication
High level of organization and time management

We’re here for one reason and one reason only – to cure cancer. Every moment is dedicated to developing treatments and every action moves us one step closer to our goal. We’ve made incredible scientific breakthroughs and our pioneering personalized CAR T-cell therapies have changed the paradigm. But we're not finished yet.

Join Kite, as we make even bigger advances in cancer therapies, and help shape where our business and medical science goes next.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfill their aspirations. Join Kite and help create more tomorrows.

Job Description

The Research Scientist I, Attribute Sciences Computational Biology, AI & Scientific Informatics will be responsible for accelerating adoption of artificial intelligence, agentic workflows, and advanced analytics across Analytical Development. This role will combine expertise in biological sciences, bioinformatics, data science, and generative AI to build AI-powered tools that improve scientific productivity, knowledge management, data accessibility, and decision-making to guide process development and product knowledge of viral vector-based gene delivery platforms and T cell therapies. In this role, the research scientist will partner closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Manufacturing Sciences, Digital/IT, and Data Science teams to develop AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, workflow automations, and predictive models that leverage laboratory, process, and knowledge-management data. Ideal candidates would possess strong communications skills with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, curiosity about emerging AI capabilities, ability to understand scientific workflows and needs and translate those into working products, and software/programming skills sufficient to independently build and deploy AI and data science solutions.

Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

AI Agent Development:

Design and deploy Copilot, Copilot Studio, or similar AI agents supporting scientific workflows.
Develop RAG-based knowledge assistants that integrate information from various enterprise knowledge sources.
Create agents that: answer scientific questions, retrieve and summarize technical information, generate draft reports, support investigations, assist with study planning and scheduling, support operational excellence.
Evaluate AI tool accuracy, groundedness, hallucination rates, performance and citation quality.

Bioinformatics & Scientific Computing

Analyze multi-modal biological datasets including NGS, omics, vector characterization, cell therapy process data.
Develop pipelines for automated data processing and visualization.

Knowledge Management and Automation

Support digital transformation initiatives involving electronic lab notebook and data lake infrastructure.
Automate repetitive scientific workflows and documentation tasks.
Build solutions that improve data discoverability and scientific knowledge reuse.

Cross-functional Collaboration

Work directly with scientists, IT and digital teams to identify opportunities where AI can improve productivity.
Translate scientific business problems into technical AI solutions.
Train stakeholders on effective use of AI tools and prompt engineering techniques.

Applied Data Science

Build predictive and descriptive models supporting process development and manufacturing.
Develop statistical tools for identifying relationships between process parameters and manufacturing outcomes.
Design dashboards and decision-support systems.

Basic Qualifications

Ph.D. in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Data Science, Computer Science or related discipline OR
Masters' Degree and 4+ years experience; OR
Bachelor's Degree and 6+ years experience; OR
Associates Degree and 8+ years experience; OR
High School Degree and 10+year experience

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of experience in AI, including experience with LLMs, vector databases, agentic frameworks, prompt engineering, and evaluation frameworks.
Knowledge of advanced statistical techniques/concepts and proficiency in statistical computer languages (i.e. R, Python, SQL) to analyze data and draw insights from large data sets.
Knowledge of cell biology, cancer biology, and/or immunology.
Experience performing bioinformatics (NGS analysis) and/or data analytics with high dimensional data to drive business solutions.
Experience with machine learning, statistical modeling, experimental design and data visualization.
Ability to think critically and demonstrate troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
Highly collaborative with excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills
Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and willing to accept temporary responsibilities outside of initial job description
Comfortable in a dynamic, fast-paced environment

About The Role

What if your voice could help teach AI how to handle a real phone call to a hospital or clinic? We're looking for native Korean speakers based in the United States to hold natural spoken conversations with an AI healthcare receptionist, then evaluate how well it listens, responds, and takes action.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff: Python, TypeScript & LLM Agent Evals | San Francisco On-site | Up to $400K + Equity
jobs.description:
"Good morning! And in case I don't see ya..." Truman Burbank, The Truman Show

Every AI agent thinks it lives in a perfect little world. Clean prompts, polite users, happy paths only. Sunny Seahaven, every day.

Your job is to sail out to the horizon and find where the sky is painted on.

THE OPPORTUNITY

A well-funded, seed-stage San Francisco startup is building the trust layer for AI agents, making sure they're safe and reliable before they're handed real responsibility in high-stakes industries. It's backed by top-tier AI investors, and the team is small, senior and stacked with people who have built companies before.

These agents are already in production at some of the most widely used AI products on the planet. Somebody has to find out how they break before the real world does. That's you.

This is a senior individual contributor seat with a rare mix: hardcore engineering, frontier AI research turned into product, and real contact with the customer teams building the agents everyone uses.

WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO

Own red-team engagements end to end on major customers' agents: scoping, recon, attack execution, remediation and sign-off
Sharpen the core engine that powers every evaluation the company runs
Turn bleeding-edge adversarial research into repeatable product
Be the palate for eval quality. If a test is weak, you send it back to the kitchen
Automate your own workflow with agents, because doing it twice by hand is a crime
Work out how to test the next wave, like computer-use agents, before anyone has a playbook for them

THE TECH YOU'LL LIVE IN

Python is the engine room.
Evals, attack pipelines and grading logic all run here, so you'll write production-grade Python fluently. That means async code that fires thousands of conversations at an agent in parallel, clean typed data models, solid tests, and the judgment to know when a script needs to grow up into a system.

TypeScript is where the work meets people.
Customers need to see results, findings and reports, and you'll ship that user-facing side yourself. If you're strong in React and Node, typed end to end and built with the same care as the backend, you'll feel at home. This one is non-negotiable: they want engineers who already write both languages well, not people planning to learn one.

LLMs and agents are your raw material.
You should be comfortable with the major model APIs, tool and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval, multi-turn agent loops, and protocols like MCP that connect agents to the outside world. Hands-on time with agent frameworks and orchestration is a big plus.

Evals are the craft.
Designing test suites that actually catch failures. Using LLM-as-judge grading without fooling yourself. Building golden datasets, generating synthetic adversarial scenarios at scale, and proving whether a fix really worked or just moved the problem somewhere else.

Adversarial AI is the fun bit.
Prompt injection, jailbreaks, tool misuse, data leakage, harmful outputs, and agents going off-script under multi-turn pressure. If you've read the latest red-teaming papers and itched to try them on a real production system, this is the job.

Integration is the glue.
Every customer's agent is different, so you'll work across SDKs, API endpoints, webhooks and the occasional ugly legacy system, often getting a new integration running in days. Browser automation and computer-use tooling will matter more and more as agents start clicking around the web on their own.

MUST HAVE

Real production experience shipping user-facing features, not just backend plumbing
Strong, hands-on Python and TypeScript. Both, not "happy to pick it up"
5+ years as a software engineer, owning high-stakes technical work from start to finish
A career arc that keeps climbing in title and scope
A CS degree or equivalent technical background
Agentic AI tools baked into how you work every day
Clear communication with engineers and non-technical stakeholders alike
On-site in San Francisco, 5 days a week

BONUS POINTS

Founder, founding engineer or early startup hire (extra credit if it was VC-backed)
Customer-facing experience
Hands-on with agentic frameworks and evals
A visible spike: a side project people talk about, open source, writing, a standout company, or a bold career move that shows real conviction

PROBABLY NOT FOR YOU IF

Your whole career has been at big tech with no early-stage time
You're an engineering manager who's drifted away from writing code
You're after a management or director title. This is a senior IC seat, and that's the point

WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH YOUR TIME

You'll work on one of the biggest open problems in AI: knowing whether an agent can be trusted before it does something that matters
Your work lands in production with customers whose agents are used by millions
Small team, huge surface area, and a direct line to the founders
The category is brand new, so the playbook you write could become the industry standard

THE PACKAGE

Up to $400K base + meaningful equity
On-site in SF with a small, sharp, very senior team
Visa transfers welcome (OPT, H-1B transfers)
A quick, focused process: a short vibe check, a coding round, then an onsite covering systems design, algorithms and a deep-dive on AI evals

HOW TO APPLY

Hit apply with your resume and answer the screening questions. Big Wave Digital is recruiting this role on behalf of our client, and every application is read by a real person.

The agentic engineering group works alongside the Physics AI research in the wider Science organisation.
