jobs.title: R&D Technician, Robotics Hardware
jobs.description:
FieldAI’s Irvine team is where embodied AI meets real robots, real sensors, and real field deployments. Based in the heart of Southern California’s robotics ecosystem, we build risk-aware, reliable, field-ready AI systems that solve the hardest problems in robotics and unlock the full potential of embodied intelligence. If you want your work to ship, get tested on hardware, and improve through real deployments, Irvine is the place. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-only architectures, combining rigorous engineering with learning systems proven in globally deployed solutions that deliver results today and get better every time our robots run in the field.

Who are We?

Field AI is transforming how robots interact with the real world. We are building risk-aware, reliable, and field-ready AI systems that address the most complex challenges in robotics, unlocking the full potential of embodied intelligence. We go beyond typical data-driven approaches or pure transformer-based architectures, and are charting a new course, with already-globally-deployed solutions delivering real-world results and rapidly improving models through real-field applications.

Learn more at https://fieldai.com.

About the Job

As an R&D Technician, you will be a hands-on contributor responsible for assembling, integrating, and validating Field AI’s sensing and compute payloads. You will build electro-mechanical subsystems, integrate sensors and embedded compute platforms, perform harnessing and power system checks, support functional testing, and ensure every payload is field-ready and reliable. This role bridges mechanical assembly, electrical integration, and practical system-level debugging. You will support both prototype development and production workflows while working closely with engineers to improve build processes and increase system reliability.  

What You’ll Get To Do

1. Payload Assembly & Integration

Assemble perception payloads including LiDAR, cameras, IMUs, GPS receivers, and auxiliary sensors using engineering drawings and build instructions

Install and integrate CPU/GPU compute modules, carrier boards, and microcontroller-based subsystems

Build and route wire harnesses for power, high-speed data, synchronization, and control

Install mounts, enclosures, gaskets, seals, thermal components, and structural hardware

2. Electrical, Power, and Communication Bring-Up

Perform continuity checks, grounding/EMI checks, and power-rail validation

Assist in bring-up of Linux- or ROS2-based embedded compute systems

Validate communication links across Ethernet, USB, CAN, GMSL, and other interfaces

Verify correct connectorization, pinouts, and harness strain-relief practices

3. System Testing & Quality Assurance

Run functional tests including sensor bring-up, calibration checks, compute boot/health tests, and network verification

Document test results, deviations, rework, and repair actions with high accuracy

Support environmental, vibration, mechanical alignment, and thermal characterization tests led by hardware engineers

Conduct inspections for workmanship quality, mechanical stability, and electrical safety

4. Debugging & Continuous Improvement

Diagnose wiring faults, mechanical misalignments, intermittent communication issues, thermal faults, and other integration failures

Work closely with electrical, mechanical, and compute engineers to root-cause issues and improve build processes

Provide feedback on assembly workflows, documentation clarity, and opportunities to streamline production

5. Field & Operations Support

Prepare, stage, and service payloads for real-world deployment

Support integration and troubleshooting activities during lab tests, field trials, and live demonstrations

Perform rapid repairs and reconfigurations in dynamic testing environments

What You Have

2+ years of hands-on technician experience in robotics, aerospace, electronics, automotive, or related electro-mechanical assembly environments

Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, torque drivers, and basic machine-shop tools

Ability to read and follow wiring diagrams, mechanical drawings, and assembly instructions

Experience building wire harnesses and working with low-voltage electrical systems

Familiarity with embedded compute systems, sensors, or robotics hardware

Strong attention to detail, documentation discipline, and ability to deliver reliable assemblies

Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and work in workshop, lab, or field environments

What Will Set You Apart

Experience working with perception systems such as LiDAR, cameras, radar, or IMUs

Familiarity with Linux, ROS2, or embedded system bring-up workflows

Soldering, crimping, or IPC-certified workmanship skills

Understanding of thermal management, weather sealing, EMI/EMC basics, and ruggedized mechanical design

Experience supporting prototype builds, rapid iteration cycles, or field test deployments

Ability to design or suggest simple fixtures or jigs to improve assembly and repeatability

Experience assembling complex electro-mechanical systems, especially robotics, drones, or ruggedized field hardware

Our salary range is generous and we consider each individual’s background and experience when determining final compensation. Base pay may vary based on role scope, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and the Irvine, California market.

Why Join FieldAI in Irvine?

In Irvine, you will work where the robots are. Our local team builds and tests systems on real hardware with real sensors, then ships them to operate in unstructured, previously unknown environments around the world. We are solving one of robotics’ hardest challenges: reliable deployment outside the lab. Our Field Foundational Models™ raise the bar for perception, planning, localization, and manipulation, with an emphasis on explainability and safety for real-world use.

You will collaborate with a world-class team that thrives on creativity, resilience, and bold thinking. We bring deep experience from organizations such as DeepMind, NASA JPL, Boston Dynamics, NVIDIA, Amazon, Tesla Autopilot, Cruise, Zoox, Toyota Research Institute, and SpaceX, along with a track record of field deployments and strong performance in DARPA challenge segments.

Be Part of the Next Robotics Revolution

We are looking for builders who want their work to leave the whiteboard and show up on robots. If you enjoy tackling tough, uncharted questions and working across disciplines, you will find your people here. Our teams span AI, software, robotics engineering, product, field deployment, and technical communication, all focused on shipping systems that perform in the real world.

Our headquarters is in Irvine, and we partner closely with teams there as well as colleagues across the US and around the world. Join us in Southern California and help define what dependable, field-ready autonomy looks like.

We value diverse perspectives and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We evaluate candidates and employees based on merit, qualifications, and performance, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally protected status.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

Contribute positively to organizing and maintaining the R&D lab

BS or MS in Bioengineering, Molecular and Cell Biology, Microbiology, Biophysics, Biochemistry, or related field

Great attention to detail

Start-up experience
Knowledge of medical genetics

Working alongside brilliant, kind, passionate and dedicated colleagues, in an empowering environment, toward a global vision, striving for a future in which transformative molecular diagnostics can help millions of patients
Open, transparent culture that includes weekly Town Hall meetings
The ability to indirectly or directly change the lives of hundreds of thousands patients
Multiple medical benefit options; employee premiums paid 100% of select plans, dependents covered up to 80%
Extremely generous Family Bonding Leave for eligible employees (16 weeks, paid at 100%)
Supplemental fertility benefits coverage
Retirement savings program including a 4% Company match
Increase paid time off with increased tenure
Latest and greatest hardware (laptop, lab equipment, facilities)
Daily on-site lunches provided from top eateries
A variety of perks on campus (state of the art gym, restaurant)
Free on-site EV charging (compatible with all EVs, including Tesla)

At BillionToOne, we are proud to offer a combination of a (1) base pay range (actual amount offered is based on experience and salary/equity options split that the candidate chooses), (2) generous equity options offering, (3) corporate bonus program, on top of (4) industry leading company benefits (free healthcare options, 401k match, very generous fully paid parental leave, etc.).

The base salary range for this role is $76,155 - $87,034. This position is eligible for an annual bonus and receives a new hire equity grant of up to $20,000 at grant value, vesting over four years, plus annual equity refresh grants equal in value to the new hire grant. Together, the total four-year value of base, target bonus, and equity is up to approximately $433,000. We also offer competitive medical and dental coverage and a 401(k) with company match.

BillionToOne is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

For more information about how we protect your information, we encourage you to review our Privacy Policy.

BillionToOne is a next-generation molecular diagnostics company on a mission to make powerful, accurate diagnostic tests accessible to everyone. Our revolutionary QCT molecular counting technology enhances disease detection resolution by over a thousandfold using cell-free DNA,a breakthrough that has already transformed the lives of over half a million patients worldwide.

Our Impact

Unity Complete™
is the only non-invasive prenatal screen capable of assessing fetal risk for both common recessive conditions and aneuploidies from a single maternal blood sample.

Unity Confirm™
enables non-invasive confirmation for high-risk screening results through the capture of intact circulating fetal cells using BillionToOne’s Fetal Cell Capture™ Technology.

Our Northstar®
liquid biopsy test uniquely combines treatment selection with real-time monitoring, giving oncologists unprecedented precision in cancer care.

Our Growth

From $0 to $400M+ annualized revenue run-rate in just 6 years. In 2025, we completed one of the most successful IPOs for a medical diagnostics company, building on nearly $400M in private funding,including our $130M Series D in 2024 and backed by world-class investors including Hummingbird, Adams Street Partners, Neuberger Berman, Baillie Gifford, and Premji Invest.

Our Recognition

Forbes named us one of America's Best Startup Employers for 2025
and we're Great Place to Work certified
, with 100% of our people willing to go the extra mile, even as we've scaled to over 700 employees.

Our Future

Headquartered in Menlo Park with facilities in Union City, CA, and a new lab opening in Austin, TX in 2027, we're continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible in molecular diagnostics. We're just getting started.

jobs.title: Clinical/HC Research Associate - Department of Radiology
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The University of Iowa Health Care Department of Radiology is seeking an experienced and motivated MRI professional to join the University of Iowa MRI Research Facility, one of the nation's premier academic MRI research programs. This is a unique opportunity to work in a world-class imaging environment that supports groundbreaking research across neuroscience, psychiatry, oncology, cardiology, musculoskeletal imaging, and advanced MRI technology development. The successful candidate will collaborate with leading faculty, physicians, physicists, engineers, and scientists who are advancing the frontiers of imaging science and precision medicine.

The University of Iowa MRI Research Facility houses state-of-the-art MRI technology that ranks among the most advanced academic imaging resources in the world. Researchers have access to sophisticated imaging systems and specialized capabilities available at only a limited number of institutions worldwide. These resources support innovative investigations ranging from basic science discovery to clinical translation and novel imaging method development.

This position offers a rare opportunity to move beyond routine clinical imaging and become an integral member of multidisciplinary research teams conducting studies that shape the future of MRI and improve patient care. The individual in this role will help lead facility operations, support cutting-edge research studies, develop advanced imaging protocols, and contribute to expanding the impact of one of the Midwest's leading imaging research programs.

Position Responsibilities

Research/Clinical Activities

Functions as a technical expert in MRI research; Performs clinical/health research activities related to MRI
Conducts complex research experiments in human and animal MRI imaging
Prepares and participates in monitoring visits; may perform activities such as patient assessments and review of medical history
Assures compliance with study protocol
Prepares research and grant proposals; Explores grant opportunities for research facility
Coordinates research teams and documents for grant submission
Maintains SMRT membership to keep current on cutting edge MRI techniques and changes in the field
Develops, troubleshoots, and formulates protocols and hypotheses in a specialized field/discipline
Maintains research website and online scheduler; Helps maintain information on the facility website to communicate with the outside users as well as document internal procedures
Facilitates technologist support and equipment use for research studies
Works with University investigators and research coordinators to develop and submit new MRI research projects

Protocol Development And Study Responsibilities

Reviews literature in the development of new imaging protocols for human and animal MRI imaging
Assists in protocol development and provide input into descriptions of routine MRI research procedures
Develops study materials
Liaison with external funding agencies related to supporting facility research.

Subject Recruitment and Enrollment

Screens, recruits, and obtains informed consent for clinical trials/studies
Assists principal investigator to determine subject eligibility
Schedules trial related procedures and visits
Assists with subject assessments during study participation

Data Collection and Monitoring

Investigates and performs critical analysis of current MRI data and MRI literature to advise principal investigators on the proper approach and techniques to achieve optimal research outcomes
Monitors and tracks research protocols for data collection
Ensures proper archiving of research images, monitor compliance with University, state and federal regulations
Assists with determining validity of data obtained.

Regulatory Guidelines and Documents

Assists with preparation of manuscripts for publication and/or presentation at national meetings.
Develops and performs quality assurance procedures
Monitors compliance with contract and grant terms in accordance with University policies and state and federal regulations.
Develops, implements, and oversees local program guidelines
Tracks and ensures IRB/IACUC compliance for facility users
Prepares documents for investigator IRB submission
Communicates with University departments to assure compliance and adherence to University, state, and federal policies
Collects and maintains regulatory documents from subjects and assist in preparation of required regulatory forms and documentation according to protocol
Reports any reportable events to appropriate part

Leadership

Adhere to institutional policies and guidelines
Provides supervision, oversight and direction for the students, staff and users of the research facility
Provides secondary supervision, support, and management of research technologists
Develops and organizes training sessions for student users of facility equipment, disseminate training materials.

Financial Responsibility

Creates and monitors budgets, establish fiscal controls, prepare fund allocations to comply with internal and sponsor deadlines
Oversees and generates monthly billing to facility users
Analyzes, monitors, and reports financial data, information and reports
Reconciles income and expenditures
Assists in budget development and management of resources/supplies for study
Contribute to identification of increased cost/inefficient spending and cost containment measures

The information contained herein is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities required of individuals performing this job.

University of Iowa Health Care — recognized as one of the best hospitals in the United States—is Iowa's only comprehensive academic medical center and a regional referral center. Each day more than 12,000 employees, students, and volunteers work together to provide safe, quality health care and excellent service for our patients. Simply stated, our mission is: Changing Medicine. Changing Lives. ®

For more information about Why Iowa? Click here

jobs.description:
Senior Manager, Data Analyst – Compliance Risk

About The Company

Information Technology Senior Management Forum is committed to advancing technology leadership and fostering inclusive, effective practices across the profession. In this role, you will work in a data-centered environment where rigorous analysis, thoughtful collaboration, and responsible risk management inform business decisions. You will partner with senior leaders and specialists across Compliance, Technology, Product, Legal, and Risk Management to develop approaches that help identify and mitigate potential compliance risks.

About The Role

As Senior Manager, Data Analyst – Compliance Risk, you will lead analytical work and help shape the current and future strategy for Compliance Testing. You will apply data analysis, statistical thinking, and technical judgment to complex business challenges, translating findings into practical recommendations for decision-makers. The role connects technical teams, including engineers, analysts, and data scientists, with non-technical partners such as Legal, Compliance, and executive leaders.

This position is suited to a confident analytical leader who can work independently, guide multiple projects, and communicate clearly in a fast-paced environment. You will also support the development of team members while helping the organization assess emerging analytical tools, opportunities, and risks.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative discipline, such as Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, or Computer Science, plus at least seven years of data analytics experience; or a master’s degree in a quantitative discipline plus at least five years of data analytics experience. The required degree must be completed by the scheduled start date.
At least five years of professional data analysis experience.
At least five years of experience leading and developing with open-source data technologies.
At least two years of people-management experience.
Strong problem-solving, conceptual thinking, communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills.
Preferred: a master’s degree or PhD in Finance, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, or a related field.
Preferred: experience with statistical or econometric analysis and modeling, large data sets, model validation, financial services, data governance, and predictive analytics.

Responsibilities

Set and advance the analytical and tooling strategy for current and future Compliance Testing.
Plan and execute analytical projects that help identify, assess, and mitigate compliance risks.
Serve as the primary liaison between technical teams and business, legal, compliance, and executive stakeholders.
Understand technical issues in analytical tools and assess associated risks, limitations, and opportunities.
Research industry practices and independently evaluate and prototype emerging analytical tools.
Present findings clearly through concise reports, presentations, and verbal briefings tailored to different audiences.
Use ongoing learning, collaboration, and training to develop effective solutions to business problems.
Coach and mentor junior colleagues, supporting their professional growth and analytical capabilities.

Benefits

This role is eligible for performance-based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonuses and/or long-term incentives, subject to the applicable plan. The organization offers a comprehensive benefits package supporting health, financial security, and overall well-being. Eligibility and available benefits may vary according to employment status and management level.

Posted annual salary ranges for this role are $182,500–$208,300 in Plano, Texas; $200,700–$229,100 in McLean, Virginia; and $182,500–$208,300 in Richmond, Virginia. Compensation for other work locations will follow the applicable location range. The final salary offer will be confirmed in the offer letter. Qualified applicants may be considered for employment authorization sponsorship.

Equal Opportunity

Information Technology Senior Management Forum is an equal opportunity employer committed to fair and inclusive employment practices. Employment decisions are made without unlawful discrimination and in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Qualified applicants with criminal histories will be considered consistent with applicable fair-chance requirements. Reasonable accommodations are available for applicants who need them during the application process. Applications are expected to be accepted for at least five business days. No agencies, please.

jobs.description:
Arup’s purpose, shared values and collaborative approach has set us apart for over 80 years, guiding how we shape a better world. At Arup, you belong to an extraordinary collective where we encourage individuality to thrive. Our culture is energetic, collaborative, and open. We value self-motivated and driven people who have a positive impact on those around them. Share your passion and experience in a global culture that believes your potential to achieve is endless.

Our West geography is looking for an experienced Senior Civil Engineer
who is skilled in developing hydrology & hydraulic (H&H) models to play a vital role on a variety of exciting site development and coastal resiliency projects. This position is based in San Francisco or Los Angeles.

You’ll Love This Position If

You want the freedom to push boundaries and the space to explore your career as you take responsibility for helping us shape a better world. Arup still follows the business principles our founder, Ove Arup, set out in his Key Speech.
You desire a high degree of autonomy and responsibility.
You enjoy working directly with clients and project teams across the Americas and beyond.
You thrive in a truly multi-disciplinary environment, with an awareness of the interconnectedness of your decisions on other disciplines.
You see yourself as an emerging leader in this field.

The Opportunity

Lead development of H&H models to inform a variety of project types including coastal resilience planning and design, drainage infrastructure for site development projects, and flood risk assessments.
Lead the design of utilities, roadways, drainage, green infrastructure and other key civil elements for a variety of site development projects throughout the country.
Serve as civil technical lead on site due diligence and master planning projects for regional and global hyperscale clients, including test fit design, grading analysis, and drainage.
Work with the local agencies to understand their land use and permit processes.
Coordinate with associated disciplines including SMEP, architecture and landscape architecture, geotechnical engineering, transportation planning, urban planning, environmental engineering, and cost engineering.
Perform construction phase engineering support and site supervision.
Develop and deepen relationships with existing and potential clients and project collaborators.
Mentor team members and nurture their professional development.

Is this role right for you?

Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering; Master’s degree preferred.
Professional Engineering license preferred.
6+ years of experience in civil engineering/site development.
Strong knowledge of core civil engineering fundamentals such as hydrologic and hydraulic analysis, low impact development, 3-D utility design, grading and earthwork, roadway and geometric alignments, and accessibility standards.
Highly proficient with H&H modeling software such as InfoWorks-ICM, HEC-HMS and other analysis software.
Highly proficient with AutoCAD Civil 3D and other civil engineering design and analysis software.
Experience coordinating project delivery and interfacing with project owners, contractors, and outside consultants.
A commitment to sustainable design practices.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with proven ability to build consensus among clients and teammates alike.

Notable Current Clients

Caltrans Climate Resilient Corridor Study
City of South San Francisco Shoreline Protection Plan
Major (confidential) hyperscale data center projects across North America
California High Speed Rail Stations

Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling members to share in the results of our collective efforts.

Benefits that Work - At Arup, we have a comprehensive and valuable benefits program that works for our employees and their families while keeping costs low. These benefits provide health and welfare security for you as well as paid time off for rest and renewal. As a member of Arup, everyone shares in our success through a global profit share scheme (payments are dependent on the firm’s financial performance). Our Global Profit Share Plan (paid bi-annually) provides an opportunity for you to share in the success of the Firm. As a valued employee of Arup, you can also choose to participate in our 401(k) plan with up to 10% company match to help you save for your future

Flexible Working - We believe that flexible arrangements create a more inclusive way of working that supports our diversity and the wellbeing of our people. Options for alternative schedules and the ability to work outside of the office for a portion of your workweek are available

Hiring Range - The good faith base salary hiring range for this job if performed in San Francisco is $120,400 to $145,000 per year. This range is commensurate with experience, educational background, and skill level. Benefits are not included in the base salary. Please note hiring ranges for candidates performing work outside of San Francisco will differ.

Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup.

Our application process

We will be reviewing our candidates for this position on a rolling basis. Once you have applied you will be evaluated and potentially moved on to the next round, at which point a member of the talent resourcing team will reach out to you directly.

jobs.title: Traffic/Transportation Engineering Specialist
jobs.description:
STV is seeking a motivated and technically strong Traffic/Transportation Engineering Specialist – Express Lanes and Tolling
to support a Bay Area public agency's express lanes program. This role is well suited for a mid-level traffic or transportation engineer with strong data analytics skills who wants to build hands-on experience in tolling, express lanes operations, and ITS
. Prior tolling experience is a plus but not required.

This is a full-time, on-site assignment embedded with the client agency's tolling team in San Jose, five days per week, for a minimum of 12 months. Before starting at the client site, the selected candidate will complete a few weeks of STV onboarding and tolling training. Throughout the assignment, they will receive ongoing mentoring and technical support from STV's Tolling and Mobility Technologies team. Final placement includes an interview with the client agency.

This is a strong learning and growth opportunity. You will work as a core member of the agency's tolling team, so you will get broad, hands-on exposure across planning, operations, performance reporting, and board-level work, and see how a public owner runs an express lanes program from the inside. There is also potential to extend the assignment beyond 12 months based on mutual fit.

The Engineering Specialist will support express lanes planning, implementation, operations, and performance reporting, coordinating with agency staff, Caltrans, CHP, and toll system vendors. The engineer will remain an STV employee, with STV benefits, long-term career growth, and a path to continue on STV's tolling and mobility technology work after the assignment, including future opportunities to grow into business development and client pursuits.

Key Responsibilities

Tolling and Managed Lane Operations

Support upcoming express lanes phases from planning through implementation and opening.
Support day-to-day express lanes operations in coordination with agency staff, operators, and vendors.
Assist with management and oversight of tolling technology assets, including roadside equipment, back-office systems, and communications infrastructure.
Coordinate with Caltrans, CHP, and toll system and back-office vendors on operations, enforcement, and system issues, including oversight and contract compliance for service providers.
Assist the agency with operational readiness, transitioning to operations, and ongoing operations support for new, existing, or expanding express lanes facilities.
Support incident response, operational troubleshooting, and other coordination.

Pricing, Traffic Management, and Operational Policies

Support tolling, congestion pricing, and managed lanes studies, including feasibility analyses, alternatives evaluations, and operational assessments, with an emphasis on policy, operations, and technology.
Assist with development and evaluation of traffic management and pricing practices, including lane configurations, pricing frameworks, operational business rules, enforcement approaches, and customer experience considerations.
Support monitoring and adjustment of toll policies and system performance measures related to reliability, throughput, compliance, enforcement, customer experience, and equity outcomes.
Support equity and policy analyses related to tolling and pricing programs, including assessment of user impacts, mitigation strategies, and technology‑enabled discounts or exemptions.

Data, Tools, and Analytics

Analyze traffic, toll transaction, and operational datasets to support planning, policy, and system design decisions.
Apply industry‑standard tools such as Excel, GIS, Tableau/Power BI, and outputs from traffic or operations models to inform decision‑making.
Support development of dashboards, summaries, and visualizations that communicate system performance and policy outcomes.
Prepare ongoing performance monitoring reports on traffic, transactions, and violations.

ITS, Technology, and Systems Integration

Coordinate with ITS and mobility technology specialists on toll system architecture, including roadside equipment, back‑office systems, communications, and data flows.
Support analyses related to all‑electronic tolling technologies, interoperability standards, enforcement systems, and operational readiness.
Support integration of tolling systems with broader ITS, TSMO, and digital roadway initiatives.
Evaluate technology pilots and system enhancements related to tolling, enforcement, and/or customer experience.

Collaboration and Coordination

Work as an embedded member of the agency's tolling team, coordinating with planners, traffic engineers, ITS specialists, and policy staff as needed.
Work day to day under agency direction, reporting to STV's Northern California Regional Director for supervision, technical support, and oversight.
Participate in meetings with Caltrans, CHP, and regional transportation partners.
Prepare staff reports, board and committee materials, technical memoranda, and presentations for agency staff, elected officials, and public stakeholders.

Professional Growth

Stay informed on evolving tolling, congestion pricing, ITS, and mobility technology practices nationwide.
With STV support, participate in professional organizations and industry forums such as IBTTA, TRB, ITS America, AASHTO, and related technology‑focused working groups.
Over time, build business development experience with STV's tolling and Mobility Technologies practice, such as proposals and client pursuits, outside the scope of the client assignment.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Transportation Engineering, or a related field, required.
Master’s degree preferred.

Experience

7–10 years of experience in traffic or transportation engineering, transportation planning, or related analytical roles.
Demonstrated experience analyzing traffic, transaction, or performance data for public‑sector clients.
Experience working on California or Western U.S. transportation projects is strongly preferred.

Skills and Competencies

Strong analytical, problem‑solving, and organizational skills.
Familiarity with tolling and congestion pricing concepts, including system operations, pricing frameworks, enforcement, and performance metrics.
Working knowledge of ITS concepts, toll systems, and technology‑enabled transportation solutions.
Strong data analytics skills, including advanced Excel and Power BI. Proficiency with PowerPoint; Tableau or GIS experience is a plus.
Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly through writing, graphics, and presentations.
Ability to work independently in a client office, using sound judgment and knowing when to draw on STV support.
Strong interpersonal skills and professional judgment in a client-facing environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting tolling, express lanes, or congestion pricing programs for public‑sector clients (e.g., DOTs, toll authorities, MPOs), particularly with strong ITS components.
Experience working for, or embedded with, a public transportation agency.
Familiarity with Bay Area transportation partners such as MTC, Caltrans District 4, and CHP.
Familiarity with equity‑focused transportation analysis and public‑facing implementation considerations.
Experience coordinating with multidisciplinary teams on large, complex transportation and mobility programs.

jobs.title: Lab Technician
jobs.description:
**Organization**: Rise Research

**Location**: Santa Clara, CA (in-person at Biocurious Lab, Santa Clara)

**Commitment:** Part-time, 3 hours per session, 2-3 times a week

**About the Role**

Rise Research is building a hands-on lab experiment program for high school students, combining real, in-person lab work with online mentor-led research training. Students run structured experiments (starting with Biofuel from Biomass) at a partner BSL-1 teaching lab, supported by a student portal and remote mentors.

The Lab Technician supervises every session on site: setting up the lab, overseeing students at the bench, checking their work at each stage, and keeping accurate records.

**What You'll Do**

* Prepare the lab before each session: set up benches, equipment, reagents, and consumables according to the experiment's equipment checklist (e.g., balances, pH meters, incubator/shaker, hotplate/stirrer, autoclave, and basic glassware)
* Take attendance and confirm every student has completed their safety sign-off and is wearing proper PPE (lab coat, gloves, goggles) before they begin
* Deliver the BSL-1 safety and lab orientation at the start of each experiment weekend
* Directly supervise all hands-on work. Students never use the biosafety cabinet, autoclave, hotplate, or incubator/shaker without supervision
* Guide students through each stage of the protocol, review the notes and photos they submit through the portal, and approve (or ask them to redo) each stage before they move on
* Check that raw data is recorded before any calculations are made, and flag unusual readings, skipped timepoints, instrument drift, or possible contamination
* Add lab technician notes to each student's stage history in the portal, and raise or resolve discrepancies as they come up
* Manage biological waste according to protocol, including autoclaving before disposal, signing off the waste log, and disinfecting benches and equipment after each session
* Maintain lab records: equipment checkout, inventory, consumables, and maintenance logs, and report shortages or equipment faults to the Head of Labs
* Stay in touch with remote mentors, who can see student notes and message you about individual students
* Share feedback on protocols, timing, and equipment so the program keeps improving

**Who You Are**

* Master’s degree (or equivalent hands-on experience) in a life sciences discipline such as biology, biotechnology, microbiology, biochemistry, or a closely related field
* Hands-on experience working in a BSL-1 laboratory, with solid knowledge of biosafety practices, aseptic technique, PPE, and biological waste handling
* Comfortable using common lab equipment such as pipettes, analytical balances, pH meters, incubators/shakers, autoclaves, and basic microscopes
* Patient, clear communicator who can explain technique to students who may be new to lab work
* Organized and detail-oriented, with accurate record-keeping
* Comfortable using a web-based portal to log notes, approvals, and records
* Prior experience teaching, tutoring, or mentoring students is a plus

**What We Offer**

* A part-time role
* The chance to be part of the founding team of a new student lab program
* Clear protocols, a purpose-built portal, and remote mentors to support you
* A collaborative, mission-driven team focused on giving students real research experience

If any questions, reach out to careers@riseglobaleducation.com

Pay: $50.00 - $80.00 per hour

Expected hours: 6.0 – 12.0 per week

Work Location: In person

*Reassignment Applicants*: Eligible Reassignment clients should contact their Disability Counselor for assistance.

**DESCRIPTION**
===============

The Center for Perinatal Discovery (CPD) is a collaboration between the Departments of Pathology, Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Reproductive Sciences, and Pediatrics. The CPD was established to promote research into perinatal health, including the health of both mothers and babies. To this end, the CPD is conducting research studies into both maternal and neonatal health. Clinical data and biospecimens are being collected at several clinical sites from normal and high-risk pregnancies, with neonatal/pediatric follow-up. The CPD is also involved in community educational activities which promote maternal and child health.

Under supervision of the PI, the incumbent will perform complex studies with molecular and cellular methods using human ex vivo model systems and single-cell high-dimensional proteomics techniques. They will perform research activities such as handling of primary cells and tissues of human and mouse origin, performing suspension and imaging mass and flow cytometry (incl. cell sorting), antibody conjugation and titration, immuno fluorescence analysis, and quantitative (real- time) PCR to assist with contributions to the laboratory and its collaborators. They will also prepare media, buffers, and solutions as needed, and maintain an antibody library. Data processing and statistical analysis as needed.

The position will coordinate human sample collection and transport with clinical and research partners and organize and execute processing, stimulation, and biobanking of samples. They will assist with other related functions as required. This individual will assist in complex research on reproductive immunology, neuroimmunology of pregnancy, and prediction and prevention of human pregnancy complications. The incumbent will assist with experimental procedures requiring ingenuity, resourcefulness, and adaptability to special and changing needs of research.

The position will also manage our biohazard use authorization and serve as our area safety coordinator, provide routine laboratory equipment maintenance, order and maintain supplies and equipment and oversee undergraduate part-time lab aides whose duties include washing glassware and making buffers for the lab.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**
==========================

* Theoretical knowledge of molecular biology techniques and genetics typically acquired through Bachelor degree in biology or related field, and/or relevant lab experience.
* Demonstrated knowledge in cytometry, ideally mass cytometry, but flow and spectral flow cytometry are equally relevant. Spatial proteomics experience/theoretical knowledge preferred but not required.
* Experience in human sample processing protocols and sterile technique.
* Demonstrated ability to follow written and verbal protocols, techniques, and instructions
* Demonstrated excellent communication and interpersonal skills over a wide range of situations and individuals needed to interact professionally and effectively in the work environment in person, on the phone, and in writing to a diverse population; including persons from foreign countries, the business community, academicians, students and staff with a high degree of diplomacy, mature judgment, tact, and flexibility.
* Knowledge of proper formats, grammar, and spelling in English and proofreading ability sufficient to compose, edit, and publish professional correspondence as well as effectively and accurately document research procedures. Ability to read, comprehend, discuss, and present research materials.
* Demonstrated experience with the operation of a personal computer and software applications, such as Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Access), Photoshop, Acrobat.
* Willingness to learn new theory, techniques, and tasks and share knowledge.
* Demonstrated experience making decisions, analyzing situations, problem solving, and initiating action for laboratory maintenance.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
============================

* Knowledge of bio, chemical, and radiation safety techniques and practices. Demonstrated ability to follow established Safety and Biohazardous Material Guidelines and implement measures to ensure compliance and maintain associated records.
* Demonstrated organizational skills to order and maintain lab reagents and supplies, and keep accurate lab records and computer files.

* Experience with mouse experiments and husbandry.

* Employees can qualify for free medical coverage in our Health Investment Plan (HIP) PPO medical plan in the next calendar year.
* An excellent retirement savings plan with a high employer contribution.
* Tuition reimbursement, the Freedom 2 Save student debt program, and FreeU education benefit - an affordable and convenient path to getting a bachelor’s degree.
* A company recognized as a great place to work in dozens of countries worldwide and named one of the most admired companies in the world by Fortune.
* A company that is recognized as one of the best big companies to work for as well as the best place to work for diversity, working mothers, female executives, and scientists.

**The Opportunity**

The CRA II will assist in the clinical execution and management of all aspects of assigned clinical studies. This includes but not limited to planning and implementation of clinical studies from concept to clinical study report per timelines and quality standards.

This position will be based in our Alameda, CA office.

**What You’ll Work On**

* Conduct single or multi-center medical device clinical studies.
* Perform study site visits (SQV, SIV, IMV, COV), generate monitoring trip reports, and track resolution of action items.
* Participate in study start up activities.
* Responsible for shipping study devices and supplies to clinical sites and performing study device accountability.
* Manage clinical monitoring activities and overall site management ensuring compliance to the Study Protocol, Good Clinical Practices (GCPs), ICH guidelines, Federal Regulations, department procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Responsible for assisting senior staff in planning study conduct, designing case report forms (CRFs), conducting User Acceptance Testing (UAT), Contract Research Organization (CRO) selection and management, selection and training of investigator sites, planning and running study meetings, evaluation, selection and training of new study investigators and writing and assembling submissions.
* Maintain and audit Trial Master File to ensure inspection readiness.
* Perform review of clinical data listings for completeness and accuracy, and escalate issues to the Clinical Operations Manager as needed.
* Participate in cross-functional clinical team(s) in the planning and execution of clinical trials.
* Proactively and effectively communicate the status of clinical studies to management.
* Ensures quality delivery of study deliverables within agreed budgets and timelines.
* Participate in the interim and final reviews of study data in preparation of regulatory submissions.
* Involved in the preparation of all applicable documents required for the conduct of the study (such as Trial Master File (TMF), Clinical Protocols and Reports).
* May interact with RA/QA in responding to audits and FDA inquiries.

**Required Qualifications**

* B.S. degree in life sciences or equivalent with minimum 5 years of clinical research experience.
* Must have 2+ years of relevant experience in site monitoring.
* Experience in conducting medical device and/or in-vitro diagnostics studies preferred. Pharmaceutical background may also be considered.
* Must be able to travel 30-50%.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Demonstrated excellence in teamwork, shared mindset for success, stellar interpersonal and communication skills including building rapport with team members, peers, and management.
* Solid understanding and demonstrated experience of the clinical trial process including study design and conduct; clinical data management systems; clinical trial management systems; data analysis; and data reporting and interpretation.
* Must have a demonstrated ability to solve problems with innovative solutions along with strong project management and organizational skills to deliver projects on time and on budget.
* Able to manage numerous projects/conflicting priorities, and to be flexible when priorities change.
* Working knowledge of GCP, Clinical and Regulatory Affairs.
* Proficient with Microsoft Suite.

The base pay for this position is $81,500.00 – $141,300.00. In specific locations, the pay range may vary from the range posted.

jobs.title: Clinical Research Assistant
jobs.description:
**Clinical Research Assistant (CRA) I Los Angeles, CA (On-Site) | Full-Time**

**About**

CalNeuro Research Group is an independently owned clinical research site based in Los Angeles, committed to advancing new therapies for disorders of the central nervous system (CNS), including major depression, PTSD, social anxiety, and more. For over 30 years, we’ve partnered with leading global pharmaceutical companies to accelerate the development of FDA-approved treatments. Our work is grounded in a deep passion for science, unwavering ethical standards, and a patient-first approach. We’re seeking individuals who share our mission to bring meaningful change to the field of mental health through clinical research.

**Job Title:**

**Clinical Research Assistant (CRA)**

**Job Description:**

As a Clinical Research Assistant at CalNeuro Research Group, you’ll help with the day-to-day work of running clinical trials that focus on mental health and brain-related conditions. This role is a great fit for someone who enjoys working in a busy environment, pays close attention to details, and wants to grow in the clinical research field.

You’ll help make sure study data is accurate, follow study rules and regulations, and support our participants with care and professionalism. This is also a great opportunity to gain hands-on experience by working on different types of clinical trials. You’ll learn how each study works and what’s required—giving you valuable skills for building a strong career in clinical research.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Identify, screen, recruit, and schedule eligible participants for clinical trials while supporting long-term retention through relationship-building and clear communication.
* Collect and process lab samples and procedures in accordance with study protocols, including blood draws, urine samples, drug/pregnancy tests, ECGs, and other assessments.
* Perform medical procedures as delegated by the Principal Investigator (PI), including vital signs, height/weight measurements, ECGs, EEGs, and similar assessments.
* Accurately enter data from source documents into study-provided eCRFs/CRFs and resolve data queries in collaboration with study monitors and management teams.
* Work closely with Clinical Research Coordinators to support data accuracy and protocol compliance across multiple studies, contributing to overall quality assurance.
* Maintain regulatory compliance, including up-to-date IRB approvals, staff training records, and FDA-required documentation.
* Manage and organize subject binders and assist in preparation for monitoring visits and audits.
* Monitor and manage inventory of study-related supplies, interfacing with vendors as needed to reorder and maintain readiness.
* Adhere to Good Clinical Practice (GCP) guidelines and ensure all research activities comply with HIPAA and applicable regulations for participant confidentiality and data integrity.
* Assist with site-level data tracking and analysis, including metrics on patient recruitment and daily clinical operations.

**Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Science, Psychology, Nursing, or related field - required
* Phlebotomy certification – required
* Minimum 6 months to 1 year of experience in a clinical or research setting – *preferred*
* Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and HIPAA regulations
* Strong organizational and time management skills with excellent attention to detail
* Ability to work independently as well as part of a collaborative team
* Comfortable working with participants and handling sensitive health information professionally and empathetically
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook); familiarity with eCRF, CTMS, or eSource platforms is a plus
* Adaptability and eagerness to learn in a fast-paced, regulatory-compliant environment
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Must be available for on-site work in Los Angeles – remote work is not available

Pay: $27.00 - $30.00 per hour

* 401(k)
* Free parking
* Paid time off

* Bachelor's (Required)

jobs.title: Electrical Engineer (AI Trainer)
jobs.description:
Why This Role Matters

When AI gets the details wrong in your field, real people pay for it. The people who know the work best have to be the ones training these models. You’re not being replaced by AI. You’re making sure it’s used accurately and safely.

How You'll Contribute

Design challenging, realistic electrical and electronics engineering problems based on professional practice, such as circuit specifications, control-loop stabilization, and power-stage sizing.
Run engineering problems through frontier AI models and evaluate outputs against professional engineering standards.
Compare model versions using identical prompts and identify which performs better and where each falls short.
Critique model-generated derivations, schematics, component selections, and calculations, documenting the reasoning behind evaluations.
Identify and document specific failures, including incorrect assumptions, sign or unit errors, unphysical results, invalid topologies, fabricated datasheet values, and off-brief interpretations.
Contribute expertise across applicable areas including analog, RF and mixed-signal circuits, electromagnetics and antennas, control and systems, devices and materials, signal processing, photonics, and power and energy systems.

What Makes You a Great Fit

Fluency in English at a native or bilingual level.
At least 2 years of industry experience in circuit or electronics engineering.
Background in electrical engineering, electronics engineering, or a closely related discipline.
Strong command of circuit analysis, design tradeoffs, and component-level and system-level decision-making.
Ability to clearly explain why an engineering answer is incorrect, not only identify that it is incorrect.
Comfort using AI tools or ability to learn them quickly.
A current, in-progress, or completed Bachelor's degree is preferred but not required.
Must be located in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, or the United States.
Ability to receive payment through PayPal.

jobs.description:
Note: By applying to this position you will have an opportunity to share your preferred working location from the following: Mountain View, CA, USA; New York, NY, USA
. Minimum qualifications:

Master's degree in Finance, Economics, quantitative fields, or equivalent practical experience.
5 years of institutional finance experience in investigative, modeling-intensive roles (Quantitative Trading, Corporate Finance, or Alternative Asset Management).
Experience with frontier LLMs, coding agents, or AI evaluation pipelines, including structured prompts and tool-use traces.
Experience identifying flaws in AI-generated financial models, backtests, or memos, and translating these errors into generalizable grading rules.

Preferred qualifications:

CFA, CPA, MBA, JD, Master of Financial Engineering (MFE), or an advanced quantitative degree in Finance, Computer Science, Math, or Economics.
Background building benchmarks, rubrics, or SFT/RLHF pipelines at AI labs, fintechs, or quantitative teams.
Domain-specific excellence in Python and SQL (Quant) or advanced, macro-free spreadsheet software and Python/SQL (Alternative Asset Management/Corporate Finance).
Familiarity with market data feeds, SEC EDGAR, Capital IQ, FactSet, Bloomberg, ERP/EPM, and tax/audit platforms.

About The Job

DeepMind is building frontier financial reasoning and agentic capabilities across Gemini and our enterprise agent harnesses. Moving AI from a generalist research assistant to an agent that can autonomously complete financial workflows requiresmore than raw pre-training scale - it requires deep domain mechanics embedded directly into how models are post-trained, how agent harnesses and tools are architected, and how evaluations measure real-world finance.

As a Finance Subject Matter Experts (SME), you will work with models, evaluations, and post-training data in the following three Finance domains -

Quantitative Trading
Corporate Finance - specifically with experience across FP&A, Audit and Tax
Alternative Asset Management

Unlike traditional advisory roles that stop at high-level feedback or static prompt writing, you will sit directly in the model development loop alongside Research Scientists, Post-Training Engineers, and Product Managers. You will prioritize differentiated financial workflows, design end-to-end financial benchmarks, construct atomic and deterministic grading rubrics, diagnose multi-step agent trajectories, repair near-miss model reasoning traces, design verifiable reward signals, and co-build domain-specific agent skills.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $207000 - $300000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Evaluate the AI's step-by-step process across calculations, ledger searches, and code to pinpoint quantitative or accounting errors.
Create realistic financial tasks (e.g., valuations, backtests, audits) and write "gold-standard" examples to correct model near-misses.
Build complex prompts featuring vague instructions, GAAP/non-GAAP differences, and conflicting estimates to test AI resilience.
Create pass/fail checklists for deliverables and draft deceptive, polished-but-wrong answers to stress-test automated graders.
Teach the AI to efficiently use core financial tools (SQL, etc) and categorize error patterns into reusable templates.

Design challenging, realistic healthcare operations scenarios based on day-to-day professional practice, including prompts and supporting de-identified or constructed files such as encounter documentation, claim forms, remittance advice, payer policies, and correspondence.

jobs.description:
JLSa2, founded in 2024, is a well-resourced, seed-stage venture backed company located in South San Francisco currently developing a robust pipeline of novel protein-drug conjugate therapies to better address human metabolic diseases and other non-oncology related diseases.

We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Research Associate I to support our drug discovery programs through compound management, sample preparation, and routine protein science activities. This role will be primarily responsible for receiving, tracking, preparing, storing, and distributing research materials used across internal studies. The Research Associate will help ensure that project teams have appropriately prepared and well-documented materials available when needed.

The position will also provide hands-on support for routine protein science and biochemistry workflows. This is an ideal opportunity for an early-career scientist who enjoys laboratory work, organization, and supporting multiple scientific teams in a fast-paced biotechnology environment.

Key Responsibilities

Compound and Sample Management

Maintain accurate inventory and tracking of research compounds and biological materials, including quantities, concentrations, storage locations, and material usage.
Receive incoming research materials and ensure they are properly documented, labeled, stored, and entered into appropriate inventory systems.
Prepare stock solutions, working solutions, and aliquots for use by internal research teams.
Perform calculations related to concentrations, dilutions, and material requirements.
Coordinate distribution of research materials while maintaining accurate records of material usage.
Monitor inventory levels and proactively identify materials that require replenishment.
Maintain organized freezer, refrigerator, and laboratory storage systems.
Help establish and improve systems for sample requests, aliquoting, tracking, and distribution.
Maintain material traceability, including identity, concentration, formulation, storage conditions, and handling history where appropriate.

Protein Science and Biochemistry Support

Assist with routine protein sample preparation and characterization.
Perform protein concentration measurements and sample normalization.
Prepare buffers, reagents, and solutions used in protein science workflows.
Support routine analytical techniques such as SDS-PAGE, chromatography sample preparation, and protein quantification.
Assist with protein purification and sample-processing activities, including buffer exchange, dialysis, filtration, concentration, and aliquoting.
Support preparation of samples for biochemical and biophysical characterization.
Maintain laboratory equipment and ensure commonly used reagents and consumables are adequately stocked.
Follow established protocols and contribute to continuous improvement of laboratory procedures.

Documentation and Laboratory Operations

Maintain complete and accurate records in electronic laboratory notebooks, inventory systems, and other internal databases.
Ensure samples are appropriately labeled and traceable throughout their lifecycle.
Coordinate with scientists across multiple functions to understand upcoming material requirements and ensure samples are available when needed.
Support general laboratory organization and contribute to a safe, efficient, and collaborative laboratory environment.
Assist with additional laboratory activities as needed to support research programs.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Biochemistry, Chemistry, Biology, Biotechnology, or a related scientific discipline.
0–2 years of relevant laboratory experience in biotechnology, pharmaceutical research, or an academic laboratory.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to manage and accurately track large numbers of research samples.
Comfortable performing laboratory calculations involving concentrations, dilutions, and molarity.
Experience with basic laboratory techniques including pipetting, buffer preparation, weighing reagents, and preparation of stock solutions.
Ability to carefully follow established procedures and maintain accurate documentation.
Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively across multiple scientific teams.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced research environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience with compound management, sample management, or laboratory inventory systems.
Experience handling proteins or other biological research materials.
Familiarity with protein characterization techniques such as SDS-PAGE, chromatography, and UV-based protein concentration measurements.
Experience with protein purification, buffer exchange, centrifugal concentrators, or chromatography systems.
Familiarity with electronic laboratory notebooks or scientific inventory/database systems.
Experience working in a biotechnology or drug discovery environment.

We're seeking passionate individuals who thrive in dynamic environments, embrace new ideas, and aren't afraid to take intelligent risks. People who act with unwavering integrity and are deeply committed to making a tangible impact.

Purpose & Scope

The Research Associate will be an integral member of the Vector Bioscience team and assist in developing, characterizing, and producing AAV vectors. Industry experience

What awaits you at Astellas?

Global collaboration: Become part of a connected global business of like-minded life science leaders, all dedicated to improving patients' lives worldwide.

Innovation, Integrity and Impact sit at the heart of what we do.

We come together as ‘One Astellas’ , working with courage and a sense of urgency . We are outcome focused and consistently take accountability for our personal contribution.

Description

The Center for Perinatal Discovery (CPD) is a collaboration between the Departments of Pathology, Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Reproductive Sciences, and Pediatrics. The CPD was established to promote research into perinatal health, including the health of both mothers and babies. To this end, the CPD is conducting research studies into both maternal and neonatal health. Clinical data and biospecimens are being collected at several clinical sites from normal and high-risk pregnancies, with neonatal/pediatric follow-up. The CPD is also involved in community educational activities which promote maternal and child health.

Under supervision of the PI, the incumbent will perform complex studies with molecular and cellular methods using human ex vivo model systems and single-cell high-dimensional proteomics techniques. They will perform research activities such as handling of primary cells and tissues of human and mouse origin, performing suspension and imaging mass and flow cytometry (incl. cell sorting), antibody conjugation and titration, immuno fluorescence analysis, and quantitative (real- time) PCR to assist with contributions to the laboratory and its collaborators. They will also prepare media, buffers, and solutions as needed, and maintain an antibody library. Data processing and statistical analysis as needed.

The position will coordinate human sample collection and transport with clinical and research partners and organize and execute processing, stimulation, and biobanking of samples. They will assist with other related functions as required. This individual will assist in complex research on reproductive immunology, neuroimmunology of pregnancy, and prediction and prevention of human pregnancy complications. The incumbent will assist with experimental procedures requiring ingenuity, resourcefulness, and adaptability to special and changing needs of research.

The position will also manage our biohazard use authorization and serve as our area safety coordinator, provide routine laboratory equipment maintenance, order and maintain supplies and equipment and oversee undergraduate part-time lab aides whose duties include washing glassware and making buffers for the lab.

Minimum Qualifications

Theoretical knowledge of molecular biology techniques and genetics typically acquired through Bachelor degree in biology or related field, and/or relevant lab experience.
Demonstrated knowledge in cytometry, ideally mass cytometry, but flow and spectral flow cytometry are equally relevant. Spatial proteomics experience/theoretical knowledge preferred but not required.
Experience in human sample processing protocols and sterile technique.
Demonstrated ability to follow written and verbal protocols, techniques, and instructions
Demonstrated excellent communication and interpersonal skills over a wide range of situations and individuals needed to interact professionally and effectively in the work environment in person, on the phone, and in writing to a diverse population; including persons from foreign countries, the business community, academicians, students and staff with a high degree of diplomacy, mature judgment, tact, and flexibility.
Knowledge of proper formats, grammar, and spelling in English and proofreading ability sufficient to compose, edit, and publish professional correspondence as well as effectively and accurately document research procedures. Ability to read, comprehend, discuss, and present research materials.
Demonstrated experience with the operation of a personal computer and software applications, such as Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Access), Photoshop, Acrobat.
Willingness to learn new theory, techniques, and tasks and share knowledge.
Demonstrated experience making decisions, analyzing situations, problem solving, and initiating action for laboratory maintenance.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of bio, chemical, and radiation safety techniques and practices. Demonstrated ability to follow established Safety and Biohazardous Material Guidelines and implement measures to ensure compliance and maintain associated records.
Demonstrated organizational skills to order and maintain lab reagents and supplies, and keep accurate lab records and computer files.
Experience with UCSD ordering, EH&S, and facilities policies and business systems.
Experience with mouse experiments and husbandry.

SPECIAL CONDITIONS

Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check.

The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Physical Sciences Laboratories (PSL) supports the effective and timely development and operation of national security systems through scientific research and the application of advanced technologies. PSL has more than 150 specialized laboratories used to test, analyze, and troubleshoot virtually every aspect of rocket and satellite system design, development, construction, deployment, and operation. The expertise of the laboratories’ technical staff allows PSL to stay abreast of new technological developments and program support issues associated with rapidly evolving space systems.

The Electric Propulsion & Plasma Science section focuses on experimentally studying electric propulsion and other low-temperature plasma space technologies. This includes performing experiments to resolve flight anomalies, as well as characterizing commercial EP devices using our extensive plasma physics expertise. With a range of test facilities at our disposal, including our world-class EP3 chamber, we are equipped to study not only low-power devices like electrosprays but also high-power (>10 kW) systems. In support of flight programs, the section also investigates other plasma-adjacent phenomena like electrostatic discharge (ESD), sputtering, multipactor breakdown, and other forms of plasma-material interaction. We are looking for a Plasma Science Research Associate (Research Associate III).

Highlights of our lab's capabilities can be seen here: Virtual Tour

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility in El Segundo, California.

Reporting to the Senior Operations Manager in the Engineering Department, the Biomedical Technician II, is responsible to complete accurately and efficiently component level repairs in multiple biomedical device modalities. This position serves as a key role in the company’s repair services. The Tech II understands the production needs with minimal guidance and works efficiently to meet operational goals.

The identification of Essential Job Function does not display an exhaustive list of all duties that may be assigned to this position, nor does it restrict the related work that may be assigned to this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Essential Job Functions & Responsibilities

Performs exceptional service, repair, calibration, regulating, fine-tuning, testing, etc. on biomedical devices and equipment; exhibits “mastery” of up to three modalities and continues to improve and learn
Performs inspections on new, used, refurbished biomedical electronic equipment and offers suggestions and input to improve processes
Calibrates and troubleshoots a variety of biomedical modalities, including telemetry, pumps, monitors, modules, fetals, analyzers, blenders, etc.
Displays exceptional ability to service and optimizes resources and requests needed materials and tools as needed
Ensures consistency of repairs and quality of work and assists new Technicians with operational issues
Communicates effectively with customers over the phone to help assist with a “virtual” fix

Works well in a multi-task, high volume environment and can triage accordingly
