jobs.title: Research Associate, Vector Engineering
jobs.description:
Are you ready to play a key role in Gordian’s discovery pipeline by producing the AAV vectors that power every one of our in vivo screens?

You will operate as a key member of the team producing AAV for all of Gordian, reliably executing laboratory protocols, learning quickly, and contributing to projects that improve important workflows. You will balance multiple projects at once, which makes excellent documentation and communication across teams essential, and you will build the habits that drive success at Gordian: curiosity, coachability, strong execution and deep ownership of outcomes.

About Gordian

Gordian Biotechnology is a therapeutics company designed as a machine that systematically reveals the right way to cure age-related diseases: a machine for creating time.

To do that, we built Mosaic Screening, which makes causal validation both grounded in human pathophysiology and radically more scalable in living diseased tissue. It lets us measure the causal effects of hundreds of perturbations directly in vivo, revealing the best therapeutic targets across vast target spaces (more details on our website and in our preprint). The machine is already producing wins: across six disease areas, we have mapped nearly as many targets as the field reported in 20 years, advanced a novel osteoarthritis candidate into IND-enabling studies, and started an obesity drug-discovery collaboration with Pfizer.

But there are still many diseases left to cure, and expanding the machine to tackle them starts with its most important resource: its people and culture. We work as a team, using clear goals, open communication, and direct feedback to make autonomous decisions with the bigger picture in mind. We aim for extraordinary outcomes, continually improving how we work and acting on what will create the most progress, even in unknown territory. We have deliberately designed an environment to sustain that standard: few standing meetings, hands-on experimentation and pre-mortems, weekly team lunches, and unlimited vacation that people are encouraged to use. You can dive deeper into our culture here.

This way of working has been crucial to Gordian’s success. And every Mosaic screen runs on AAV, which is where you come in.

About The Role

Your primary mission as Vector Engineering research associate is to play a key role in the execution and workflows responsible for producing AAV for all of Gordian. You’ll contribute to the production of AAV vectors through adherent and suspension HEK293 cell transfection techniques and a suite of scalable AAV purification techniques (iodixanol ultracentrifugation, depth filtration, TFF, FPLC).

In your first month, you will shadow team members to learn the Vector team’s adherent and suspension production protocols, documentation standards, and workflows. You will take on routine lab tasks such as media prep and media changes with care and attention to detail, with no labeling errors or sample swaps and clear, detailed records in our ELN. You will learn how the Vector team interfaces with the groups that request AAV, and help our HFpEF and CKD programs by producing critical AAV vector.

Within three months, you will independently run core production tasks such as HEK293 cell splits, transfections, and harvests, and perform purification steps such as iodixanol ultracentrifugation and FPLC with limited supervision. You will have expanded your understanding of AAV biology, particularly the serotypes Gordian uses and how they are produced and purified. You will own weekly media forecasting and routine reagent ordering with no outages, and calculate AAV requirements for project requests by referencing historical production data in Gordian’s databases. You will communicate progress, blockers, and handoffs clearly, surface risks early, and close loops without repeated prompting. You will also have identified a concrete process improvement and will be designing and executing a mini-project to address it, such as testing protocol optimization ideas.

At the six-month mark, you will independently execute all existing Vector SOPs with little or no supervision, faster than when you started, while maintaining excellent record keeping and communication. You will be the sole owner of two Vector areas of responsibility, TC hood organization and shaking-incubator maintenance, with no lapses in coverage. You will have completed your first mini-project, a meaningful improvement that helps the team move faster, communicate better, or execute more robustly, and will be bringing further ideas to the Vector team’s weekly meetings.

And You

You want a chance to do your best work, immerse yourself and excel, alongside people who will inspire you and whom you’ll be excited to spend your days with.

You want to play a key role in an early-stage startup: a fast-paced environment full of both uncertainty and new challenges, demanding relentless resourcefulness, but full of opportunities and excitement.

You are organized and detail-oriented, with a history of managing multiple time-sensitive projects at once, collaborating across teams, and keeping a thorough lab notebook.

You have a background in biology and hands-on serological pipetting experience, and you are capable of making an accurate serial dilution.

You are curious, coachable, and driven: you take initiative, dig into problems, and own your outcomes.

You can articulate how this role fits into your long-term plans and why Gordian’s mission matters to you.

Bonus Points If You Have

Tissue culture experience
Wet lab experience such as transfections, qPCR, Western blot, or SDS-PAGE
Experience with flow systems such as FPLC, TFF, or depth filtration
Previous experience with AAV, lentivirus, or gene therapy

The Details

Gordian aims to provide everything you need to thrive. Beyond our community and science, you’ll have enough equity to be a true stakeholder in the company, competitive salary, full health/dental/vision/life insurance, 401k with match, onsite lunch paid for 3 days a week, an onsite gym, whatever vacation you need to be at your peak, remote work flexibility, and access to world-class mentors and advisors to support your professional growth. Our building is in the heart of the biotech capital of South San Francisco.

The Pay Range For This Role Is

66,000 - 100,000 USD per year (South San Francisco)

Department Overview

This position supports ongoing research in the laboratory of Dr. Tamara Phillips. The individual will assist with research projects that utilize behavioral, molecular, and pharmacogenetic tools to determine mechanisms involved in drug and alcohol intake, drug and alcohol responses and other addiction-related traits in mice. This work will also involve studying potential therapies for addiction by testing their effects on behaviors and examining the importance of specific areas of the brain. Studies will focus on hypotheses derived from research studying the role of genetics, individual differences, acute and chronic behavioral drug effects and molecular genetic findings.

Function/Duties of Position

Behavioral testing of mice using a variety of assays including, but not limited to measuring locomotor activity, motor coordination, body temperature, 2-bottle choice drinking, single bottle limited access drinking, operant self-administration, drug conditioned place preference, drug conditioned taste aversion, cognitive testing, and other behavioral assays, as dictated by the research aims. These may be part of collaborative endeavors.
Preparation and planning for biomedical experiments in a timely manner. This will include: obtaining subjects, obtaining supplies, reserving space and equipment, assuring the proper environment for subjects, creating data collection sheets, aiding with the development of the experimental protocol, obtaining final approval of the experimental protocol before moving forward, and other duties as assigned/necessary to ensure successful study completion. Preparation may include discussion with Drs. Phillips and Reed, Phillips Lab staff, animal care staff, and/or other laboratories.
Data collection and data entry for biomedical experiments. Physical and electronic records will be kept for each study in an orderly and timely manner. All records must accurately, legibly and completely record experimental data and results of procedures used, to allow for replication by others. Deviations from protocol or issues during experiments must also be documented. Experimental data entry is not considered complete until double-checked. All results are to be provided to the lab manager/PI within a timely manner.
Lab/equipment maintenance, supply ordering.
Record keeping, data analysis and archiving; data figure preparation.
Other duties as needed, including: brain surgery, brain harvesting, brain slicing for immunohistochemical (IHC) or structural analysis, IHC analysis for c-fos or other proteins, radioimmunoassay for specific hormones or neurotransmitters, DNA sampling and extraction, quantitative PCR genotyping, among others as determined with development of the research.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in relevant field; OR
Associate's AND 3 years of relevant experience; OR
4 years of relevant experience; OR
Equivalent combination of training and experience.
Proficiency with MS Office software.
Demonstrated knowledge of statistical software and its use for data analysis.
Applied expertise with laboratory animal handling.
Proven track record of performing detailed laboratory work and working collegially in a group setting.

B.S. in Biology, Experimental or Physiological Psychology, or Neuroscience field.
2-5 years of laboratory experience performing mouse behavior protocols.
Strong statistical expertise.
Advanced proficiency in small rodent handling, husbandry, and behavioral testing.
Experience with pharmacological research, including drug administration via subcutaneous (SC), intraperitoneal (IP), and/or intravenous (IV) injection routes.

A proven track record of autonomy in experimental execution, troubleshooting protocols, and managing daily laboratory workflows with minimal supervision.

jobs.title: Senior Research Associate, Assay Development (Contract)
jobs.description:
DELFI Diagnostics, Inc. (DELFI Diagnostics) is developing next-generation, blood-based tests that are reliable, accessible and deliver a new way to help detect cancer. Employing advanced machine-learning methods to whole-genome sequencing data, the DELFI ("DNA EvaLuation of Fragments for early Interception") platform is built to address the highest-burden health challenges. DELFI Diagnostics prioritizes solutions that have the potential to save lives on a global scale, including for historically underserved populations. DELFI Diagnostics’ platform relies on fragmentomics – the discovery that cancer cells are more chaotic than normal cells and, when they die, leave behind tell-tale patterns and characteristics of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragments. FirstLook Lung, for individuals eligible for lung cancer screening, is DELFI Diagnostics’ first laboratory-developed screening test and can be part of routine blood work. FirstLook Lung uses millions of data points to reliably identify individuals who may have cancer detected through low-dose CT, including early stage disease with a negative predictive value of 99.8 percent. This test has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

In our passionate pursuit to radically improve health outcomes, we serve humanity when we:

Lead with Science, Anchor in Pragmatism:
We pioneer life-changing science by ensuring quality, transparency, and rigor at all times. We explore thoughtfully, experiment smartly, and deliver impact with conviction.

Build With & For All:
We embrace diverse backgrounds to innovate and achieve together. We are not just building a product - we aim to disrupt the path of cancer for all - no matter geography or socioeconomic class 

Put We over I:
We are a home for high-performing people. Through teamwork, we build collective intelligence. Each of us wins when those we serve and those who serve with us--win. We show up with empathy, humility, and integrity at every step of the journey.

You will contribute to product development, verification, and validation activities for NGS-based laboratory tests for early cancer detection. The ideal candidates would have experience working under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) in a CAP/CLIA/FDA-regulated environment.

Design, execute, and troubleshoot moderate to complex laboratory experiments utilizing molecular biology techniques for Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS).

BS with 3-4 years of experience, or MS with 2-3 years relevant field (e.g., biomedical engineering, molecular biology, genetics, or genomics) in assay development for the life science industry

A bility to work PM shift 4PM to 12AM for up to 3 months during  January - March 

Proven ability to thoughtfully troubleshoot, communicate and escalate while working with limited support on a PM shift

Proficient in high-throughput manual laboratory techniques, including precision pipetting for large-scale sample processing

Strong analytical skills with demonstrated ability to independently

Superior organizational and project management abilities, including meticulous documentation practices, strategic planning, and effective time management with keen attention to detail

Experience troubleshooting and communicating issues

Overview

The Manager of Data Science is responsible for supporting advanced audience development and data and technology enablement to drive client growth. Navigate a complex, multi-source data environment and creatively identify appropriate datasets and methodologies for ever-changing client questions

Proactively identify and pursue opportunities for developing new capabilities, demonstrating end-to-end project ownership from ideation through deployment
Contribute to data science team- and practice-building initiatives, e.g. presenting case studies in cross-functional forums, creating collateral around data capabilities, and pursuing internal research projects
Document and share optimized, reusable code with data science colleagues using Git
Continuously innovate, staying current with the latest technological developments and applying them to current workflows
Deliver timely, accurate outputs aligned with client- and agency-defined best practices

Qualifications

3+ years of data science experience with consumer data; marketing agency experience preferred
Degree in Statistics, Data Science, or other quantitative fields
Deep theoretical and practical understanding of statistical/ML techniques and experimental design
Hands-on experience with granular, disaggregated data, particularly behavioral consumer datasets and/or media logs; engagement with publisher walled gardens (AMC, ADH, etc.) a plus
Advanced proficiency with SQL for big data analytics and Python for production-ready workflow development
Experience with Databricks or similar platforms, e.g. Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift
Experience building agentic workflows and integrating AI solutions into existing data and tech stacks

This on-site role combines order review, queue management, material tracking, laboratory logistics, customer support, and selected sample-preparation activities while protecting customer material and intellectual property.

What You’ll Do

Review microscopy orders, samples, carriers, labels, RFID tags, paperwork, requested services, and digital records for completeness, accuracy, and correct routing.
Manage queue status and chain-of-custody records; use RFID, locker, and tracking systems to document sample location and movement.
Resolve incomplete, duplicate, delayed, misrouted, missing, or non-actionable work by coordinating with submitters, technical teams, logistics providers, and partner laboratories.
Coordinate shipments and returns among Lam sites and external laboratories, including packaging, labeling, barcodes, courier staging, receiving, and supporting documentation.
Perform trained sample-support activities, including ALD and LSOC coating, sample sorting, inventory control, and safe handling of coupons, chips, carriers, and related materials.
Communicate order status and urgent issues clearly, escalating material, process, or data discrepancies when appropriate.
Follow safety, quality, material-control, and customer IP requirements; maintain SOPs, checklists, and training materials and support continuous improvement.

Who We’re Looking For

High school diploma or equivalent.
Experience in a laboratory, semiconductor, manufacturing, logistics, quality, production-control, customer-service, or similar detail-sensitive environment.
Strong communication, organization, time-management, and follow-through skills, with the ability to review detailed information and manage multiple priorities.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and computer-based tracking systems; ability to work independently and collaboratively on-site.
Ability to work the assigned shift and safely lift or move approximately 25 pounds.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a semiconductor cleanroom, metrology, microscopy, application lab, or high-tech manufacturing environment.
Experience with shipments, couriers, receiving, external laboratory services, RFID, inventory, asset tracking, LIMS, MES, or queue systems.
Familiarity with semiconductor coupons, wafers, chips, carriers, coating, or sample-preparation processes.
Experience creating SOPs, training materials, checklists, or controlled documentation.
